Chilli con carne, ragu and burgers all rely on minced beef, cooked until browned.
beef-mince.visual: a small heap of raw beef mince, bright red with fine flecks of white fat
beef-mince.what: Finely minced raw beef, the base of many classic dishes.

facts: Neck of beef is a hard-working muscle, so its sinew softens with long, slow cooking.
beef-neck.visual: a raw beef neck cut, dark red meat with white sinew running through, lying flat on a plain background
beef-neck.what: A tough, rich cut from the neck, best slow-cooked.

facts: The ribeye is cut from the rib section of the cow, and is also called a Scotch fillet in Australia and New Zealand.
Marbling, the streaks of fat within the muscle, helps keep the meat juicy when cooked.
A bone-in ribeye is known in France as côte de bœuf.
beef-ribeye-steak.visual: one raw ribeye steak, a thick cut with fat marbling visible through the red meat, lying flat
beef-ribeye-steak.what: A richly marbled, tender steak cut from the rib of beef.

facts: Beef sausages are made from ground beef mixed with seasoning and sometimes fat or breadcrumbs.
beef-sausage.visual: one whole raw beef sausage link, pale pinkish-brown, smooth casing, lying in a gentle curve
beef-sausage.what: A firm, savoury sausage made from minced beef.

facts: Shin is a working muscle from the lower leg of the cow, rich in connective tissue.
That connective tissue turns tender with slow cooking, and the marrow bone adds flavour to the liquid.
Osso buco, the Italian braise, is made from cross-cut shanks, usually of veal.
beef-shin.visual: a raw cross-cut beef shin, dark red meat around a round marrow bone, lying flat on its cut face
beef-shin.what: A tough, flavourful cut from the leg, best slow-cooked.

facts: Short ribs come from the rib section of the cow and are often cut into thick pieces.
Slow braising breaks down the connective tissue in short ribs, making the meat tender.
Korean galbi and American barbecue both use beef short ribs, prepared in very different ways.
beef-short-rib.visual: a single raw bone-in beef short rib, marbled red meat and white fat, lying flat
beef-short-rib.what: A fatty cut of beef from the rib, rich when slow-cooked.

facts: In British butchery, silverside is the cut from the outer part of the back leg.
Because it is lean, it is best cooked slowly so that the meat becomes tender.
beef-silverside.visual: a whole raw boneless beef silverside joint, lean deep red meat with a thin fat cap
beef-silverside.what: A lean beef cut from the outer leg, good for slow cooking.

facts: Sirloin is cut from the loin, behind the ribs and in front of the rump.
In Britain, sirloin is a common steak sold by butchers and supermarkets.
beef-sirloin-steak.visual: a single raw beef sirloin steak with a rim of creamy white fat, lying flat on the surface
beef-sirloin-steak.what: A beef cut from the loin with a flavourful rim of fat.

facts: Skirt steak comes from the diaphragm muscle that sits beneath the cow's ribs.
Its grain is long and open, so it is usually sliced thinly across the grain.
beef-skirt.visual: one raw beef skirt steak, a long flat strip of deep red meat with visible grain and a thin silver membrane along one edge
beef-skirt.what: A long, flat cut of beef with a strong, rich flavour.

facts: Spleen is an organ that filters the blood and is eaten as offal in many cuisines.
In Palermo, Sicily, pani ca meusa is a street-food sandwich of boiled, then fried, spleen.
beef-spleen.visual: a single raw beef spleen, dark purplish-red and smooth, lying flat directly on the background
beef-spleen.what: A dark, spongy offal from cattle, cooked in stews or fried.

facts: Stir-frying is a Chinese cooking method in which small pieces are cooked quickly in a little oil.
The wok is a rounded pan whose shape lets food be tossed and cooked over high heat.
Beef strips for stir-frying are cut thin across the grain, which keeps them tender when cooked fast.
beef-stir-fry-strips.visual: thin raw beef strips, deep red, fanned loosely in a curve on the background
beef-stir-fry-strips.what: Thin beef strips, ready for quick cooking in a wok.

facts: Stock is the liquid made by simmering bones, meat and vegetables for a long time.
Stocks are the base of many sauces, gravies and stews in French and British cooking.
Beef stock is often reduced to a glaze or sauce, concentrating its flavour.
beef-stock.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of clear, rich brown beef stock
beef-stock.what: Rich brown broth made by simmering beef bones.

facts: Concentrated stock cubes became common in British kitchens in the early twentieth century.
A cube is crumbled or dissolved in hot water to make a quick stock for soups and gravies.
Traditional beef stock is made by simmering beef bones and vegetables for a long time.
beef-stock-cube.visual: a plain white ceramic bowl holding one dark brown stock cube, compressed and slightly crumbly at the edges
beef-stock-cube.what: A dried block of savoury beef stock for soups and gravies.

facts: Reducing stock by simmering concentrates its flavour into a thick, glossy liquid.
Concentrated meat extracts were sold in jars during the nineteenth century as an early way to flavour broths.
beef-stock-pot.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, holding a dark brown, glossy, set beef stock gel
beef-stock-pot.what: A concentrated beef paste that dissolves into hot water.

facts: Steak tartare is made from raw beef, usually seasoned with onion and capers.
Because the beef is not cooked, it must be very fresh and kept cold.
beef-tartare.visual: a neat round mound of finely chopped raw beef, deep red and glossy, on a plain white plate
beef-tartare.what: Finely chopped raw beef, usually seasoned and served cold.

facts: Thick flank is a cut sold in British butchers and supermarkets for roasting and slicing.
Lean joints like this are often slow-cooked to keep the meat moist and sliced thinly.
beef-thick-flank.visual: one raw beef thick flank joint, deep red meat with a thin layer of fat, lying flat
beef-thick-flank.what: A lean, economical cut from the rear leg of the cow.

facts: Tomatoes are botanically fruits, but are used as a vegetable in cooking.
Beefsteak tomatoes are large varieties, often sliced for sandwiches and salads.
beef-tomato.visual: one whole large, ribbed red beef tomato, slightly lobed and glossy
beef-tomato.what: A large, meaty, ribbed tomato that is good for slicing.

beef-topside.visual: one whole raw beef topside joint, lean deep red meat, a thin layer of fat on top, tied with string
beef-topside.what: A lean roasting joint from the back of the leg.

facts: Tripe is the edible lining of a cow's stomach, taken from several of its compartments.
Tripe is traditionally simmered slowly with onions in Britain, Spain and Mexico.
beef-tripe.visual: a raw piece of pale honeycomb beef tripe with a ridged texture, lying flat
beef-tripe.what: The honeycomb lining of a cow's stomach, eaten as food.

facts: Mustard is made by grinding mustard seeds and mixing them with liquid such as vinegar, water or beer.
Mustards made with beer are often served with sausages, ham and pork.
Mustard seeds have been used as a spice in Europe and Asia since ancient times.
beer-mustard.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, pale-brown mustard
beer-mustard.what: A smooth, tangy mustard made with beer for a malty edge.

facts: Beetroot was cultivated in ancient times, and its wild relative, sea beet, grows around the Mediterranean.
Its deep red colour comes from betalain pigments, which are also used as a natural food colouring.
In Britain beetroot is often pickled and eaten with cheese, and it features in soups such as borscht.
beetroot.visual: one whole raw beetroot with smooth dark-red skin and a short stub of stalk, on a plain background
beetroot.what: A sweet, earthy root vegetable with deep red flesh.

facts: Its deep red colour comes from natural pigments called betalains.
Beetroot juice is used in cooking to colour soups such as borscht and to tint cakes.
beetroot-juice.visual: a clear drinking glass filled with deep crimson beetroot juice
beetroot-juice.what: Deep red juice pressed from cooked or raw beetroot.

facts: Beetroot is a cultivated form of sea beet, and its leaves are closely related to chard.
Beetroot leaves are cooked much like spinach or chard, and wilt quickly in a pan.
beetroot-leaves.visual: a small bunch of crinkled dark green leaves on deep red stalks
beetroot-leaves.what: Tender, earthy leaves from the top of a beetroot.

facts: Pasta is made from flour and water, often durum wheat, and has been eaten in Italy for centuries.
Beetroot was grown for its leaves in antiquity, and the sweet root became popular in Europe later.
beetroot-pasta.visual: a small loose heap of dried, vivid magenta ribbon pasta, each strand flat and dry
beetroot-pasta.what: Ribbon pasta coloured and flavoured with cooked beetroot.

facts: Beetroot was grown in the Mediterranean for its leaves long before the swollen root became popular.
Beetroot's deep colour comes from betalain pigments, which is why it stains other foods.
beetroot-relish.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with deep purple-red beetroot relish, lid off
beetroot-relish.what: A sweet-sour relish of beetroot, often with horseradish.

facts: Bel paese is Italian for beautiful country, a phrase often used to describe Italy.
It is a semi-soft cheese from northern Italy, made from cow's milk.
bel-paese.visual: a block of pale ivory-yellow cheese with one wedge cut away
bel-paese.what: A mild, buttery Italian cheese that melts smoothly.

facts: Dubbel is a style of strong, dark Belgian ale linked to the monastic breweries of the region.
Belgian ales are often brewed with yeasts that give fruity and spicy flavours.
Belgium has a long brewing tradition with many distinct beer styles, some made in abbeys.
belgian-ale.visual: a clear drinking glass of dark amber-brown ale with a creamy light brown head
belgian-ale.what: A dark, fruity Belgian beer in the style of abbey brewing.

facts: Belgian waffles come in two main styles: a light Brussels waffle, and a yeasted Liege waffle.
Liege waffles contain pearl sugar, which caramelises on the hot iron and sweetens the outside.
Waffles are cooked between two hinged metal plates, which imprint the pattern.
belgian-waffles.visual: one golden Belgian waffle with deep square pockets, served plainly on a plain white plate
belgian-waffles.what: A thick waffle with deep pockets that hold syrup well.

facts: Peppers are native to the Americas and were carried to Europe and Asia after 1492.
Sweet peppers are the same species as chilli, bred to have little or no heat.
bell-pepper.visual: a whole glossy red bell pepper, four lobes, green stalk attached at the top
bell-pepper.what: A juicy, crunchy pepper, eaten raw or roasted until sweet.

facts: Beluga caviar comes from the beluga sturgeon, a huge fish living mainly in the Caspian Sea area.
Caviar is traditionally served chilled as a luxury starter, often with blinis or toast.
International trade rules now limit beluga sturgeon fishing, because overfishing reduced wild stocks.
beluga-caviar.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl holding glossy, pearl-grey beluga caviar eggs
beluga-caviar.what: Large, delicate salted eggs of the beluga sturgeon.

facts: Beluga lentils are called that because they resemble beluga caviar in size and shine.
They are used in salads and side dishes because they keep their shape better than many other lentils.
beluga-lentils.visual: a small heap of tiny, glossy black lentils, dry and shiny
beluga-lentils.what: Tiny black lentils that stay firm and hold their shape.

facts: Berbere is central to Ethiopian stews such as doro wat, a spiced chicken dish.
Its main ingredients usually include dried chillies, fenugreek, coriander seed and ginger.
Recipes vary from family to family, so the heat and flavour of berbere can differ widely.
berbere.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of dark red-brown spice powder, fine and slightly coarse
berbere.what: A hot, warm spice blend from Ethiopian cooking.

facts: Bergamot is grown mainly in Calabria, in southern Italy.
Its fragrant oil is pressed from the peel and used in perfumes and foods.
The fruit is too sour to eat fresh, so cooks use its zest and oil instead.
bergamot.visual: a whole pear-shaped bergamot, yellow-green and bumpy-skinned
bergamot.what: A bitter, floral citrus whose oil flavours Earl Grey tea.

facts: Beurre blanc is associated with the Loire Valley in western France.
Beurre means butter and blanc means white, describing the pale colour of the finished sauce.
beurre-blanc.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of pale golden, glossy, creamy sauce
beurre-blanc.what: A silky French butter sauce, whisked with shallot and wine.

facts: Beyaz peynir means white cheese in Turkish and is a staple of the country's breakfast tables.
It is traditionally made from sheep's milk, though cow's milk versions are also common.
The cheese is stored in brine, which gives it its salty flavour and firm texture.
beyaz-peynir.visual: a block of pale white cheese with one wedge cut out, the cut face showing a crumbly texture
beyaz-peynir.what: A salty, crumbly white cheese from Turkey, kept in brine.

facts: It is traditionally served with chole, a spiced chickpea curry from the Punjab region.
Chole bhature is a popular dish across Delhi and northern India.
bhatura.visual: one whole puffed, golden-brown fried bread with a pale soft interior, on a plain white plate
bhatura.what: A soft, puffed, fried bread from North India.

facts: Bhuna is a cooking method in which spices and onions are fried until most of the liquid has evaporated.
The word bhuna comes from the Hindi and Urdu word for roasting or frying, which describes the method.
Bhuna dishes are popular in Bangladeshi and British restaurants, where they are often served as medium-hot curries.
bhuna-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, dark reddish-brown curry sauce, glossy and dry-looking
bhuna-sauce.what: A thick, dry-fried curry base from British curry houses.

facts: The name comes from a written character called biang, which has many strokes and is hard to write.
The noodles are hand-pulled and stretched, then slapped against the work surface to make them wide.
In Shaanxi they are traditionally served with chilli oil, vinegar and garlic.
biang-biang-noodles.visual: a small heap of wide, flat, pale dried noodles, uncooked and unbroken
biang-biang-noodles.what: Broad, hand-pulled noodles from Shaanxi, China.

facts: Bicarbonate of soda reacts with acidic ingredients such as buttermilk to release gas that lifts a bake.
Soda bread, a traditional Irish bread, uses bicarbonate of soda in place of yeast.
bicarbonate-of-soda.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine white powder, dry and slightly granular
bicarbonate-of-soda.what: A white alkaline powder that makes cakes and bakes rise.

facts: It is a fast-swimming, deep-diving fish that is prized for sashimi and sushi.
Its name refers to its large eyes.
bigeye-tuna.visual: a fillet of raw bigeye tuna, deep red with fine dark streaks, lying flat on a plain background
bigeye-tuna.what: A large, deep red tuna with rich, meaty flesh.

facts: Bilberries grow wild on heathland and moorland, especially in upland parts of Britain.
Bilberries have been gathered from the wild for centuries, and they are often used in pies and jams.
bilberry.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of tiny, dark blue-black wild berries with a dusty bloom
bilberry.what: Small wild berries that stain pies and puddings purple.

facts: They are close relatives of blueberries and have been gathered wild for centuries.
Bilberry preserves are traditional in Scandinavia and Germany.
bilberry-jam.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with deep purple-black jam
bilberry-jam.what: A dark, tart preserve made from wild European bilberries.

facts: Biltong is traditionally dried in the air rather than smoked, often by hanging strips of meat.
biltong.visual: a single dark reddish-brown strip of dry-cured beef biltong, its edges slightly curled, lying flat
biltong.what: Dry-cured South African beef, sliced thin for snacking.

facts: The Bing cherry was developed in Oregon, in the north-western United States.
Cherries have been cultivated for thousands of years and are eaten fresh or cooked.
Cherries are used in tarts, jams and salsas, and pair well with savoury dishes.
bing-cherry.visual: a small cluster of plump dark red cherries, green stalks still attached
bing-cherry.what: A dark, sweet cherry that is large and plump.

facts: Birch syrup is made by boiling down sap tapped from birch trees in cold northern regions.
Birch syrup has a tangy, caramel-like flavour and is often compared with maple syrup.
Birch syrup is produced in Alaska, Canada and Finland, where birch trees grow abundantly.
birch-syrup.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of pale amber birch syrup, half full
birch-syrup.what: A tangy, sweet syrup boiled down from birch tree sap.

facts: Bird's eye chillies are widely used in South-East Asian cooking, especially in Thai dishes.
They are often pounded into curry pastes or sliced into stir-fries and soups.
Their small size and fierce heat make them one of the hottest chillies in common use.
bird-s-eye-chilli.visual: a small heap of tiny red bird's eye chillies, slender and smooth-skinned
bird-s-eye-chilli.what: A tiny red or green chilli with a very fierce heat.

facts: Biryani is a mixed rice dish from the Indian subcontinent, cooked with meat or vegetables.
The word masala means a mix of spices, and home blends vary widely between cooks.
Whole spices are often toasted before grinding, which deepens their flavour.
biryani-masala.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of reddish-brown ground spice blend, slightly coarse and dusty
biryani-masala.what: A warm, fragrant spice blend for layered rice dishes.

facts: Biryani is a layered rice dish from South Asia, often made with meat or vegetables.
Biryani is particularly associated with Hyderabad and Lucknow, where distinct regional styles developed.
The origins of biryani are debated, but its development is linked to the Mughal courts of South Asia.
biryani-paste.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, orange-brown spice paste with a glossy surface
biryani-paste.what: A thick spice paste used to flavour rice and meat dishes.

facts: Speculoos are thin, spiced biscuits traditionally baked in Belgium and the Netherlands.
Speculaas biscuits are traditionally baked for the feast of Saint Nicholas in the Low Countries.
Warm spices such as cinnamon, cloves and ginger give the biscuits their flavour.
biscuit-spread.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with smooth golden-brown spiced biscuit spread
biscuit-spread.what: A sweet, spiced biscuit paste you spread on toast.

facts: Bison, often called buffalo, once roamed the North American plains in huge herds.
Bison meat is also raised on farms in North America and Europe.
Bison steaks are usually cooked quickly over high heat, as they can dry out if overcooked.
bison.visual: one raw bison steak, deep red meat, lying flat with a smooth, slightly moist surface
bison.what: Sweet red meat from a shaggy, large grazing animal.

facts: Bison once roamed North America in very large herds across the plains.
Plains peoples relied on bison for food, clothing and tools.
bison-burger.visual: one raw bison burger patty, deep red and round, lying flat on the background
bison-burger.what: A lean patty of bison, a large animal related to cattle.

facts: Bitter red aperitifs are traditionally drunk before a meal in Italy.
They are often mixed with prosecco and soda water to make a spritz.
Many are flavoured with herbs, citrus peel and spices, giving a bittersweet taste.
bitter-aperitif.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle filled with a deep red, translucent liquid
bitter-aperitif.what: A bitter red Italian spirit, often mixed in spritzes.

facts: Bitter leaf is a plant known as Vernonia, native to tropical Africa.
Its leaves are washed several times to soften the bitter taste before cooking.
It is a key ingredient in ofe onugbu, a bitter leaf soup from south-eastern Nigeria.
bitter-leaf.visual: a bunch of fresh washed bitter leaf, dark green serrated leaves on short stems
bitter-leaf.what: Leaves of a West African shrub, used in Nigerian soups.

facts: Bitter melon is grown across South Asia, East Asia and the Caribbean, where it is cooked in many dishes.
In Hindi and Urdu it is called karela, and it is often cooked with spices or stuffed.
Salting the sliced gourd before cooking is a common way to reduce its bitterness.
bitter-melon.visual: a whole warty, pale green bitter melon, elongated and slightly curved
bitter-melon.what: A warty green gourd with a sharp, bitter flavour.

facts: Black bean sauce is a staple of Cantonese cooking, made from fermented soya beans, salt and spices.
The beans are fermented with salt, which gives the sauce its deep savoury flavour.
Chinese cooks have used fermented soya beans for many centuries, and the method spread across East Asia.
black-bean-sauce.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with thick, dark brown, glossy sauce
black-bean-sauce.what: A salty, fermented sauce made from black soya beans.

facts: Black beans are native to the Americas and have been a staple food in Latin America for centuries.
They are a key ingredient in Cuban black beans and rice, and in Brazil's feijoada stew.
Their dark skins give the cooked beans and their cooking liquid a deep, dark colour.
black-beans.visual: a small heap of glossy, shiny black dried beans, oval and smooth
black-beans.what: Glossy black beans, a staple of Latin American cooking.

facts: Its pods are traditionally dried over open fires, which gives them a smoky flavour.
It is used in slow-cooked curries and rice dishes across South Asian cooking.
black-cardamom-pods.visual: a small heap of large, dark brown, ridged cardamom pods, dry and papery
black-cardamom-pods.what: Large, smoky dried pods with a warm, camphor-like aroma.

facts: Kala chana is a dark-skinned variety of chickpea, and it is widely eaten across India.
The dried peas are usually soaked overnight, then simmered in curries or roasted as a snack.
Chickpeas have been cultivated in the Middle East and South Asia for thousands of years.
black-chickpeas.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of small dark brown-black dried chickpeas, wrinkled and matte
black-chickpeas.what: A dark, earthy pulse popular in Indian curries and snacks.

facts: Black cod, also known as sablefish, lives in the deep cold waters of the North Pacific.
Miso-glazed black cod is a well-known dish in Japanese restaurants.
black-cod.visual: a fresh fillet of silvery-white fish flesh with a dark glossy skin, lying flat on the background
black-cod.what: A rich, oily deep-sea fish with silky, buttery flesh.

facts: Black cumin is a different plant from common cumin, though the seeds look somewhat similar.
The seeds are used in Indian and Persian cooking, and are often added to rice dishes such as biryani.
black-cumin-seeds.visual: a small heap of slender black seeds, curved and matte, lying loose
black-cumin-seeds.what: Slender black seeds with a smoky, sweet flavour.

facts: They are a traditional dish in Southern American cooking, often eaten on New Year's Day.
Cowpeas are now grown in warm regions across Africa, Asia and the Americas.
black-eyed-peas.visual: a small heap of dried, creamy white beans, each with a neat black spot
black-eyed-peas.what: Creamy beans with a black eye, used in Southern stews.

facts: Figs grew wild around the eastern Mediterranean and were among the earliest fruits cultivated by people.
What looks like a fig fruit is really a hollow cluster of tiny flowers, turned inward.
The soft flesh of ripe figs is jammy, so they are often roasted with honey or served with cheese.
black-fig.visual: two whole ripe dark purple figs with a dusty bloom on the skin, lying directly on the background
black-fig.what: A dark purple, soft-skinned fig with jammy, sweet flesh.

facts: Black Forest ham takes its name from the Black Forest region in south-west Germany.
It is traditionally smoked over fir or spruce wood and seasoned with juniper.
black-forest-ham.visual: one thin slice of dark-rinded smoked ham, rosy pink meat with white fat, lying flat
black-forest-ham.what: Smoked German ham, dark-rinded and subtly spiced.

facts: Black garlic is made by holding whole bulbs at low heat for several weeks, so they darken naturally.
It is popular across East Asian cooking and is now used in Western kitchens as a sweet, dark seasoning.
black-garlic.visual: one whole black garlic bulb, dark and glossy, its cloves soft and sticky
black-garlic.what: Aged bulbs of garlic that turn dark, soft and sweet.

facts: Black gram is native to the Indian subcontinent and has been grown there for thousands of years.
Split and skinned, it turns white and is used to make the batter for idli and dosa.
black-gram.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of dried black gram, small glossy black beans
black-gram.what: A small black pulse used in dals, curries and batters.

facts: Grapes are one of the oldest cultivated fruits, grown for eating fresh, for drying and for wine.
Grapes grow on vines, and the fruit is usually harvested in late summer or autumn.
black-grapes.visual: a small bunch of dark purple-black grapes on a short green stalk, plump and glossy
black-grapes.what: Sweet, juicy dark grapes that are good eaten raw.

facts: Black Krim is an heirloom variety, named after the Crimean peninsula where it is thought to have originated.
Heirloom tomatoes like this one are grown from seed passed down through generations rather than hybrid seed.
Tomatoes originated in western South America and were domesticated in Mexico.
black-krim-tomato.visual: a whole ripe Black Krim tomato, dark brownish-red with green shoulders, on a plain background
black-krim-tomato.what: A deep-coloured tomato with a smoky, rich flavour.

facts: Black mulberry trees are native to western Asia, and the fruit has long been grown in the Mediterranean.
Its juice is deep purple and can leave strong stains on clothes and fingers.
Because the fruit bruises easily, black mulberries are usually eaten or cooked soon after picking.
black-mulberry.visual: a small heap of ripe black mulberries with glossy dark skins, some stems still attached
black-mulberry.what: Dark, juicy berries with a sharp, winey taste.

facts: Black mustard seeds are used across South Asian cooking, especially in South Indian dishes.
They release a nutty flavour when they are heated in oil until they pop.
The plant that produces them, Brassica nigra, belongs to the cabbage family.
black-mustard-seeds.visual: a small heap of black mustard seeds, tiny round dark grains piled loosely on a plain background
black-mustard-seeds.what: Tiny dark seeds that crackle and pop when fried in oil.

facts: Olive paste is made by crushing olives, often with oil, salt and herbs.
Tapenade, a spread from Provence, is traditionally made from olives, capers and anchovies.
black-olive-paste.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, glossy purple-black olive paste, smooth on top
black-olive-paste.what: A dark, salty spread made from crushed black olives.

facts: Olives have been grown around the Mediterranean for thousands of years.
They are brined or salted to remove the bitterness found in raw olives.
black-olives.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of glossy, dark black olives, whole and unpitted
black-olives.what: Ripe, mellow olives with a soft, briny flavour.

facts: Black pepper is native to the Western Ghats of India, where the vine has grown for centuries.
Pepper was a highly prized spice in medieval Europe, traded along long routes from Asia.
Black pepper comes from unripe berries, dried until they turn dark and wrinkled.
black-pepper.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of coarse ground black pepper, dark grey-black
black-pepper.what: Dried, ground berries of a vine; a sharp, peppery spice.

facts: Black pepper is native to the Western Ghats of India and has been traded for thousands of years.
Pepper was a major spice in the medieval trade between Asia and Europe.
black-pepper-sauce.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of dark, glossy brown sauce flecked with black pepper
black-pepper-sauce.what: A hot, peppery sauce, often used to glaze beef dishes.

facts: Plums belong to the same genus as cherries, apricots and peaches.
Plums are often roasted or stewed, and their sweetness deepens as they cook.
Plums have been cultivated in Europe and Asia for thousands of years.
black-plum.visual: a whole ripe black plum with dark purple-black skin and a faint bloom
black-plum.what: Dark-skinned, juicy stone fruit with a sweet, tart flavour.

facts: Black pudding is a traditional British and Irish food, and similar blood sausages are made across Europe.
Oatmeal is often added to black pudding, helping to bind it and give it a firm texture.
It is usually sold cooked and is commonly fried or grilled until crisp at the edges.
black-pudding.visual: a thick round slice of dark, crumbly black pudding showing its dense, speckled cut face
black-pudding.what: A dark, dense sausage made from pork blood, fat and oats.

facts: Quinoa has been grown in the Andes of South America for thousands of years.
The name quinoa comes from the Quechua word kinwa.
black-quinoa.visual: a small heap of glossy black quinoa seeds, tiny and round
black-quinoa.what: A dark, earthy seed cooked and eaten like a grain.

facts: Black radish, also called Spanish radish, is a winter variety with dark skin and white flesh.
Its flesh is firm and white with a sharp, peppery taste that is milder when cooked.
black-radish.visual: a whole raw black radish with rough dark skin and a round shape
black-radish.what: A large black-skinned winter radish with a peppery bite.

facts: Black rice is often called forbidden rice, a name said to link to a belief that it was once reserved for Chinese emperors.
Its dark colour comes from anthocyanin pigments held in the bran layer of the grain.
Black rice is grown in parts of Asia and is often cooked like brown rice, with more water and a longer time.
black-rice.visual: a small loose heap of uncooked black rice grains, glossy and deep purple-black
black-rice.what: Dark purple grains with a nutty, slightly sweet taste.

facts: Chinkiang vinegar is named after Zhenjiang, a city in Jiangsu province in eastern China, where it is traditionally made.
It is made from glutinous rice and wheat bran, then aged in earthenware jars, which gives it a smoky depth.
black-rice-vinegar.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of dark, glossy black-brown vinegar
black-rice-vinegar.what: A dark, malty Chinese vinegar used for dumpling dips.

facts: Nigella is a small flowering plant whose black seeds have long been used in Middle Eastern and South Asian cooking.
black-seed-oil.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of dark golden-brown oil
black-seed-oil.what: A peppery, bitter oil pressed from the seeds of nigella.

facts: Black sesame is used in Chinese and Japanese sweets, including fillings for dumplings and pastries.
Sesame is one of the oldest cultivated oilseeds, grown in Asia and Africa for thousands of years.
black-sesame-paste.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, dark grey-black sesame paste
black-sesame-paste.what: A dark, nutty paste made from ground black sesame seeds.

facts: Black sesame seeds are unhulled sesame, so they keep their dark outer coat.
In Japanese cooking they are ground into a paste called neri goma for sweets and dressings.
black-sesame-seeds.visual: a small heap of black sesame seeds, glossy and jet black
black-sesame-seeds.what: Small dark seeds with a nutty, slightly bitter taste.

facts: Tahini is a paste made from ground sesame seeds, and it is widely used across Middle Eastern cooking.
Sesame has been cultivated for thousands of years and is one of the oldest oilseed crops.
black-tahini.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, dark grey-black sesame paste with a smooth surface
black-tahini.what: A dark, bitter sesame paste made from unhulled seeds.

facts: Black treacle is the thick syrup left behind when sugar is refined.
Treacle is a traditional British ingredient, used in gingerbread and parkin.
It is much darker and more bitter than golden syrup, which is milder.
black-treacle.visual: a plain unlabelled glass jar filled with thick, very dark brown syrup
black-treacle.what: A thick, dark, bitter-sweet syrup from sugar refining.

facts: Black truffles are underground fungi that are hunted in Europe with trained dogs or pigs.
Truffles have been valued in European cooking for centuries, and remain costly.
black-truffle-oil.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of pale golden oil, a small amount inside, cap on
black-truffle-oil.what: A cooking oil flavoured to taste of black truffle.

facts: Its French name, trompette de la mort, translates as trumpet of death.
The mushroom grows in woodland, often under oak and beech trees.
Cooks often dry black trumpets, which concentrates their flavour for sauces and soups.
black-trumpet.visual: a small heap of black trumpet mushrooms, dark funnel-shaped caps with wavy edges and a few short stems visible
black-trumpet.what: A dark, funnel-shaped wild mushroom with a fruity taste.

facts: Black walnut is a native tree of eastern North America, valued for its dense timber.
Its nuts have a stronger, more pungent flavour than English walnuts.
Native North Americans gathered and ate black walnuts long before European settlement.
black-walnuts.visual: a small heap of shelled black walnut halves, dark brown and knobbly, loose on the surface
black-walnuts.what: Large, strong-tasting nuts from a North American tree.

facts: The Perigord truffle is a fungus that grows around the roots of oak and hazel trees.
Truffles are often found by trained dogs or pigs sniffing them out in woodland.
Black winter truffles are prized in French and Italian cooking, often shaved thinly over dishes.
black-winter-truffle.visual: one whole black winter truffle, knobbly dark surface, a little earth clinging to it
black-winter-truffle.what: An aromatic underground fungus, prized in French cooking.

facts: Blackberries grow wild across Europe, picked from brambles in hedgerows and woodland edges.
In Britain, blackberries are traditionally picked from late summer into autumn and baked into crumbles and pies.
blackberry.visual: a small heap of plump, glossy, dark blackberries lying loose on the background
blackberry.what: A dark, tart wild berry picked from autumn hedgerows.

facts: Blackberries grow wild in hedgerows across Britain and Europe, and have been picked for centuries.
Bramble is another name for the blackberry plant, and bramble jelly is made from strained juice.
blackberry-jam.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, full of deep purple blackberry jam
blackberry-jam.what: A dark, thick jam of cooked blackberries and sugar.

facts: Blackcurrants are grown widely in northern Europe and are a traditional British fruit for jams.
During the Second World War, blackcurrants were a key home-grown fruit in Britain for cordials and syrups.
blackcurrant.visual: a small heap of fresh blackcurrants, glossy dark purple-black berries on their small stalks
blackcurrant.what: A small, dark berry with a deeply tart, musky flavour.

facts: Blackcurrants are small, dark berries grown on compact shrubs in cool northern climates.
Cordial is a sweet syrup that is diluted with water, a term used in Britain for fruit squash.
Blackcurrant is traditionally paired with game and venison in sauces.
blackcurrant-cordial.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle filled with deep purple blackcurrant cordial
blackcurrant-cordial.what: A concentrated blackcurrant squash, diluted for drinks.

facts: Blackcurrants grow across northern Europe and Asia, and they are a common British garden fruit.
Blackcurrant jam is traditionally made by boiling the fruit with sugar until it sets.
Cassis, the French blackcurrant liqueur, is made from the same fruit.
blackcurrant-jam.visual: a plain glass jar without a label filled with deep purple-black jam
blackcurrant-jam.what: A thick, tart preserve made from blackcurrants and sugar.

facts: Blackstrap is the dark syrup that remains after sugar is extracted from cane.
Molasses appears in many traditional baked goods, including gingerbread and parkin.
blackstrap-molasses.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with thick, very dark brown molasses
blackstrap-molasses.what: A thick, dark, bitter syrup left from refining sugar.

facts: Blanching removes the brown skin by soaking the nuts in hot water, then the skins are slipped off.
Ground almonds are the base of marzipan, a sweet paste used in cakes and confectionery.
blanched-almonds.visual: a small heap of pale, skinless almonds, smooth ivory-coloured nuts, lying loose on a plain background
blanched-almonds.what: Pale, skinless nut kernels with a mild, sweet flavour.

facts: The name is French, meaning white food.
Blancmange dates back to medieval times, when it was often made with almond milk.
blancmange-powder.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with fine white powder
blancmange-powder.what: A powdered mix that sets with milk into a wobbly pudding.

facts: Bleu d'Auvergne is made in the Auvergne region of central France from cow's milk.
The cheese is pierced so that the blue mould spreads evenly through the paste.
bleu-d-auvergne.visual: a wedge cut from a round of blue cheese, creamy pale ivory with blue-green veins and a grey-brown rind
bleu-d-auvergne.what: A creamy French blue cheese with a peppery, tangy flavour.

facts: Bleu de Bresse is made in the Bresse region of eastern France, an area known for its poultry.
Its blue veining comes from moulds added to the curd, which spread through it as it ages.
bleu-de-bresse.visual: one wedge cut from a round of pale creamy blue cheese, soft white rind on the outside, a few blue veins inside
bleu-de-bresse.what: A mild, creamy blue cheese with a soft white rind.

facts: Blewit is a wild mushroom that grows in woodland and leaf litter, mostly in autumn.
Blewits are foraged in Britain and across Europe, and are usually cooked before eating.
blewit.visual: a small heap of fresh wood blewit mushrooms, lilac-violet caps and stems, pale gills, lying loose on a plain background
blewit.what: A lilac-tinged wild mushroom, best cooked thoroughly.

facts: Blini are traditionally eaten in Russia during Maslenitsa, the festival before Lent.
The name comes from the Russian word blin, meaning pancake.
blini.visual: a small plain white plate holding three round golden-brown blini
blini.what: Small yeasted pancakes, traditionally served in Russia.

facts: Bloaters are traditionally cured in Great Yarmouth, the Norfolk port linked to herring fishing.
The herring is salted briefly and then smoked whole, which keeps it moist.
bloater.visual: a whole bloater, a lightly smoked herring with pale golden-brown skin, lying on its side
bloater.what: A lightly smoked whole herring with a rich flavour.

facts: Blood oranges are thought to have originated in Sicily, where they are still widely grown.
Their red colour develops when nights are cool, through pigments called anthocyanins.
They are used in salads, sorbets and cocktails across Italy and beyond.
blood-orange.visual: half a blood orange, cut, deep crimson flesh facing up
blood-orange.what: A citrus fruit with crimson flesh and a berry-like flavour.

facts: Bloomer bread is widely sold in British bakeries and supermarkets.
Bloomers are often eaten sliced for sandwiches, toast or alongside soup.
bloomer.visual: one whole bloomer loaf on a plain white plate, golden crust with diagonal slashes, open crumb visible
bloomer.what: A crusty British loaf, slashed on top, with a chewy crumb.

facts: Blue cheeses are made by adding a mould culture to the curds, which spreads through the cheese as veins.
Roquefort, from southern France, is one of the best-known blues and must be made from sheep's milk.
blue-cheese.visual: a block of creamy pale cheese streaked with blue-green veins, with one wedge cut away
blue-cheese.what: A pungent, creamy cheese streaked with blue-green veins.

facts: Blue cheese dressing is a creamy sauce usually made from mayonnaise or sour cream and blue cheese.
It became a popular salad dressing in the United States, where it is often served with chicken wings.
A classic choice for the dressing is Roquefort, a sheep's-milk cheese from southern France.
blue-cheese-dressing.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of creamy off-white dressing with small blue-green flecks
blue-cheese-dressing.what: A creamy, tangy dressing with crumbled blue cheese.

facts: Blue corn is a variety of maize grown in Mexico and the south-western United States.
Tortilla chips are made by cutting corn tortillas into wedges and frying or baking them.
Maize was first domesticated in Mexico, and tortillas made from it are central to Mexican cooking.
blue-corn-tortilla-chips.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl heaped with deep blue-purple tortilla chips, triangular and crisp, slightly golden at the edges
blue-corn-tortilla-chips.what: Crisp triangles of corn tortilla with a deep blue colour.

facts: Blue crabs live in estuaries and shallow waters along the western Atlantic coast of the Americas.
The scientific name Callinectes sapidus means beautiful swimmer in Greek, and sapidus means savoury.
In Chesapeake Bay, blue crabs are often steamed with spices and picked by hand.
blue-crab.visual: one whole raw blue crab with a blue-green shell and blue-tinged claws, lying on its back
blue-crab.what: A sweet-fleshed crab with blue claws, popular in the US.

facts: The Araucana is a chicken breed associated with Chile, and it lays blue-shelled eggs.
The blue colour comes from a pigment deposited on the shell as the egg forms.
The colour is in the shell, not the yolk or white.
blue-egg.visual: one whole raw pale blue egg in its natural shell, lying on its side
blue-egg.what: A pale blue-shelled egg, laid by Araucana and similar hens.

facts: In France it is known as pied bleu, meaning blue foot.
It grows in woodland and leaf litter, usually in autumn.
In English it is also known as the wood blewit.
blue-foot-mushroom.visual: a small bunch of wild mushrooms with pale brown caps and lilac-blue stems, lying on the background
blue-foot-mushroom.what: A wild mushroom with a lilac-blue stem and a pale cap.

facts: The pale dusty coating on a blueberry is a natural waxy layer called bloom.
Cultivated blueberries were developed in the United States in the early twentieth century.
blueberry.visual: a small heap of fresh, round blueberries, dark blue with a pale dusty bloom on their skins
blueberry.what: Small dark-blue berries, sweet with a tangy edge.

facts: Blueberries are native to North America, and wild species were gathered there long before European settlement.
Jam is made by cooking fruit with sugar until it thickens, and the sugar helps the jam keep.
Blueberry plants were first cultivated commercially in the early 20th century in the United States.
blueberry-jam.visual: a small plain glass jar without a label, holding deep purple-blue blueberry jam, smooth and glossy
blueberry-jam.what: A sweet preserve of cooked blueberries and sugar.

facts: Bluefin tuna are among the largest bony fish, and they roam the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
Their rich, fatty flesh is highly prized in Japan, especially for sashimi and sushi.
Bluefin have been caught in the Mediterranean since ancient times.
bluefin-tuna.visual: a whole raw bluefin tuna, dark silvery-blue skin and glossy firm body, lying on its side
bluefin-tuna.what: A huge, fatty, deep-red ocean fish prized for sushi.

facts: Boerenkaas is Dutch for farmhouse cheese, traditionally made on the farm from the farm's own milk.
Traditional Dutch farmhouse cheeses are often made from raw, unpasteurised cow's milk.
boerenkaas.visual: a small wheel of pale yellow Dutch cheese with one wedge cut out, showing a firm cream-coloured interior and a rind
boerenkaas.what: A rich, firm Dutch cheese made on farms from raw milk.

facts: In Britain, strips of toast called soldiers are dipped into the soft yolk.
boiled-egg.visual: a whole peeled boiled egg, cut in half to show a runny yolk, on a plain white plate
boiled-egg.what: A hen's egg, simmered in its shell until cooked.

facts: The long cooking gives a soft texture, unlike roasted peanuts, which are dried and crisp.
They are a traditional snack across the Southern United States, often sold at roadside stands.
boiled-peanuts.visual: a small heap of boiled peanuts in soft, pale tan shells, on a plain white background
boiled-peanuts.what: Soft, salty peanuts simmered in their shells.

facts: Boiled sweets are made by cooking sugar and syrup to high heat, then cooling it until hard.
Many traditional British sweets, such as humbugs, are boiled sweets.
Crushed boiled sweets are sometimes scattered over cakes and biscuits for colour and crunch.
boiled-sweets.visual: a small loose heap of hard, glossy, brightly coloured boiled sweets, each with a smooth round shape
boiled-sweets.what: Hard, glassy sweets made by boiling sugar until it sets.

facts: Boiling fowl are older hens, kept past laying age, and need long, slow cooking to become tender.
Stewing hens were a traditional part of farmhouse cooking in Britain and Europe, valued for the rich flavour they gave broth.
boiling-fowl.visual: one whole raw older hen with pale yellowish skin, plump and untrussed, lying on its side
boiling-fowl.what: An older hen, tough but rich, best in slow-cooked stock.

facts: The sauce is named after Bologna, the city in northern Italy where it developed.
In Italy the sauce is called ragù alla bolognese and is traditionally served with tagliatelle.
bolognese-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, deep red meat sauce, glossy and rich
bolognese-sauce.what: A rich, slow-cooked meat and tomato sauce for pasta.

facts: Bombay mix is named after Bombay, the former name of Mumbai in western India.
It is typically made from fried lentils, peanuts and thin, crisp strands of gram flour.
bombay-mix.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of golden, crunchy spiced snack mix, evenly mixed
bombay-mix.what: A crunchy snack of lentils, peanuts and fried noodles.

facts: Marrow is the soft, fatty tissue found inside the hollow centres of large animal bones.
Roast bone marrow served on toast is a classic dish in British and French cooking.
bone-marrow.visual: a cut section of raw beef shin bone lying flat, the pale pink marrow visible in its centre
bone-marrow.what: Soft, rich fat from inside beef bones, usually roasted.

facts: Thigh meat is darker than breast meat because the leg muscles are used more during a bird's life.
Boneless thighs are widely used in curries, kebabs and braises in cuisines around the world.
boneless-chicken-thigh.visual: two raw skin-on boneless chicken thigh fillets, pale pink with smooth skin, lying side by side
boneless-chicken-thigh.what: Tender, juicy dark meat from the leg, with no bone.

facts: Quail are small birds that have been hunted and farmed for a very long time.
Quail are farmed in many countries and are sold whole, halved or boned.
Boning removes the small bones so that the bird can be stuffed or flattened for quick grilling.
boneless-quail.visual: a whole raw boneless quail, opened out flat, pale pink meat and dark brown skin, on a plain background
boneless-quail.what: A small game bird, boned and ready to cook.

facts: Bonito is the source of katsuobushi, a dried and smoked fish shaved into flakes to make Japanese stock.
Bonito belongs to the tuna and mackerel family and is a fast-swimming fish of warm seas.
bonito.visual: a whole raw bonito fish, sleek silver-blue back with dark stripes
bonito.what: A robust, oily fish of the tuna family, good grilled.

facts: Katsuobushi is made from skipjack tuna that is boiled, smoked and dried until hard.
They are shaved thinly and often sprinkled over hot dishes, where the heat makes them move.
bonito-flakes.visual: a small heap of thin, curled dried bonito flakes, pale amber with a silky sheen
bonito-flakes.what: Smoky dried fish shavings used to flavour Japanese stock.

facts: Borage is native to the Mediterranean region and was grown in European gardens for centuries.
Its star-shaped flowers are edible and are often used to decorate drinks and salads.
The leaves were traditionally added to cool summer drinks for their mild cucumber taste.
borage.visual: a small bunch of hairy green leaves and star-shaped blue flowers on their stems
borage.what: A herb with cucumber-tasting leaves and blue star flowers.

facts: Borlotti beans are a variety of common bean that reached Europe from the Americas.
In Italy they are a classic ingredient in pasta e fagioli and minestrone soups.
Their red speckles fade to a plain beige once the beans are cooked.
borlotti-beans-fresh.visual: a small heap of fresh borlotti bean pods, pale cream flecked with bright red
borlotti-beans-fresh.what: A speckled Italian bean, eaten shelled and fresh.

facts: The Bosc pear is named after Louis Bosc, a French botanist.
Its russeted skin is a natural layer of corky cells, and the pear holds its shape well when cooked.
It is widely grown in Europe and North America, and is often used in tarts and for poaching.
bosc-pear.visual: a whole ripe Bosc pear, brown russeted skin and long narrow neck, lying on its side
bosc-pear.what: A firm, spicy pear with a long neck and brown skin.

facts: Bottarga is roe that is salted, pressed and air-dried, most often from grey mullet or tuna.
It is a traditional food of Sardinia, Sicily and other Mediterranean coasts.
It is usually finely grated over pasta, and its name comes from the Arabic word for roe.
bottarga.visual: one cut piece of firm, smooth amber fish roe, the cut face clearly showing
bottarga.what: Salted, pressed fish roe, usually from grey mullet.

facts: Bottle gourd is one of the oldest cultivated plants, grown in Africa and Asia for thousands of years.
Bottle gourd belongs to the cucurbit family, which includes cucumbers, melons and pumpkins.
It is widely eaten in India, where it is cooked in dals, curries and stir-fries.
bottle-gourd.visual: one whole pale green bottle gourd, long and narrow with a bulbous base, lying on its side
bottle-gourd.what: A mild, pale green squash used in curries and soups.

facts: Boudin blanc is a traditional French sausage, often eaten at Christmas and the New Year.
Its filling is a smooth, pale mixture of minced meat, milk or cream, and mild seasoning.
boudin-blanc.visual: one whole raw boudin blanc sausage, pale cream-coloured casing, lying in a gentle curve
boudin-blanc.what: A delicate French white sausage of pork or chicken.

facts: Boudin noir is a sausage made from pork blood, usually with fat, onion and sometimes apple.
Many regional versions exist in France, and apple is a common addition in areas such as Normandy.
boudin-noir.visual: one whole black sausage link, glossy purple-black casing, lying in a gentle curve
boudin-noir.what: A French blood sausage, often with apple and onion.

facts: The name is French and means a garnished bouquet of herbs.
Classic French cooking used it for stocks, soups and braises.
bouquet-garni.visual: a small bundle of fresh parsley, thyme sprigs and a bay leaf tied together with white string
bouquet-garni.what: A tied bundle of herbs that flavours stocks and stews.

facts: Bourbon must be made in the United States, and it is mostly made from corn.
Ageing in charred oak barrels gives bourbon its colour and its vanilla and caramel notes.
bourbon.visual: a clear drinking glass half full of deep amber bourbon
bourbon.what: A sweet American whiskey, aged in charred oak barrels.

facts: Bourbon biscuits have been a British favourite for more than a century.
bourbon-biscuits.visual: two dark chocolate-brown biscuits stacked on a plain white plate, one turned to show the pale cream filling
bourbon-biscuits.what: Chocolate biscuits sandwiched with sweet cream filling.

facts: The berry is a cross of several berries, including blackberry and raspberry.
Boysenberries are often made into jams, pies and syrups, and are sold fresh in summer.
boysenberry.visual: a small heap of ripe boysenberries, deep purple-red, glossy and plump, loose on the background
boysenberry.what: A large, juicy, winey berry, good for jams and pies.

facts: The Braeburn apple was first found as a chance seedling in a New Zealand orchard in the 1950s.
Braeburns are now grown in many countries, including New Zealand, South Africa and the United States.
Braeburn is firm enough to hold its shape when baked, which makes it good for tarts and crumbles.
braeburn-apple.visual: one whole red and gold braeburn apple, streaked skin, lying on its side
braeburn-apple.what: A crisp, sweet-tart apple from New Zealand that bakes well.

facts: The Bramley grew from a seedling planted in Southwell, Nottinghamshire, in the early 1800s.
It takes its name from Matthew Bramley, a local landowner connected with the tree's early history.
bramley-apple.visual: a whole green Bramley apple, slightly flattened and lumpy, with a dull green skin flecked with red
bramley-apple.what: A tart, green cooking apple that softens when baked.

facts: Bran is the tough outer layer of the wheat grain, separated during milling.
Bran flakes were developed in the United States as a breakfast cereal.
bran-flakes.visual: a small heap of golden-brown bran flakes, loose and crisp, on a plain background
bran-flakes.what: Crisp cereal flakes made mostly from wheat bran.

facts: The name comes from the Dutch word brandewijn, meaning burnt wine.
Cognac and Armagnac are two well-known brandies from France.
Brandy is often set alight in a dish, a technique called flambe.
brandy.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle holding amber brandy
brandy.what: A strong spirit distilled from fermented wine or fruit.

facts: Bratwurst is a family of fresh sausages with a long history in German cooking.
It is usually grilled, pan-fried or simmered, and often served in a bread roll with mustard.
bratwurst.visual: a pair of raw pale pink bratwurst sausages, smooth skins, lying in a gentle curve
bratwurst.what: A German pork sausage seasoned with nutmeg and marjoram.

facts: Brawn is traditionally made by simmering pig's head until the meat falls away and sets in its own jelly.
brawn.visual: A thick cut slice of pale pink jellied pork, set in clear jelly with flecks of meat, showing a clean cut face.
brawn.what: Jellied pork made from the head, sliced cold.

facts: Brazil nuts come from very tall trees native to the Amazon rainforest.
They grow inside a hard, round woody fruit that falls from the tree when ripe.
brazil-nuts.visual: a small heap of raw shelled Brazil nuts, pale beige triangular nuts with a dark brown skin
brazil-nuts.what: Large, creamy nuts that grow inside a hard woody pod.

facts: Bread and butter pickles are an American style, traditionally made with cucumber, sugar, vinegar and spices.
Sliced cucumbers are salted before pickling, which draws out water and helps them stay crisp.
bread-and-butter-pickles.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thin, pale green sliced pickled cucumber in a light golden brine
bread-and-butter-pickles.what: Thin cucumber slices pickled in a sweet and sour brine.

facts: Bread sauce is a traditional English accompaniment to roast turkey, chicken and game.
It is thickened with breadcrumbs and simmered with milk, onion and cloves.
bread-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, pale cream-coloured sauce, thick and slightly speckled
bread-sauce.what: A creamy, spiced sauce served with roast poultry.

facts: Squid has been eaten in coastal Mediterranean and East Asian cooking for centuries.
breaded-calamari-rings.visual: a small pile of golden, crumb-coated fried squid rings on a plain white plate, evenly coloured
breaded-calamari-rings.what: Squid rings coated in crumbs and fried until crisp.

facts: Camembert is a soft cheese from Normandy, named after a village there.
breaded-camembert-wedges.visual: golden breaded cheese wedges arranged on a plain white plate, one wedge cut open to show the soft melted centre
breaded-camembert-wedges.what: Wedges of soft cheese coated in breadcrumbs and fried.

facts: Coating meat in egg and crumbs before frying is an old technique found in many cuisines.
The word burger is short for hamburger, named after the German city of Hamburg.
breaded-chicken-burger.visual: one golden-brown breaded chicken patty with a crisp crumb coating, served on a plain white plate
breaded-chicken-burger.what: A crumbed chicken patty shaped to sit in a bun.

facts: The name goujon is French and originally referred to a small freshwater fish called the gudgeon.
They are typically dipped in egg, coated in breadcrumbs, then fried or baked until golden.
breaded-chicken-goujons.visual: three golden crumbed chicken goujons lying side by side on a plain white plate
breaded-chicken-goujons.what: Strips of chicken coated in crispy golden breadcrumbs.

facts: Breadfruit is native to the Pacific islands and was later carried by sailors to the Caribbean.
It is harvested while still firm, then roasted, boiled or fried before eating.
It is an important staple food in parts of the Pacific and the Caribbean.
breadfruit.visual: a whole round green breadfruit with a bumpy, textured skin, lying on a plain white background
breadfruit.what: A starchy tropical fruit, cooked and eaten like potato.

facts: Bream is a name used for several fish, found in both fresh water and the sea.
Common bream live in lakes and slow-moving rivers across much of Europe.
Sea bream is popular around the Mediterranean, where it is often baked whole.
bream.visual: one whole raw bream, silvery scales and a dark grey back, lying in a gentle curve on a plain background
bream.what: A silvery, mild white fish with sweet, flaky flesh.

facts: Bresaola comes from the Valtellina valley in the Lombardy region of northern Italy.
The beef is salted, seasoned and air-dried until it becomes dense and deep red.
bresaola.visual: a neat fan of thin dark red air-dried beef slices, lying flat, with pale fat marbling visible
bresaola.what: Air-dried, salted beef from Italy, sliced paper-thin.

facts: Bresse chicken comes from the Bresse region of eastern France and has a protected designation of origin.
Birds are traditionally raised outdoors and identified by their white feathers and blue legs.
bresse-chicken.visual: one whole raw Bresse chicken, white plumage and blue-grey legs, lying on its side on a plain background
bresse-chicken.what: A French chicken prized for its firm, flavourful meat.

facts: Brik is a thin pastry leaf used across North Africa, especially in Tunisia.
In Tunisia it is traditionally wrapped around a whole egg and fried until crisp, in a dish called brik a l'oeuf.
brick-pastry.visual: a single round sheet of thin, pale golden-cream brick pastry, lying flat, slightly translucent
brick-pastry.what: A paper-thin North African pastry used for crisp parcels.

facts: Bridge rolls are a British bakery staple, popular at buffets, weddings and afternoon teas.
Soft white bread rolls have been made in Britain for centuries, often split and filled.
Their small size makes them easy to fill, which is why they suit finger food.
bridge-roll.visual: one soft white finger-shaped bread roll, pale and lightly dusted, on a plain white plate
bridge-roll.what: Small, soft, finger-shaped rolls for party sandwiches.

facts: Brie takes its name from the Brie region of northern France, east of Paris.
It is made from cow's milk and ripened from the outside in by a white mould.
brie.visual: one wedge cut from a round of brie, pale ivory interior and a soft white rind along the edge
brie.what: A soft, mild cheese with a white bloomy rind.

facts: Brie de Meaux is a French cheese from the Meaux area east of Paris.
It has a white bloomy rind and a soft, runny interior when fully ripe.
It is protected by a French appellation d'origine contrôlée, which sets rules on where and how it is made.
brie-de-meaux.visual: a round wheel of soft white-rinded cheese with one wedge cut out, pale creamy interior showing, resting on a plain background
brie-de-meaux.what: A soft, creamy French cheese with a white rind.

facts: Brill is a flatfish found in the eastern Atlantic and the Mediterranean Sea.
Its delicate white flesh flakes easily, so it is often cooked gently in butter.
Brill and turbot are close relatives, so cooks often treat them in similar ways.
brill.visual: one whole raw brill, flat brown speckled body, pale underside, lying flat on the background
brill.what: A flat, mild sea fish that is a cousin of turbot.

facts: It is named after Jean Anthelme Brillat-Savarin, the French gastronome and food writer.
brillat-savarin.visual: a round, soft white-rinded cheese with one wedge cut, creamy pale interior visible
brillat-savarin.what: A rich, soft cow's milk cheese from Normandy, France.

facts: Brioche is a French bread enriched with butter and eggs, which gives it a tender, golden crumb.
Brioche is a traditional French bread, and there are many regional shapes, from round loaves to small buns.
Brioche dough is kneaded for a long time with butter, which makes it softer and richer than plain bread.
brioche-burger-bun.visual: a single whole round brioche burger bun with a glossy golden top, plain and unfilled
brioche-burger-bun.what: A soft, golden bun made with butter and eggs.

facts: Brioche is a traditional French enriched bread, with origins often linked to Normandy.
The dough is enriched with butter and eggs, which gives it a soft, tender crumb.
In France it is often eaten at breakfast, and it is used for French toast and bread-and-butter pudding.
brioche-loaf.visual: a whole golden brioche loaf with a glossy, domed top and a rounded, browned crust
brioche-loaf.what: A rich, golden loaf made with butter and eggs.

facts: Broccoli belongs to the same species as cabbage, cauliflower and kale.
The name comes from the Italian broccolo, meaning the flowering top of a cabbage.
It was grown in Italy for centuries before it became popular in other countries.
broccoli.visual: a whole fresh head of green broccoli with tight florets and a thick pale stalk, on a plain background
broccoli.what: A green vegetable of tight florets on thick stems.

facts: Broccoli sprouts are young seedlings, picked only a few days after germination.
They belong to the cabbage family, like broccoli and kale.
They are often grown in trays and eaten raw in salads and sandwiches.
broccoli-sprouts.visual: a small heap of tiny bright green sprouts with pale stems and small leaves
broccoli-sprouts.what: Tiny young shoots with a peppery, fresh taste.

facts: Bronze fennel is a variety of common fennel, selected for its reddish-bronze leaves.
The name fennel is thought to come from the Latin word faenum, meaning hay.
bronze-fennel.visual: a small bunch of bronze fennel, feathery copper-green fronds on pale stalks
bronze-fennel.what: A coppery-leaved fennel with a mild aniseed flavour.

facts: Brown ales are dark beers with malt flavours of toffee, biscuit and nut.
Beer is often used to braise beef, as the malt adds depth to a stew.
brown-ale.visual: a clear drinking glass of dark brown ale, topped by a small off-white foam
brown-ale.what: A malty, nutty beer that gives rich body to beef stews.

facts: Basmati is often said to mean fragrant, and it is grown in the foothills of the Himalayas.
Brown basmati keeps its bran layer, so it has a chewier texture and a nuttier flavour.
brown-basmati-rice.visual: a small heap of long slender brown basmati rice grains, dry and matt, lying on a plain background
brown-basmati-rice.what: Long, nutty whole grain rice with a fragrant aroma.

facts: Brown beech mushrooms grow in tight clusters that share a common base.
They are native to East Asia, where they have long been used in cooking.
brown-beech-mushroom.visual: one small cluster of brown beech mushrooms, with thin pale-brown stems and tiny caps, raw, on the background
brown-beech-mushroom.what: Small clustered mushrooms with a crisp, nutty bite.

facts: Brown butter is made by heating butter until its milk solids toast and turn nutty.
Beurre noisette is the French name, meaning hazelnut butter, for its colour and aroma.
brown-butter.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of golden-brown melted butter, clear amber liquid with brown specks
brown-butter.what: Butter cooked until golden-brown and nutty in flavour.

facts: Brown stock is made by roasting chicken bones before they are simmered slowly in water.
Roasted bones give brown stock a darker colour and a richer, more savoury taste than white stock.
brown-chicken-stock.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of dark brown chicken stock, glossy and clear
brown-chicken-stock.what: A rich, dark stock made from roasted chicken bones.

facts: Brown crab is a common shellfish around the coasts of Britain and Ireland.
The body meat, called brown meat, is rich and strongly flavoured, while the claws yield sweet white meat.
Dressed crab is a traditional British dish, with the brown and white meat served back in the shell.
brown-crab.visual: a whole raw brown crab with a mottled reddish-brown shell, claws held together in front
brown-crab.what: A crab with rich brown meat and sweet white claw meat.

facts: Brown crab meat comes from the body cavity, not the claws, and is softer than white meat.
The brown crab is common around the British Isles and the coasts of northern Europe.
In Britain, dressed crab is traditionally made by mixing brown and white meat with seasoning.
brown-crab-meat.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of brown crab meat, soft creamy brown flakes
brown-crab-meat.what: Dark, richly flavoured meat from the body of a crab.

facts: Shell colour is set by the breed of hen, not by the quality of the egg.
The brown colour is a pigment the hen deposits on the shell while the egg forms inside her.
brown-egg.visual: a single whole brown hen's egg with a smooth matte shell, lying on its side
brown-egg.what: A hen's egg with a brown shell, popular in Britain.

facts: Lentils are among the oldest cultivated crops, grown in the Middle East for thousands of years.
Lentils are the dried seeds of a small bushy plant in the pea family, grown in many countries.
Lentils are common in Indian dhal and in British hearty soups and stews.
brown-lentils.visual: a small loose heap of dry, flat, brown lentils, seen from above
brown-lentils.what: Small, flat, earthy pulses, widely used in soups.

facts: Brown mustard seeds come from Brassica juncea, a plant widely grown in India and parts of Asia.
In Indian cooking the seeds are fried in hot oil at the start of a dish, a process called tempering.
Whole-grain mustard is made by crushing mustard seeds and mixing them with vinegar, rather than grinding them smooth.
brown-mustard-seeds.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of small, round, dark brown mustard seeds, loose and dry
brown-mustard-seeds.what: Small, hot seeds used for tempering spices.

facts: Onions have been cultivated for thousands of years, with origins in Central Asia.
When cooked slowly, their natural sugars caramelise and turn them sweet and golden.
Brown onions are the usual choice for soups, stews and gravies in British and American cooking.
brown-onion.visual: a whole brown onion with papery golden-brown skin and trimmed roots
brown-onion.what: The everyday cooking onion, sweet when browned.

facts: Brown rice keeps the bran and germ that white rice loses during milling.
It takes longer to cook than white rice because its outer layer is left intact.
Brown rice is also sold as wholegrain rice, a term used in British supermarkets.
brown-rice.visual: a small heap of uncooked brown rice grains
brown-rice.what: Rice with the bran kept on, so it is chewy and nutty.

facts: It is made by cooking brown rice and treating it with enzymes, which turn its starch into sugars.
Its flavour is often described as butterscotch-like, and it is used as a sweetener in baking.
Similar rice-based syrups have a long history in East Asian cooking.
brown-rice-syrup.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass jar of thick, golden-brown syrup
brown-rice-syrup.what: A thick, mildly sweet syrup made from cooked brown rice.

facts: Brown sauce became a popular British table condiment in the late nineteenth century.
It is usually made from tomatoes, dates, malt vinegar and spices.
brown-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, dark brown sauce, smooth and glossy
brown-sauce.what: A thick, tangy, fruity sauce, often served with bacon.

facts: Brown shrimp live in shallow, sandy waters around Britain and the North Sea.
Potted shrimp, cooked and sealed under clarified butter with spices, is a traditional dish from Morecambe Bay.
brown-shrimp.visual: a small heap of tiny cooked brown shrimp, curled and pale pinkish-brown, on a plain white plate
brown-shrimp.what: Tiny sweet shrimp from British coasts, often sold potted.

facts: Brown trout are native to Europe, western Asia and North Africa, and were later introduced widely.
Brown trout is often cooked whole and simply, such as grilled or pan-fried in butter.
brown-trout.visual: a whole raw brown trout, speckled brown and gold, with pinkish-orange spots along its flank, lying straight
brown-trout.what: A freshwater trout with a gamier, stronger flavour.

facts: Sprout tops are a winter green, often cooked like spring greens or cabbage.
Brussels sprouts grow along a tall stalk, and the leafy top can be picked and cooked separately.
brussels-sprout-tops.visual: a bunch of fresh green Brussels sprout tops, loose frilly leaves on short pale stalks
brussels-sprout-tops.what: Leafy green tops picked from the sprout stalk.

facts: Brussels sprouts are named after Brussels, the capital of Belgium, where they were grown.
They grow along a tall stalk, with each sprout forming in the join between stem and leaf.
brussels-sprouts.visual: a loose heap of firm, bright green Brussels sprouts, some outer leaves still attached
brussels-sprouts.what: Tiny green cabbage-like buds that grow along a tall stem.

facts: Bryndza is made from sheep's milk and is a traditional cheese in Slovakia and Poland.
It is often spread over halušky, Slovak potato dumplings, in a much-loved dish.
Bryndza is often made by shepherds in mountain regions, where sheep's milk is plentiful.
bryndza.visual: a soft white block of sheep's cheese with one crumbly cut face, lying on the background
bryndza.what: A tangy, creamy sheep's cheese from Slovakia.

facts: Bucatini is a long pasta with a hole running through the centre of each strand, like a thick spaghetti.
The name comes from the Italian word bucato, meaning pierced, for the hole through each strand.
Amatriciana, from the town of Amatrice, is a classic sauce for bucatini in Rome.
bucatini.visual: a small heap of dried bucatini pasta, long hollow strands loosely tangled
bucatini.what: Thick hollow spaghetti that holds sauce well.

facts: Hot-smoking cooks the fish while smoke flavours it, so buckling needs no further cooking.
Hot-smoked fish is cooked by smoke at higher temperatures than cold-smoked fish.
buckling.visual: one whole hot-smoked herring with golden-brown skin, lying on its side
buckling.what: A hot-smoked whole herring, ready to eat without cooking.

facts: Buckwheat is not a true cereal; it is the seed of a plant related to rhubarb.
Buckwheat flour is used in Japanese soba noodles and in galettes from Brittany in France.
Buckwheat has been grown across Asia and Europe for centuries, often on poor soils.
buckwheat-flour.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine greyish-beige buckwheat flour, level surface
buckwheat-flour.what: A nutty, earthy flour milled from buckwheat seeds.

facts: Savoury galettes from Brittany in north-west France are often folded into squares or triangles.
They are traditionally cooked on a flat griddle called a bilig in the Breton language.
buckwheat-galette.visual: a single folded galette, greyish-brown and lacy at the edges, served flat on a small plain white plate
buckwheat-galette.what: A thin, lacy crepe of buckwheat flour from Brittany.

facts: Buckwheat is not a true cereal, but the seed of a plant related to rhubarb and sorrel.
Kasha is the Russian and Eastern European name for cooked buckwheat groats.
Groats are often toasted before cooking, which deepens their nutty flavour.
buckwheat-groats.visual: a small heap of golden-brown buckwheat groats, sharp-edged triangular grains
buckwheat-groats.what: Toasted buckwheat seeds with a nutty, earthy flavour.

facts: Citron is one of the original citrus fruits, and Buddha's Hand is a fingered variety of it.
Its name refers to its fingered shape, and it is sometimes used as a temple offering in East Asia.
The peel is very fragrant and is grated for zest or candied, as the fruit has little flesh.
buddha-s-hand.visual: one whole yellow citron with long finger-like segments, bumpy textured skin, pale yellow
buddha-s-hand.what: A citron with finger-like segments and very little juice.

facts: Buffalo mozzarella is traditionally made in southern Italy, especially around Campania.
Water buffalo are kept for their milk in parts of southern Italy and across India.
buffalo-milk.visual: a clear drinking glass of thick, creamy white milk
buffalo-milk.what: Rich, creamy milk from water buffalo, used for mozzarella.

facts: Mozzarella di bufala is made from the milk of water buffalo, rather than cow's milk.
The Campania version is protected by an EU designation of origin.
The curd is stretched in hot water in a process called pasta filata.
buffalo-mozzarella.visual: one whole smooth white mozzarella ball with a glossy, slightly domed surface
buffalo-mozzarella.what: A soft, milky Italian cheese made from water buffalo milk.

facts: Buffalo wings were popularised in Buffalo, New York, in the 1960s.
The classic sauce is a cayenne-based hot sauce whisked together with melted butter.
Blue cheese dip is a traditional partner, its creaminess cooling the heat.
buffalo-wing-sauce.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of bright orange-red hot sauce, a little butter visible
buffalo-wing-sauce.what: Hot sauce and butter, spooned over chicken wings.

facts: Bulgogi's name is Korean for fire meat, reflecting how it is grilled.
Grated Asian pear is a traditional marinade ingredient, adding sweetness and softening the meat.
bulgogi-beef.visual: thin raw beef slices, deep red with fine marbling, fanned out in an overlapping row
bulgogi-beef.what: Thin beef slices, ready to marinate for Korean barbecue.

facts: Bulgur is an ancient food of the Middle East, made by parboiling wheat, drying it and cracking it.
Tabbouleh, a salad from the Levant, is traditionally made with bulgur, parsley and mint.
Bulgur is also used in pilaf and in kibbeh, a dish of meat and spiced bulgur shaped into patties.
bulgur-wheat.visual: a small plain white bowl of dry, pale golden bulgur grains, coarse and cracked
bulgur-wheat.what: Parboiled, dried and cracked wheat, ready in minutes.

facts: A popular dish, bún thịt nướng, serves the noodles cold with grilled pork and herbs.
The noodles are cooked briefly in boiling water and then rinsed to stop them sticking.
bun-noodles.visual: a small plain white bowl of cooked white rice vermicelli noodles, loosely tangled
bun-noodles.what: A thin Vietnamese rice noodle served cold with herbs.

facts: Burdock is a thistle-like plant, and its root has been eaten in Japan and China for centuries.
In Japan the root is known as gobo, and it is often braised in soy and sugar as kinpira.
Burdock burrs once inspired the design of hook-and-loop fasteners.
burdock-root.visual: a whole long brown burdock root, thin and tapering, with rough dark skin and pale flesh
burdock-root.what: A long, earthy root with crisp, fibrous flesh.

facts: Relish is a condiment of chopped vegetables or fruit, pickled or cooked with vinegar and sugar.
Sweet pickle relish became popular in the United States, where it is a standard topping for hot dogs.
burger-relish.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with chunky green-flecked relish
burger-relish.what: A tangy, sweet-sour relish of chopped onion and gherkin.

facts: Burger sauce is a mayonnaise-based condiment, usually flavoured with ketchup, pickles and mustard.
Similar sauces are known as Thousand Island dressing in North America, though the recipes differ.
Burger sauces are typically spooned onto burgers or used as a dip for fries.
burger-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of pale orange, creamy burger sauce with a smooth, glossy surface
burger-sauce.what: A creamy, tangy, pale orange sauce for burgers.

facts: Burgundy wine takes its name from the region in eastern France where it is made.
Pinot Noir is the principal red grape of the Burgundy region.
Boeuf bourguignon takes its name from Burgundy, meaning beef in the style of Burgundy.
burgundy.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle filled with deep ruby-red wine
burgundy.what: A dry red wine from the Burgundy region of France.

facts: It is harvested in autumn and winter, often with trained dogs that sniff out the fungus.
Its flavour is milder than the black winter truffle, and it is often grated over dishes at the end.
burgundy-truffle.visual: a whole, knobbly dark brown truffle with a wrinkled surface and a few traces of earth
burgundy-truffle.what: An earthy fungus that grows below ground near tree roots.

facts: It has a mozzarella shell wrapped around a soft filling of cream and shredded curd.
The name comes from the Italian word burro, meaning butter, a reference to its creamy centre.
burrata.visual: one whole round ball of soft white burrata cheese with a smooth, thin skin, lying on its side
burrata.what: A fresh Italian cheese with a soft, creamy centre.

facts: Butter is made by churning cream until the fat separates from the liquid buttermilk.
Butter has been made for thousands of years, long before refrigeration existed.
Ghee is clarified butter with the milk solids removed, and is widely used in South Asian cooking.
butter.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth pale golden butter with a soft glossy surface
butter.what: A rich, creamy fat churned from cow's milk cream.

facts: Butter beans are the large variety of the lima bean, which was first grown in the Americas.
In Britain they are often sold dried or in jars, and used in stews and casseroles.
butter-beans.visual: a small heap of large, dried, cream-coloured butter beans, smooth and plump
butter-beans.what: Large, creamy white beans with a soft, buttery texture.

facts: Buttercream is a general term for frostings based on butter, and many versions exist.
Icing sugar is finely ground sugar, usually mixed with a little starch to stop it clumping.
Buttercream is widely used to decorate cakes and cupcakes in British and American baking.
buttercream.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of pale, softly whipped buttercream
buttercream.what: A smooth, sweet frosting made from butter and icing sugar.

facts: Butterflying means cutting out the bone and opening the joint so it cooks more evenly and quickly.
Lamb has been reared in Britain for centuries, and the leg is a classic joint for roasting.
