butterflied-leg-of-lamb.visual: one raw butterflied leg of lamb, boneless and opened flat, dark red meat and a thin fat cap
butterflied-leg-of-lamb.what: A leg of lamb boned and opened flat for quick cooking.

facts: Its name comes from the soft, buttery texture of its leaves.
Boston and Bibb are two popular varieties of butterhead lettuce.
Lettuce has been cultivated in Europe and the Middle East for thousands of years.
butterhead-lettuce.visual: one whole butterhead lettuce with soft, pale green, loosely layered leaves and trimmed roots
butterhead-lettuce.what: A soft, loose-leaved lettuce with a buttery texture.

facts: Traditionally, buttermilk was the liquid left after churning butter from cream.
Most modern buttermilk is cultured milk, thickened and soured by bacteria.
Its acidity reacts with baking soda, helping scones and pancakes rise.
buttermilk.visual: a clear drinking glass of thin, pale off-white liquid
buttermilk.what: Tangy, slightly thick milk used in baking and marinades.

facts: Butternut squash is a type of Cucurbita moschata, a species originally from Central America.
It is roasted, puréed into soup, or cubed into curries across many cuisines.
butternut-squash.visual: one whole butternut squash with smooth beige skin and a bulbous base
butternut-squash.what: A pale, sweet winter squash with a long neck.

facts: Ravioli are small pasta parcels, typically filled and sealed, and they originated in Italy.
Butternut squash is a winter squash, and its sweet flesh works well as a pasta filling.
Ravioli is often served with brown butter and sage, a classic Italian pairing.
butternut-squash-ravioli.visual: a small plain white plate holding several pale orange ravioli parcels, sealed at the edges and lightly cooked
butternut-squash-ravioli.what: Pasta parcels filled with sweet, mashed squash.

facts: Butterscotch flavour is a traditional favourite in both Britain and the United States.
In America, butterscotch is often used in puddings, sauces and sweets.
butterscotch.visual: a small heap of golden-brown, glossy butterscotch pieces, broken into irregular chunks
butterscotch.what: Toffee made from brown sugar and butter, slightly salty.

facts: Butterscotch flavour comes from cooking brown sugar and butter together until it caramelises.
Butterscotch is widely used in baking, especially in cookies, bars and sauces.
butterscotch-chips.visual: a small heap of golden-brown butterscotch chips, glossy and flat-sided, lying on a plain background
butterscotch-chips.what: Sweet brown-sugar drops that melt and set in baking.

facts: Button, chestnut and portobello mushrooms are all the same species, Agaricus bisporus, at different stages of growth.
They are grown on compost in dark, controlled rooms rather than foraged.
button-mushroom.visual: a whole raw button mushroom with a smooth, pale cream cap and short stem, lying on its side
button-mushroom.what: A mild, common cultivated mushroom sold in most shops.

facts: Byadgi chillies are named after Byadgi, a town in Karnataka in southern India.
They are prized for their colour, which tints dishes without making them very hot.
Chilli reached India from the Americas and is now central to many Indian dishes.
byadgi-chilli.visual: a small heap of dried deep red chillies with wrinkled skins, stems removed
byadgi-chilli.what: A deep red Indian chilli, mild in heat but rich in colour.

facts: Cabernet Sauvignon is a widely planted red grape variety across many wine regions.
It is a cross of Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc, developed in France.
cabernet-sauvignon.visual: a clear drinking glass filled with deep ruby-red wine
cabernet-sauvignon.what: A full-bodied red wine with blackcurrant flavours.

facts: Caboc is a soft, full-fat cheese that originated in the Highlands of Scotland.
Oats have been a staple of Scottish cooking for centuries, and porridge is the best known example.
caboc.visual: one whole roll of soft white cheese, its outside coated in toasted oat flakes, lying on its side
caboc.what: A soft Scottish cheese rolled in toasted oats.

facts: Cabrales is made in the Asturias region of northern Spain, from a mix of cow's, goat's and sheep's milk.
It is matured in natural limestone caves in the Picos de Europa mountains, which keep it cool and humid.
Cabrales has a protected designation of origin, which means only cheese made in the area can carry its name.
cabrales.visual: a block of crumbly blue cheese with a grey-brown rind and one wedge cut away, blue veins showing
cabrales.what: A strong, crumbly blue cheese from northern Spain.

facts: Cacao butter is the natural fat in cocoa beans, pressed out when cocoa solids are separated.
It is what gives white chocolate its smooth texture and melting quality.
Cacao butter is solid at room temperature but melts close to body temperature.
cacao-butter.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of pale ivory cacao butter, smooth and solid, with a few shaved curls
cacao-butter.what: A pale, mild fat pressed from cocoa beans.

facts: Cachaça is made in Brazil from fermented sugarcane juice.
It is the base spirit of the caipirinha, Brazil's best-known cocktail.
It can be aged in wooden barrels, which gives some versions a golden colour.
cachaca.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of clear, colourless spirit
cachaca.what: A clear spirit distilled from fresh sugarcane juice.

facts: It is made by stretching curd, then shaping and hanging it to dry in southern Italy.
Caciocavallo is made in several regions of southern Italy, including Campania and Puglia.
caciocavallo.visual: one whole teardrop-shaped cheese with a smooth pale golden rind, lying on its side
caciocavallo.what: A firm, tangy Italian cheese shaped like a teardrop.

facts: Caerphilly is named after the town of Caerphilly in South Wales, where it was traditionally made.
It is traditionally eaten young, when it is moist and crumbly with a clean, fresh flavour.
caerphilly.visual: a block of pale white crumbly cheese with one wedge cut away, the crumbly texture visible
caerphilly.what: A crumbly, lemony white cheese from Wales.

facts: The Caesar salad was created in Tijuana, Mexico, in the 1920s by restaurateur Caesar Cardini.
The dressing is usually served with crisp romaine lettuce, croutons and shaved parmesan.
caesar-dressing.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of creamy pale dressing, smooth and thick
caesar-dressing.what: A creamy, savoury dressing for crisp lettuce salads.

facts: Cajeta is most associated with Celaya in the Mexican state of Guanajuato, where goat milk caramel is traditional.
Cajeta is spooned over ice cream, pancakes and fruit, and is a common filling for pastries.
cajeta.visual: a plain glass jar without a label of thick, glossy amber-brown caramel
cajeta.what: A thick, sweet caramel made from slowly cooked goat milk.

facts: Cajun seasoning takes its name from Cajun cooking in south Louisiana.
Cajun cooking grew from the traditions of Acadian settlers who arrived in Louisiana in the 1700s.
cajun-seasoning.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of reddish-brown ground spice blend
cajun-seasoning.what: A peppery, garlicky spice mix for Louisiana-style dishes.

facts: Calabrese is named after Calabria in southern Italy, where it has been grown for a long time.
Broccoli and cauliflower are both forms of the same wild cabbage species.
The name broccoli comes from the Italian 'broccolo', a word for a cabbage's flowering top.
calabrese.visual: one whole fresh head of green calabrese broccoli on its stem, dense tight florets, bright green, lying on a plain background
calabrese.what: The standard green headed broccoli sold across Britain.

facts: Calamansi is thought to be a hybrid of kumquat and mandarin orange.
It is widely grown across Southeast Asia and is used as juice, or squeezed over food.
In Florida the same tree is grown as an ornamental and known as calamondin.
calamansi.visual: one whole small round green calamansi fruit, smooth-skinned and slightly glossy
calamansi.what: A tiny, tart, fragrant citrus used in Philippine cooking.

facts: Calamarata means squid-like in Italian, from the word calamaro, meaning squid.
Calamarata is associated with Naples and the Campania region of southern Italy.
Its wide rings suit chunky sauces, and it is often served with seafood in coastal Italian cooking.
calamarata.visual: a small heap of dried calamarata pasta, short wide pale rings with a smooth surface
calamarata.what: Wide ring pasta, traditionally served with seafood sauces.

facts: Calasparra rice is grown in the Segura river valley in Murcia, in south-east Spain.
It holds its shape and absorbs stock well, which makes it suited to paella.
It has a protected designation of origin, so only rice grown in its region can carry the name.
calasparra-rice.visual: a small loose heap of dry, pale white short-grain rice grains
calasparra-rice.what: A short-grain Spanish rice that soaks up liquid well.

facts: Calf's liver is prized in European cooking for its mild flavour and tender texture.
It is often fried quickly with onions, a classic pairing in British and European cooking.
calf-s-liver.visual: one thin raw calf's liver slice, smooth, glossy and reddish-brown, lying flat on a plain background
calf-s-liver.what: Tender, mild liver from a young calf, quickly seared.

facts: Calvados is made from cider apples and aged in oak casks.
It takes its name from the Calvados department in north-west France.
calvados.visual: a clear drinking glass of amber-coloured calvados
calvados.what: A strong apple brandy distilled from cider in Normandy.

facts: The name calzone comes from the Italian word for a stocking, a reference to its folded shape.
Dough for a calzone is usually the same as pizza dough, rolled out and folded over the filling.
calzone-dough.visual: one smooth round ball of pale unbaked bread dough, lightly floured, sitting alone
calzone-dough.what: Soft dough that is folded over a filling and baked.

facts: Camels have been herded across desert regions of North Africa, Arabia and Central Asia.
Camel meat is often slow-cooked in stews in parts of North Africa and the Middle East.
Camels are also kept for their milk, which is drunk and made into cheese.
camel-meat.visual: a raw boneless cut of deep red camel meat, fine grain and a thin rim of fat, lying flat
camel-meat.what: Lean red meat from the camel, eaten in Africa and Asia.

facts: It has been used for cooking in East Asia for centuries.
The tea-oil camellia is closely related to the plant that gives us tea, which is why the oil is sometimes called tea seed oil.
camellia-oil.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of light golden camellia oil
camellia-oil.what: A light oil pressed from the seeds of a camellia shrub.

facts: Camembert takes its name from a village in Normandy in northern France.
The cheese is made from cow's milk and ripens from the outside in as the white rind develops.
Baking a whole camembert until molten and serving it with bread is a popular way to eat it.
camembert.visual: a whole round camembert cheese in its white rind, one wedge cut out to show the soft pale interior
camembert.what: A soft, creamy cheese with a white rind from Normandy.

facts: Camomile is a daisy-like plant, and its dried flowers are used to make tea.
The plant has been used in herbal drinks in Europe and the Middle East for centuries.
Its name comes from the Greek for earth apple, a nod to its scent.
camomile-tea.visual: a clear drinking glass of pale golden tea
camomile-tea.what: A floral herbal tea with a gentle, apple-like scent.

facts: Campanelle means little bells in Italian, a name that describes the pasta's shape.
It is made in Italy and is one of many short pasta shapes sold across the country.
campanelle.visual: a small heap of dried uncooked campanelle pasta, pale cream bell shapes with frilled edges, lying loose
campanelle.what: Frilled, bell-shaped pasta that holds creamy sauce well.

facts: Canadian bacon is cut from the lean loin, unlike streaky bacon, which comes from the belly.
In North America it is traditionally used in eggs Benedict.
canadian-bacon.visual: two round, pale pink slices of cured pork loin with a thin edge of fat, lying flat
canadian-bacon.what: Lean cured pork loin, cut into round slices.

facts: Canary melon is a winter melon in the same species as cantaloupe and honeydew.
It is usually eaten chilled and sliced, with the seeds scooped out first.
canary-melon.visual: one whole yellow canary melon, smooth bright yellow skin, lying on its side
canary-melon.what: A yellow-skinned melon with pale, mildly sweet flesh.

facts: Cancoillotte is made from curd cheese, cooked with butter and water until smooth.
It is traditionally eaten warm, spread on bread or poured over potatoes.
It is mostly associated with the Jura and Franche-Comte area of eastern France.
cancoillotte.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, pale yellow runny cheese spread
cancoillotte.what: A soft, runny spread of cooked cheese from eastern France.

facts: Candied citron is a traditional ingredient in Italian panettone and in Christmas fruit cakes.
Citron is one of the original citrus fruits and has been grown in the Mediterranean for a very long time.
candied-citron.visual: a small heap of candied citron pieces, translucent pale green-gold strips coated in sugar
candied-citron.what: Sugar-preserved citron peel, chopped and used in cakes.

facts: Candied peel is made by simmering citrus peel in sugar syrup until it becomes translucent.
It is a traditional ingredient in Italian panettone and in British Christmas cakes and puddings.
The sugar both sweetens the peel and helps preserve it.
candied-lemon-peel.visual: a small heap of glossy, sugar-coated yellow peel strips
candied-lemon-peel.what: Sweet, chewy strips of peel cooked slowly in sugar syrup.

facts: Candying nuts means cooking them in sugar until the sugar crisps around them.
Pecans, almonds and walnuts are all commonly candied, especially in North America.
Candied nuts are often scattered over salads and cheese boards for sweetness and crunch.
candied-nuts.visual: a small heap of sugar-glazed nuts with a glossy golden coating, lying on a plain background
candied-nuts.what: Nuts coated in a crisp layer of caramelised sugar.

facts: Candied peel was once a common preserve in Europe and is used in fruitcakes and Christmas puddings.
The peel is simmered repeatedly in sugar syrup until it turns soft and translucent.
Oranges originated in Asia, and the sweet orange spread to Europe through trade.
candied-orange-peel.visual: a small heap of glossy orange-yellow candied orange peel strips, sugar-coated and chewy-looking
candied-orange-peel.what: Strips of orange peel cooked in sugar syrup until chewy.

facts: Candying fruit means simmering it slowly in sugar syrup until the sugar replaces the water in it.
Candied citrus peel has been made around the Mediterranean for centuries and is used in Italian panettone.
Candied orange slices are often used to decorate Christmas cakes, a custom common in Britain.
candied-orange-slices.visual: one glossy candied orange slice, bright orange and sugar-glazed, lying flat
candied-orange-slices.what: Orange rounds simmered in syrup until glossy and sweet.

facts: It is a traditional ingredient in Christmas cakes, hot cross buns and panettone.
Candying was a traditional way to preserve fruit before refrigeration.
candied-peel.visual: a small heap of orange candied citrus peel pieces, sugar-glazed and translucent
candied-peel.what: Citrus peel cooked in sugar syrup until soft and sweet.

facts: Candying is a process in which fruit is slowly cooked in sugar syrup until it becomes preserved.
Candied fruit has been a feature of European baking and festive cakes, including Christmas puddings.
Pineapples are native to South America and were later spread across the tropics by traders.
candied-pineapple.visual: one candied pineapple ring, golden and glossy with sugar, lying flat
candied-pineapple.what: Chewy pineapple rings, cooked and coated in sugar.

facts: Candied violets have been used to decorate sweets and cakes in France for generations.
The flowers are painted with egg white or water and then dusted with fine sugar to dry.
Sweet violets are small scented flowers in the same family as pansies.
candied-violets.visual: a loose heap of sugar-crusted purple violet flowers in a small plain white ceramic bowl
candied-violets.what: A sugar-coated violet flower, used to decorate cakes.

facts: Candying nuts means coating them in sugar, which is then cooked until it hardens around them.
Walnuts are thought to have originated in Central Asia and spread westwards.
candied-walnuts.visual: a small heap of golden candied walnut halves, glossy with sugar, lying loose on the background
candied-walnuts.what: Sweet, crisp nut halves glazed in caramelised sugar.

facts: In parts of the Pacific, the oily nuts were once threaded on sticks and burned as candles.
The nut is widely grown across Southeast Asia and the Pacific islands.
candlenuts.visual: a small heap of shelled candlenuts, ivory-coloured and slightly lumpy
candlenuts.what: A waxy, cream-coloured nut used to thicken curry pastes.

facts: Candy floss is made by melting sugar and spinning it into fine threads, a process patented in the United States in 1897.
In America it is called cotton candy, a name that reflects its fluffy, cloud-like texture.
In Britain it is a classic fairground treat, often sold from brightly coloured stalls by the seaside.
candy-floss.visual: a small loose heap of pale pink candy floss, light and airy
candy-floss.what: Light, fluffy strands of spun sugar that melt away.

facts: Cane syrup is made by boiling down juice pressed from sugar cane.
It is lighter and milder than molasses, which is boiled for longer.
In Louisiana, it is poured over pancakes, waffles and biscuits.
cane-syrup.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of dark golden-brown syrup
cane-syrup.what: Dark syrup boiled from pressed sugar cane juice.

facts: Cannelloni means large reeds in Italian, a name that refers to the shape of the tubes.
Cannelloni are a baked pasta dish from Italy, usually filled and covered with sauce.
Traditionally, cannelloni were made at home by rolling sheets of fresh pasta around a filling.
cannelloni.visual: a small heap of uncooked dried cannelloni tubes, smooth pale cream pasta lying loosely together
cannelloni.what: Large pasta tubes, filled with cheese or meat and baked.

facts: Cantal is made in the Auvergne region of central France, mainly in the Cantal department.
It is traditionally made in large cylindrical wheels from cow's milk.
Cantal has Protected Designation of Origin status in the European Union.
cantal.visual: a block of firm pale yellow cheese with one thick wedge cut away, showing a smooth paste and a natural grey-brown rind
cantal.what: A firm, tangy French cheese from the Auvergne mountains.

facts: The name comes from Cantalupo, a papal summer estate near Rome.
Cantaloupe is often served in slices with Parma ham.
Its netted, tan skin is typical of muskmelons, a group of melons with fragrant flesh.
cantaloupe-melon.visual: a whole cantaloupe melon with pale netted tan skin, lying on its side
cantaloupe-melon.what: A round melon with orange flesh and a musky, sweet taste.

facts: Capellini means little hairs in Italian, a name for the very thin strands.
It cooks very quickly and suits light broths.
Pasta of this kind is traditionally served in Italian broths and light sauces.
capellini-d-angelo.visual: a small heap of pale, hair-fine dried pasta strands, loosely tangled
capellini-d-angelo.what: Very thin Italian pasta, sometimes called angel hair.

facts: Caperberries are the fruit of the caper bush, which grows wild around the Mediterranean.
They are picked before they ripen and then pickled in brine or vinegar.
caperberries.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of pale green pickled caperberries, oval berries with short stalks
caperberries.what: Pickled fruit from the caper bush, larger than capers.

facts: Capers are the unopened flower buds of a shrub that grows in dry, rocky Mediterranean places.
They have been pickled in salt or vinegar for use in Mediterranean cooking for a very long time.
Caperberries are the fruit that forms after the flower, and are sold as a separate pickle.
capers.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of small green pickled caper buds in brine
capers.what: Salty, sharp pickled buds of a Mediterranean shrub.

capon.visual: one whole raw capon with pale plump skin and tied legs, lying on its side
capon.what: A large, tender, castrated male chicken for roasting.

facts: The name cappellacci means large hats, a reference to the shape of the filled pasta.
A traditional speciality of Ferrara in Emilia-Romagna, it is often served with butter and sage.
cappellacci.visual: a small heap of uncooked pale yellow filled pasta parcels, shaped like little hats
cappellacci.what: Hat-shaped pasta from Ferrara, filled with pumpkin.

facts: Cappelletti are a stuffed pasta from Emilia-Romagna in northern Italy, where they are often served in broth.
The name means little hats, a reference to their shape.
Traditional fillings include meat, cheese or both, wrapped in fresh egg pasta.
cappelletti.visual: a small heap of raw cappelletti pasta, little pale yellow hat-shapes, dry and loose
cappelletti.what: Hat-shaped stuffed pasta, traditionally served in broth.

facts: The Cara Cara is a navel orange first found in 1976 on a farm in Venezuela.
Its pink flesh is coloured by natural pigments called carotenoids, which also colour carrots.
Navel oranges are usually seedless and are named for the small navel-like mark at the base of the fruit.
cara-cara-orange.visual: one orange cut in half, showing deep coral-pink segments, lying flat on a plain white background
cara-cara-orange.what: A pink-fleshed orange with a mild, berry-like sweetness.

facts: Caramel is made by heating sugar until it melts and turns brown, a process called caramelisation.
Caramel is used in crème caramel, flans and sauces across Europe and the Americas.
Caramel is also a chewy sweet, made by cooking sugar with butter and cream.
caramel.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of glossy amber-brown caramel sauce
caramel.what: Sugar cooked until it turns amber, bitter-sweet and glossy.

facts: Popcorn is made from a type of maize whose kernels burst when heated.
Popcorn was eaten by Indigenous peoples of the Americas thousands of years ago.
caramel-popcorn.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of golden caramel-coated popcorn pieces
caramel-popcorn.what: Puffed corn kernels coated in a sticky, sweet caramel.

facts: Caramel syrup is used in coffee drinks, puddings and cocktails.
Caramelised sugar has been used to colour and flavour food for centuries.
caramel-syrup.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of smooth, amber caramel syrup
caramel-syrup.what: A smooth amber sauce made by cooking sugar until golden.

facts: Spiced biscuits such as speculaas are traditionally baked in the Netherlands and Belgium around St Nicholas' feast.
Cinnamon, ginger and cloves are common spices in this style of biscuit.
caramelised-biscuits.visual: one golden spiced caramelised biscuit, crisp and brown, on a plain white plate
caramelised-biscuits.what: Crisp spiced biscuits with a caramel taste.

facts: Chutney takes its name from the Hindi word chatni, meaning a spiced relish.
caramelised-onion-chutney.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, full of dark glossy onion chutney, lid off
caramelised-onion-chutney.what: A dark, sweet, tangy relish of slow-cooked onions.

facts: Caraway seeds are the fruit of a plant related to parsley and carrot.
They have long been used in rye bread and in Central and Eastern European cooking.
Caraway is traditionally added to sauerkraut and to some rye and cabbage dishes.
caraway-seeds.visual: a small heap of curved brown caraway seeds, scattered loosely
caraway-seeds.what: Small, curved seeds with an aniseed-like flavour.

facts: Carbonara is a Roman pasta dish, and the story of its origins is still debated by food historians.
Traditional carbonara thickens from beaten egg and hot pasta, without cream.
Guanciale, cured pork cheek, is the traditional meat, though pancetta is widely used.
carbonara-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl holding a thick, pale golden creamy sauce, glossy and smooth
carbonara-sauce.what: A silky pasta sauce of egg, hard cheese and cured pork.

facts: Cardamom is native to the Western Ghats of southern India and the Sri Lankan highlands.
Cardamom has been traded for centuries and features in Indian, Scandinavian and Middle Eastern cooking.
Scandinavian bakers use cardamom in buns, and it flavours Arabic coffee.
cardamom-seeds.visual: a small loose heap of tiny dark brown-black cardamom seeds, shiny and angular
cardamom-seeds.what: Tiny dark seeds from cardamom pods, with a floral scent.

facts: Cardamom has been traded for thousands of years along routes linking South Asia and the Middle East.
Cardamom is a traditional flavour in Scandinavian baking, especially in sweet buns.
cardamom-sugar.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine pale golden sugar, dotted with tiny dark seed specks
cardamom-sugar.what: A fine sugar scented with ground cardamom pods.

facts: Cardoon is a close relative of the globe artichoke and grows wild around the Mediterranean.
The stalks are bitter when raw, so they are usually peeled and cooked before eating.
cardoon.visual: a bunch of long, ribbed, silvery-green cardoon stalks lying on a plain background
cardoon.what: A thistle relative with long, ribbed stalks for braising.

facts: Carnaroli is a medium-grain rice grown mainly in the Po Valley of northern Italy.
It was bred in Italy in the twentieth century to give a firm, creamy risotto.
Its grains hold their shape while releasing starch that thickens the cooking liquid.
carnaroli-rice.visual: a small heap of raw ivory-white carnaroli grains, plump and slightly chalky
carnaroli-rice.what: A long-grained Italian rice prized for creamy risotto.

facts: Carob comes from the carob tree, which grows around the Mediterranean and in the Middle East.
Carob pods are dried and ground into a flour, sometimes used as a cocoa substitute.
In Britain it is often sold as a chocolate-style alternative in shops.
carob.visual: one whole dried carob pod, long, flat, dark brown and leathery, lying on its side
carob.what: A sweet, cocoa-like pod from a Mediterranean tree.

facts: Carob is the pod of an evergreen Mediterranean tree, Ceratonia siliqua.
The pods are roasted and ground to a powder with a naturally sweet, toasty flavour.
The name carob comes from an Arabic word, kharrub, for the bean-like pod.
carob-powder.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine, dark brown carob powder with a smooth surface
carob-powder.what: A sweet powder from carob pods, used instead of cocoa.

facts: Carob is the pod of an evergreen tree native to the Mediterranean.
Carob pods have a naturally sweet flavour, and carob powder is used in place of cocoa.
Carob pods are also known in English as locust beans.
carob-syrup.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of dark brown syrup
carob-syrup.what: A dark, treacly syrup boiled from carob pods.

facts: Mustard-based barbecue sauce is a speciality of South Carolina, where it is often called Carolina gold.
The sauce is linked to German settlers in South Carolina, whose mustard-based traditions influenced it.
carolina-mustard-bbq-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, golden-yellow sauce, glossy and thick
carolina-mustard-bbq-sauce.what: A tangy, yellow barbecue sauce from South Carolina.

facts: It is a type of Capsicum chinense, the same species as the habanero pepper.
It was developed in South Carolina in the United States, and its heat is measured in Scoville units.
carolina-reaper.visual: a whole fresh red chilli pepper with a bumpy wrinkled skin and a curled tip
carolina-reaper.what: A very hot chilli, sweet at first and then scorching.

facts: The Carolina Reaper was developed in South Carolina in the United States, from a cross of chilli peppers.
Its heat is measured on the Scoville scale, a system based on how much a sample must be diluted.
carolina-reaper-flakes.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of dark red crushed chilli flakes, seeds visible
carolina-reaper-flakes.what: Crushed dried pepper flakes from a very hot chilli variety.

facts: The Carolina Reaper chilli was bred in South Carolina, United States, and is among the hottest chillies known.
Chilli heat is measured in Scoville units, a scale that rates the pungency of chillies.
Chillies are native to the Americas and spread to Asia and Europe after contact with the New World.
carolina-reaper-sauce.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with glossy deep red sauce
carolina-reaper-sauce.what: A fiery hot sauce made with one of the hottest chillies.

facts: Carp were kept in ponds in medieval Europe, and were eaten at festivals and feast days.
Carp are traditionally eaten at Christmas in Poland and the Czech Republic.
Carp is native to Asia and Europe and is now farmed in many countries.
carp.visual: one whole raw carp, scaled, olive-green and gold on the back, lying on its side
carp.what: A freshwater fish with firm white flesh and a mild flavour.

facts: Carrageen moss grows on rocky shores of the North Atlantic, including around the coasts of Ireland.
In Ireland and Britain it has long been simmered in milk to set a light, wobbly pudding.
carrageen-moss.visual: a small bunch of dried carrageen moss, thin twiggy fronds in reddish-brown and cream, lying on the background
carrageen-moss.what: A red seaweed that sets into a soft jelly when simmered.

facts: Carrot is a biennial plant in the parsley family, grown for its swollen taproot.
Carrots are thought to have been first cultivated in Central Asia, around modern Afghanistan.
The English word carrot comes from the French carotte, which goes back to Latin and Greek.
carrot.visual: a bunch of three whole orange carrots, long roots with feathery green tops still attached, on the plain background
carrot.what: A sweet, crunchy orange root used in soups and cakes.

facts: Carrots were first cultivated in Central Asia, and early roots were often purple or yellow.
Carrot juice is made by pressing or blending raw carrots, sometimes with a little water.
It is used as a base for some soups, sauces and cakes, as well as drunk on its own.
carrot-juice.visual: a clear drinking glass filled with bright orange carrot juice
carrot-juice.what: Sweet orange juice pressed from carrots.

facts: Casarecce is a traditional pasta of southern Italy, often served with robust tomato or meat sauces.
Its name is thought to come from an Italian word meaning homemade.
The twisted shape and ridges are well suited to catch chunky sauces.
casarecce.visual: a small heap of dry, twisted casarecce pasta in a small plain white bowl
casarecce.what: Rolled, S-shaped dried pasta with ridges that hold sauce.

facts: It is grown in Mexico and used in salsas and sauces.
Dried chillies like this are often toasted and ground to deepen their flavour.
cascabel-chilli.visual: a small heap of dried round cascabel chillies, dark red and wrinkled
cascabel-chilli.what: A small round dried chilli with a mild, nutty warmth.

facts: Cashews grow on a tree native to north-eastern Brazil, beneath a fleshy fruit called the cashew apple.
The shell contains a harsh oil, so cashews are processed before they reach shops.
cashew-butter.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with smooth pale beige nut butter
cashew-butter.what: A smooth, mellow spread made from ground cashew nuts.

facts: Cashews are native to north-eastern Brazil, and the tree was later spread to India and Africa by traders.
Cashew milk is often used in place of cream or dairy milk in vegan sauces and desserts.
cashew-milk.visual: a clear drinking glass filled with smooth, creamy off-white cashew milk
cashew-milk.what: A smooth, creamy plant milk blended from cashew nuts.

facts: Cashews grow on the cashew tree in tropical regions, and each nut hangs from the bottom of a fruit.
Cashews are native to north-eastern Brazil and were carried to India and Africa by Portuguese traders.
cashews.visual: a small heap of raw, pale cream-coloured cashew nuts in their curved shape
cashews.what: Curved, creamy nuts that grow beneath a cashew apple fruit.

facts: Casoncelli are a stuffed pasta from the Bergamo area of Lombardy in northern Italy.
Traditional fillings are often a mix of meat, breadcrumbs and cheese, sometimes with a sweet note.
The dough is folded over the filling and pinched shut at the edges, much like a ravioli.
casoncelli.visual: a small loose heap of fresh uncooked casoncelli pasta parcels with pinched edges, pale yellow dough
casoncelli.what: A folded Italian pasta parcel from Bergamo.

facts: Cassava is native to South America and is now a staple food across much of Africa and Asia.
Raw cassava contains natural compounds that must be removed by thorough cooking or processing.
Tapioca is made from cassava starch and is used in puddings and drinks.
cassava.visual: a whole raw cassava root, brown bark-like skin, one end cut to show white flesh, lying on its side
cassava.what: A starchy tropical root, boiled, fried or mashed.

facts: Cassava is a root vegetable native to South America and now grown across tropical regions.
The root is peeled, sliced thinly and fried or baked until crisp.
Cassava is a staple food in many parts of Africa, South America and Asia.
cassava-crisps.visual: a small loose heap of thin, golden-brown cassava crisps, lightly curled at the edges
cassava-crisps.what: Thin fried slices of cassava root, crisp and nutty.

facts: Cassava is a root crop native to South America and now widely grown across Africa.
In West Africa, the leaves are pounded until smooth and then stewed, often with palm oil.
Raw cassava leaves contain natural compounds that release cyanide, so they must be cooked thoroughly.
cassava-leaves.visual: a loose bunch of fresh dark green cassava leaves, glossy and lobed, their stems still attached
cassava-leaves.what: Green leaves of the cassava plant, cooked as a vegetable.

facts: Cassia is grown mainly in southern China and is widely used in Chinese cooking.
It is often sold as Chinese cinnamon and has a stronger, coarser flavour than true cinnamon.
The bark dries into rolled quills, which curl as the thick bark contracts.
cassia-bark.visual: a single rolled cassia bark quill, dark reddish-brown and rough, lying on its side
cassia-bark.what: A robust, spicy-sweet bark from Asian cassia trees.

facts: It is made in the Grana valley of Piedmont, traditionally from cow's milk, sometimes with goat's or sheep's milk too.
Castelmagno holds protected designation of origin status in the European Union.
The cheese is aged for months, which makes it firmer and more crumbly as it matures.
castelmagno.visual: a block of pale, crumbly cheese with one wedge cut, showing a creamy interior with faint blue-grey veins
castelmagno.what: A crumbly, tangy cheese from the Piedmont region of Italy.

facts: Castelvetrano olives take their name from a town in western Sicily.
They are a Nocellara del Belice variety, traditionally grown in the Belice valley of Sicily.
They are picked while still green and are usually cured in brine to soften their bitterness.
castelvetrano-olives.visual: a small heap of whole bright green olives with glossy, smooth skins, scattered loosely
castelvetrano-olives.what: Bright green Sicilian olives with a mild, buttery flavour.

facts: In the United States, caster sugar is usually called superfine sugar.
Its fine crystals dissolve more easily than granulated sugar, especially in cold liquids.
It is used for meringues, sponges and other light cakes.
caster-sugar.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine white sugar crystals
caster-sugar.what: Fine white sugar that dissolves quickly in baking.

facts: Catfish are named for their whiskers, which look a little like a cat's.
In the southern United States, catfish is traditionally coated in cornmeal and fried.
Much of the catfish eaten in the United States is farmed in ponds.
catfish-fillet.visual: a boneless raw catfish fillet, pale white flesh and a neat, flat shape, lying flat
catfish-fillet.what: A mild, firm white fish, popular for frying and grilling.

facts: Cauliflower is a cabbage relative that was developed in the Mediterranean region over centuries.
Cauliflower is grown for its dense flower head, which is kept pale by covering the leaves.
cauliflower.visual: one whole cauliflower, creamy white head, pale green leaves at its base, lying on a plain background
cauliflower.what: A pale white brassica with a mild, nutty flavour.

facts: It is named for its resemblance to a cauliflower head.
It grows at the base of trees, most often conifers, in woodland.
cauliflower-fungus.visual: a whole cauliflower fungus, a pale cream frilly cluster of flat wavy lobes, lying on the surface
cauliflower-fungus.what: A wild, frilly mushroom with a crunchy, nutty flavour.

facts: Cava is made mostly in Catalonia using the traditional method, as champagne is.
The name cava comes from the Catalan word for cellar.
cava.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle holding pale golden sparkling wine
cava.what: A dry sparkling wine from Spain, used in sauces and sangria.

facts: Cavatappi means corkscrew in Italian, a name that describes its twisted shape.
The ridged, spiral shape traps sauce, which is why it suits cheese sauces and baked dishes.
Cavatappi is often used in baked macaroni and cheese.
cavatappi.visual: a small heap of dry, golden-yellow corkscrew pasta tubes, ridged and twisted
cavatappi.what: Corkscrew-shaped pasta tubes that hold sauce well.

facts: Cavatelli come from southern Italy, where they are traditionally shaped by hand.
The name is often linked to the Italian word cavare, meaning to hollow out.
Cavatelli are often served with broccoli rabe and sausage, a classic pairing in Italian-American cooking.
cavatelli.visual: a small heap of dried cavatelli pasta, short curled ridged shapes, pale cream colour, lying loose on the background
cavatelli.what: Small curled pasta shells with a soft, chewy bite.

facts: Cavolo nero is an Italian kale, grown especially in Tuscany and used in the soup ribollita.
Its name means black cabbage in Italian, a reference to its very dark blue-green leaves.
The leaves are often shredded and simmered in soups, or braised with garlic and olive oil.
cavolo-nero.visual: a bunch of long dark blue-green cavolo nero leaves with pale stems, deeply crinkled
cavolo-nero.what: Dark, crinkled Italian greens that soften when cooked.

facts: The name cayenne is often used for ground red chilli powder, sold dried and finely milled.
Cayenne chillies are grown in many warm countries and are often dried before being ground.
cayenne-chilli.visual: one whole slim red cayenne chilli with a glossy skin and a curved stalk
cayenne-chilli.what: A long, thin red chilli with a sharp, fiery heat.

facts: Cayenne is a fine powder ground from dried hot red chillies of the Capsicum family.
It is widely used in Cajun, Indian and Mexican cooking to add heat to sauces and rubs.
cayenne-pepper.visual: a small plain glass jar without a label, holding fine bright red cayenne powder
cayenne-pepper.what: A hot, fine powder ground from dried red chillies.

facts: Celeriac is a variety of celery grown for its swollen root rather than its stalks.
Celeriac is native to the Mediterranean region, where wild celery grows along coasts and in marshes.
It is often grated raw into remoulade, a mustard-dressed salad, or mashed and roasted.
celeriac.visual: one whole raw celeriac bulb, knobbly brown skin, a few thin roots and a short stalk stub
celeriac.what: A knobbly, pale root vegetable with a celery-like flavour.

facts: The name celery comes from the Greek word selinon, meaning parsley.
Celery is one of the base vegetables in French cooking, alongside onion and carrot.
celery.visual: a bunch of pale green celery stalks with their leafy tops, the stalks lying flat and neatly gathered together
celery.what: A crisp vegetable with long, ribbed green stalks.

facts: Wild celery grows on Mediterranean coasts, and the ancient Greeks used it in garlands.
Blanched celery is grown with soil or covers that keep the inner stalks pale and mild.
celery-hearts.visual: a bunch of pale celery hearts with small pale leaves and cut ends visible
celery-hearts.what: Tender, pale, inner stalks from the centre of a celery.

facts: Celery is native to the Mediterranean region, and its green leaves are the tops of the same plant.
Celery seed, dried from the same plant, is ground into a spice used in soups and pickles.
celery-leaf.visual: a small bunch of fresh, bright green celery leaves on their trimmed stalks
celery-leaf.what: Strong, leafy tops of celery, good in soups and salads.

facts: Celery seed comes from the same plant as the crunchy stalks, grown for its seeds instead.
Celery salt became popular in American cooking and is a traditional rim seasoning for Bloody Mary cocktails.
Celery salt is a mix of salt and ground seed, so it is simple to make at home.
celery-salt.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with fine pale salt mixed with tiny brown celery seeds
celery-salt.what: Salt blended with ground celery seed for savoury flavour.

facts: Celery seeds come from the same species as cultivated celery, the wild plant it descends from.
They have been used in Mediterranean and European cooking for many centuries.
In America they are a classic addition to coleslaw and to the Bloody Mary cocktail.
celery-seeds.visual: a small heap of tiny brown oval seeds with fine ridges
celery-seeds.what: Tiny, bitter seeds with a strong celery-like aroma.

facts: Grey sea salt from Guérande is traditionally raked by hand from shallow tidal pools on the French Atlantic coast.
Sel gris means grey salt in French, and its colour comes from the clay lining of the salt pans.
celtic-grey-salt.visual: a small heap of coarse grey sea salt crystals, slightly damp and clumped, lying loose
celtic-grey-salt.what: A moist, grey sea salt raked from French tidal flats.

facts: Celtuce is grown mainly in China, where people have long eaten its thick stem.
The stem is peeled and then often stir-fried, pickled or sliced into salads.
Its name blends celery and lettuce, a nod to its crisp stem.
celtuce.visual: one whole raw celtuce stalk, long pale green stem with a few slim leaves at one end, lying flat
celtuce.what: A Chinese lettuce grown for its thick, crisp stem.

facts: They are a traditional food in China and are often served cold as a starter or snack.
Despite their name, they are cured for weeks or months rather than a century.
century-egg.visual: a whole century egg with its shell removed, dark amber-black surface with a glossy, jelly-like sheen
century-egg.what: A preserved egg with a dark, jelly-like white.

facts: Ceps grow wild in woodlands in Europe and North America, often near pine and oak trees.
The Italian name porcini means little pigs, though the origin of the nickname is uncertain.
In Italy and France, dried ceps are soaked and used to add deep flavour to risottos and sauces.
cep.visual: a whole fresh cep mushroom, domed brown cap above a thick pale bulbous stem
cep.what: A prized wild mushroom with a firm, nutty, meaty flavour.

facts: Cereal bars are made by pressing cereal grains, often oats, with a binder such as syrup or honey.
cereal-bar.visual: one plain rectangular cereal bar, unwrapped, golden-brown with visible oat flakes, lying flat
cereal-bar.what: A chewy bar of toasted grains bound with sugar syrup.

facts: Cerignola olives take their name from the town of Cerignola in Puglia, southern Italy.
Their size and firm flesh make them a popular choice for stuffing.
Puglia is one of Italy's main olive-growing regions.
cerignola-olives.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of large, plump green olives, some partly submerged in brine
cerignola-olives.what: Very large, mild green olives from southern Italy.

facts: Cervelat is usually made from pork and beef, and is sold ready to eat.
cervelat.visual: one whole uncut Swiss cervelat sausage, plump and smooth with a pale brown casing, lying in a gentle curve
cervelat.what: A mild Swiss sausage, popular for grilling and snacks.

facts: Ceylon cinnamon comes from the inner bark of an evergreen tree native to Sri Lanka.
It is sometimes called true cinnamon, to distinguish it from cassia.
Its quills are thin and crumble easily, unlike the thick, hard sticks of cassia.
ceylon-cinnamon.visual: a neat stack of thin, pale brown papery cinnamon quills
ceylon-cinnamon.what: Mild, delicate cinnamon from Sri Lanka in thin quills.

facts: Soba is a Japanese noodle made from buckwheat flour, and the name simply means buckwheat.
Cha soba is coloured and flavoured with powdered green tea, usually matcha, mixed into the dough.
Soba is often served cold with a dipping sauce, or hot in broth, across Japan.
cha-soba.visual: a loose heap of thin, straight, pale green dried noodles
cha-soba.what: Thin buckwheat noodles flecked green with tea.

facts: Chaat is a family of savoury Indian snacks, often sold by street vendors.
Black salt, a rock salt with a sulphur-like smell, is often used in these blends.
The blend is sprinkled over fruit, vegetables and snacks just before serving.
chaat-masala.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl heaped with pale brownish spice powder
chaat-masala.what: A tangy, salty spice blend for Indian street snacks.

facts: Chablis is made from Chardonnay grapes grown in the Chablis area of northern Burgundy.
The vineyards sit on ancient seabed limestone, full of fossilised oyster shells.
Chablis is often served with oysters and shellfish, and is made under strict appellation rules.
chablis.visual: a clear drinking glass of pale straw-coloured white wine
chablis.what: A dry, crisp white wine from the Burgundy region of France.

facts: The word chai comes from the Chinese word for tea and spread along trade routes.
Masala chai, a spiced milky tea, is widely drunk in India and Pakistan.
Cardamom, cinnamon, ginger and cloves are among the spices most often used in chai.
chai-tea.visual: a clear drinking glass of hot reddish-brown tea, plain and unadorned
chai-tea.what: Black tea brewed with milk and warm spices.

facts: Challah is traditionally eaten on the Jewish Sabbath and on festival days.
Eggs and oil in the dough give challah its rich, soft texture.
challah.visual: a whole braided golden challah loaf, its glossy crust catching the light, lying on the background
challah.what: A soft, slightly sweet braided bread for Shabbat.

facts: Chamomile is a daisy family plant, and its flowers have been used in infusions for centuries.
The name comes from the Greek for earth apple, a nod to its apple scent.
chamomile-flowers.visual: a small heap of dried chamomile flowers, tiny yellow centres and white petals, in a small plain white ceramic bowl
chamomile-flowers.what: Small daisy-like flowers with an apple-like scent.

facts: Champagne is a region of north-east France, and only sparkling wine from it may use the name.
Its bubbles come from a second fermentation inside the bottle.
The wine is mainly made from chardonnay, pinot noir and pinot meunier grapes.
champagne.visual: a plain unlabelled dark green glass bottle, full of pale golden sparkling wine
champagne.what: Sparkling white wine from the Champagne region of France.

facts: Champagne vinegar is traditionally made from wine from the Champagne region of France.
Wine vinegar forms when bacteria turn the alcohol in wine into acetic acid.
champagne-vinegar.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of pale golden vinegar, the glass catching light
champagne-vinegar.what: A pale, mild vinegar made from wine, for light dressings.

facts: Chana dal is a split, hulled form of chickpea widely used across India.
Chana dal is also roasted and eaten as a crunchy snack.
chana-dal.visual: a small heap of pale yellow split chickpeas, smooth and dry
chana-dal.what: Split, hulled chickpeas that stay firm when simmered.

facts: Chana masala is a North Indian dish of chickpeas cooked in a spiced tomato and onion sauce.
In Hindi, chana means chickpea, and masala means a blend of ground spices.
Chana masala is popular across India and Pakistan and is often served with bread.
chana-masala-paste.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, dark orange-brown spice paste
chana-masala-paste.what: A tangy spice paste for chickpea curry.

facts: Short, broad carrots like this were developed for heavy soils, where long roots struggle to grow.
Chantenay is an old French carrot type, still grown for its short, sturdy roots.
Carrots were once grown for their leaves and seeds as well as their roots.
chantenay-carrot.visual: a small bunch of short, blunt, deep orange carrots, green leafy tops still attached, on the plain background
chantenay-carrot.what: A short, stubby orange carrot with a deep, sweet flavour.

facts: Chanterelles are wild mushrooms that grow in woodland, partnering with the roots of trees.
In France they are called girolles, and they are prized in French cooking.
Preserving them in brine lets the mushrooms be kept for use long after the wild season.
chanterelle-mushrooms-in-brine.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of drained golden chanterelle mushrooms, glossy with brine
chanterelle-mushrooms-in-brine.what: Golden wild mushrooms preserved in salty brine.

facts: Chaource is named after the village of Chaource in the Aube department of north-eastern France.
It is a cow's milk cheese, ripened for a few weeks until the white rind forms.
chaource.visual: a round of soft white-rinded cheese, one wedge cut away to show a creamy pale centre
chaource.what: A soft, creamy Champagne cheese with a white rind.

facts: Chapati is made from wholemeal flour and water, rolled thin and cooked on a dry griddle.
It is a daily staple across the Indian subcontinent and East Africa.
chapati.visual: one thin round chapati flatbread, pale wholemeal colour with light brown toasted spots, lying flat
chapati.what: A thin, unleavened wholemeal flatbread from India.

facts: Char siu means fork-roasted in Cantonese, a name for meat cooked on long skewers or forks.
Its sticky texture comes from sugar and sweet syrups, and it is brushed on during roasting.
Char siu is a staple of Cantonese barbecue shops, where roast pork hangs in the window.
char-siu-sauce.visual: a small plain glass bowl holding a thick, glossy, deep red-brown sauce
char-siu-sauce.what: A sweet, sticky red Cantonese glaze for barbecued pork.

facts: Chard is a type of beet grown for its leaves rather than its root.
It has been eaten around the Mediterranean since ancient times.
The stems can be cooked separately, as they take longer to soften than the leaves.
chard.visual: a bunch of fresh chard, broad dark green leaves on bright red stems, tied loosely at the base
chard.what: Leafy green with bright coloured stems, earthy and mild.

facts: Chardonnay is a green-skinned white grape that originated in the Burgundy region of France.

chicken-wing-tips.visual: a small heap of raw chicken wing tips, pale pink skin, small bones showing, lying loose
chicken-wing-tips.what: The bony end of a chicken wing, often used for stock.

chicken-winglets.visual: a small heap of raw chicken winglets, pale pink skin on, lying loosely together
chicken-winglets.what: The meaty middle joint of a chicken wing, cut separately.

facts: Buffalo wings, deep-fried and tossed in hot sauce, are a popular American dish.
A wing has three sections: the drumette, the flat and the tip.
chicken-wings.visual: a small heap of raw chicken wings, pale skin, joints intact, piled loosely
chicken-wings.what: The wing of a chicken, with more skin and bone than meat.

facts: Chickpeas were domesticated in the Middle East and have been grown there for thousands of years.

chickpea-flour.visual: a small plain white bowl of fine, pale yellow chickpea flour
chickpea-flour.what: A pale, nutty flour milled from dried chickpeas.

chickpea-pasta.visual: a small heap of uncooked chickpea pasta shapes, pale beige and dry, loosely scattered and lying flat
chickpea-pasta.what: Firm, nutty pasta made from ground chickpeas.

Hummus, a paste made from cooked chickpeas, comes from the Levant.
Chickpeas are sold dried, where they must be soaked before cooking, or tinned ready to use.

facts: Chickweed is a low-growing annual plant that spreads across gardens and fields.

chickweed.visual: a small bunch of fresh, bright green chickweed sprigs, fine stems and tiny leaves
chickweed.what: A wild green plant with tender, mild leaves for salads.

chicory-coffee.visual: a clear drinking glass filled with dark brown, opaque hot drink
chicory-coffee.what: A drink brewed from roasted chicory root, bitter and nutty.

facts: Chikuwa is a Japanese kamaboko, a fish paste product made from pureed white fish.

chikuwa.visual: a whole chikuwa, a hollow pale fish-paste tube with golden grilled edges, lying on its side

chilled-pastry-block.visual: one rectangular block of pale cream shortcrust pastry, plain and unwrapped, with a smooth matte surface

facts: Chilli con carne is a dish associated with Texas and the southern United States.

chilli-con-carne-seasoning.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine reddish-brown seasoning powder, loose and slightly textured
chilli-con-carne-seasoning.what: A ready-mixed spice blend for a quick beef chilli.

facts: The crunchy pieces are fried in oil until golden and are then stirred back into the chilli oil.
Chilli crisp has become widely sold outside China in recent years, usually in glass jars.
chilli-crisp-oil.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, full of glossy red oil and crunchy flakes of fried garlic and shallot
chilli-crisp-oil.what: A chilli oil packed with crunchy fried garlic and shallot.

facts: Chilli flakes are usually made from dried red chillies crushed with their seeds.
Chillies come from the Americas and spread to Europe and Asia after the late fifteenth century.
chilli-flakes.visual: a small heap of dried red chilli flakes with visible seeds, loosely piled on a plain background
chilli-flakes.what: Dried red chilli crushed into small, hot flakes.

Chillies originated in the Americas and reached Asia through Portuguese and Spanish trade routes.
Garlic softens and its flavour mellows as it is fried or simmered in a sauce.
chilli-garlic-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, chunky deep red sauce, glossy and speckled
chilli-garlic-sauce.what: A thick, chunky red sauce with a spicy kick.

facts: Chilli jam is a sweet preserve made from chillies, sugar and vinegar.
Chillies are native to the Americas and were spread around the world by traders.
chilli-jam.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with glossy, deep red chilli jam
chilli-jam.what: A sticky, sweet jam with a gentle chilli heat.

facts: Chilli oil is a staple condiment in Sichuan and other regions of China, often made by pouring hot oil over chillies.

chilli-oil.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with bright red oil and dark flecks of chilli
chilli-oil.what: Spicy oil infused with dried chillies, used as a condiment.

facts: Chilli peppers originated in the Americas and spread widely after contact with Europe.
Chilli con carne is a dish associated with Texas that uses chilli powder as its key seasoning.
chilli-powder.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine, brick-red chilli powder
chilli-powder.what: A mixed ground chilli spice, often with cumin and garlic.

facts: Chimichurri is a sauce from Argentina and Uruguay, traditionally served with grilled beef.

chimichurri.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of finely chopped bright green herb sauce, loose and glossy
chimichurri.what: A green Argentine sauce of herbs, garlic and vinegar.

facts: Chinese artichoke, or crosne, was named after the French village of Crosne, near Paris.

chinese-artichoke.visual: a small heap of pale, knobbly Chinese artichoke tubers, looking like tiny twisted pearls
chinese-artichoke.what: Small, crunchy tubers that belong to the mint family.

facts: Chinese celery is a leafy, strongly flavoured relative of the common celery.

chinese-celery.visual: a small bunch of thin pale-green Chinese celery stalks with feathery leaves, tied at the base
chinese-celery.what: Thin, pungent stalks used in Chinese stir-fries.

chinese-five-spice.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl heaped with reddish-brown five spice powder
chinese-five-spice.what: A warm, sweet-savoury spice blend used in Chinese cooking.

Five-spice marinades are widely used in Cantonese cooking for roast meats such as pork and duck.
chinese-five-spice-marinade.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with dark brown, glossy marinade
chinese-five-spice-marinade.what: A dark, sweet-spiced marinade for roast pork.

facts: It is made from ground mustard seed mixed with water, which lets its sharp heat develop.
Its heat comes from compounds released when mustard seed is crushed and wetted.
chinese-hot-mustard.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth pale yellow mustard paste
chinese-hot-mustard.what: A fiery yellow mustard paste served with spring rolls.

chinese-pancake.visual: a stack of thin, round, pale cream steamed pancakes on a small plain white plate
chinese-pancake.what: A thin, soft, steamed wheat pancake for wrapping food.

facts: Nagaimo is the Japanese name for the yam, and it is often grated raw over rice as tororo.

chinese-yam.visual: one whole long Chinese yam with rough, brownish skin, lying flat on the background
chinese-yam.what: A slippery, starchy mountain yam from East Asia.

facts: Chinook salmon is native to the North Pacific and to rivers of western North America.

chinook-salmon.visual: a fresh raw chinook salmon fillet, deep orange-pink flesh with pale fat lines, skin on
chinook-salmon.what: A large Pacific salmon with rich, oily, silky flesh.

facts: Chioggia beetroot is named after the fishing town of Chioggia, near Venice in north-eastern Italy.

chioggia-beetroot.visual: a halved raw Chioggia beetroot, cut side up, showing concentric pink and white rings, lying flat
chioggia-beetroot.what: A round beetroot with pink and white rings inside.

facts: British chip shops traditionally sprinkle salt on hot chips straight after frying.

chip-shop-salt.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with fine white salt
chip-shop-salt.what: Fine salt, sprinkled over fish and chips to season them.

facts: The name is thought to come from the Italian word cipolla, meaning onion.
chipolata.visual: a pair of raw chipolata sausages, thin pale pink links, lying side by side
chipolata.what: A small, thin pork sausage, often wrapped in bacon.

facts: Chipotle is a smoked, dried ripe jalapeno, and the name comes from a Nahuatl word for smoked chilli.

chipotle-chilli.visual: a small heap of dried, wrinkled, dark brown chipotle chillies lying loose on the background
chipotle-chilli.what: A smoke-dried jalapeno chilli with a deep, smoky heat.

chipotle-hot-sauce.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of thick, dark red-brown hot sauce, standing upright
chipotle-hot-sauce.what: A smoky hot sauce made from smoked jalapeño chillies.

facts: Mayonnaise is an emulsion of oil and egg yolk, thickened by whisking them together.
Chipotles are smoked, dried red jalapeño chillies, traditionally from Mexico.
chipotle-mayonnaise.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, creamy, pale orange-brown spread
chipotle-mayonnaise.what: Creamy mayonnaise with smoky, spicy chipotle chilli.

chipotle-powder.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine, dark reddish-brown smoked chilli powder
chipotle-powder.what: Smoked, dried jalapeño chillies ground into a fine powder.

The word chipotle comes from the Nahuatl word chilpoctli, meaning smoked chilli.

chipotles-in-adobo.what: Smoked red jalapeños, packed in a tangy, spiced sauce.

facts: Chistorra is a fast-cured sausage from the Basque Country and Navarre in northern Spain.

chistorra.what: A thin Basque pork sausage that cooks in minutes.

facts: Chive flowers are edible and come from the same plant as the green chive leaves.

chive-flowers.what: Small purple flowers from chives, with a mild onion taste.

facts: Chocolate buttons are made by pouring melted chocolate into small round moulds and letting it set.

chocolate-buttons.visual: a small heap of glossy dark brown round chocolate buttons, loosely piled together
chocolate-buttons.what: Small, round drops of chocolate, easy to melt or scatter.

facts: Breakfast cereals were developed in the late nineteenth century, mainly in the United States.
chocolate-cereal.visual: a small heap of brown chocolate cereal loops, glossy and ring-shaped
chocolate-cereal.what: Crunchy cocoa-flavoured cereal loops for breakfast.

chocolate-chips.visual: a small heap of dark chocolate chips, glossy and rounded
chocolate-chips.what: Small chocolate pieces that keep their shape when baked.

Chocolate-coated beans are eaten as a snack and used to decorate cakes and desserts.
chocolate-coated-coffee-beans.visual: a small heap of glossy dark brown chocolate-coated coffee beans, lying loose
chocolate-coated-coffee-beans.what: Crunchy roasted coffee beans coated in dark chocolate.

chocolate-digestives.visual: one round biscuit, its top face smooth and coated in brown chocolate, lying flat on a plain background
chocolate-digestives.what: Crisp, slightly sweet biscuits coated in chocolate.

chocolate-fudge-icing.what: A thick, sweet chocolate frosting for spreading on cakes.

chocolate-ganache.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, glossy dark chocolate ganache
chocolate-ganache.what: Melted chocolate and cream, used as a filling or glaze.

facts: Gianduja, a chocolate and hazelnut paste from Turin in northern Italy, is its ancestor.

chocolate-hazelnut-spread.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, lid off, holding smooth dark brown spread
chocolate-hazelnut-spread.what: A sweet spread of chocolate and ground hazelnuts.

facts: Cocoa comes from cacao beans, the seeds of the Theobroma cacao tree.

chocolate-ice-cream.visual: a round scoop of dark chocolate ice cream in a small plain white bowl
chocolate-ice-cream.what: A frozen dessert of cream, sugar and cocoa.

facts: Peppermint is a hybrid of watermint and spearmint, and chocolate mint is one of its varieties.

chocolate-mint.what: A mint with a chocolatey smell, used in sweet dishes.

facts: Moulded chocolate bars became popular in Britain in the nineteenth century.

Chocolate is made from cacao beans, which grow in pods on tropical trees.
chocolate-orange.visual: a round milk chocolate orange divided into segments, one segment broken off and lying beside it
chocolate-orange.what: Milk chocolate flavoured with orange oil, sold in segments.

facts: Puffed rice cakes are made by heating rice under pressure in a machine, which makes the grains puff.

chocolate-rice-cakes.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of round puffed rice cakes, each coated in smooth dark chocolate
chocolate-rice-cakes.what: Crisp puffed rice discs with a coating of chocolate.

facts: Chocolate sauce is poured warm or cold over ice cream, pancakes and sponge puddings.
Cocoa beans are the source of chocolate; they grow in pods on trees native to tropical America.

chocolate-sauce.what: A smooth, pourable sauce made from cocoa, sugar and cream.

facts: Chocolate is made from the seeds of the cacao tree, which grows in hot, humid tropical regions.

Shavings are made by drawing a vegetable peeler along the edge of a block of chocolate.
chocolate-shavings.visual: a small heap of fine dark chocolate shavings, thin curls and flakes, glossy brown
chocolate-shavings.what: Thin curls of chocolate for finishing cakes and desserts.

facts: Sprinkles are small pieces of sugar or chocolate used to decorate cakes, biscuits and ice cream.

chocolate-sprinkles.what: Tiny strands or specks of chocolate used as a decoration.

facts: Chocolate syrup is made by dissolving sugar and cocoa in water, often with thickeners and flavourings.

chocolate-syrup.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle filled with dark brown glossy chocolate syrup
chocolate-syrup.what: A pourable, sweet cocoa syrup for milk and desserts.

facts: Vermicelli means little worms in Italian, and the name is also used for thin pastas.

chocolate-vermicelli.what: Fine chocolate strands for decorating cakes and desserts.

facts: Hazelnuts grow on hazel shrubs, a plant group known as Corylus.

chopped-hazelnuts.visual: a small heap of chopped brown hazelnut pieces, irregular in size, with a little skin visible

facts: Spanish chorizo gets its colour and smoky taste from paprika, made from dried peppers that are smoked.

chorizo-picante.what: A dry Spanish sausage, hot with paprika.

facts: Choux is made by cooking water, butter and flour together before beating in eggs.

choux-paste.what: A soft, eggy pastry dough that puffs up when baked.

facts: Choux is made by cooking flour, water and butter together, then beating in eggs.
Steam trapped inside the dough as it bakes is what makes the pastry hollow.
choux-pastry.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of soft, smooth, pale choux pastry dough
choux-pastry.what: A light, hollow pastry that puffs up in the oven.

facts: Chow mein is a dish of stir-fried noodles, and its name means fried noodles in Chinese.
Crispy chow mein, where the noodles are fried until golden, became popular in Chinese-American restaurants.

chow-mein-noodles.what: Springy egg noodles that crisp up in a hot wok.

facts: Choy sum is a Chinese brassica grown for its stalks, leaves and edible yellow flowers.

choy-sum.what: Chinese greens with tender stalks and small yellow flowers.

facts: British Christmas cakes are soaked in dried fruit, often in brandy or sherry, before baking.

christmas-cake.visual: one whole round dark fruit cake under smooth white icing, on a plain white plate
christmas-cake.what: A dense, dark fruit cake traditionally eaten at Christmas.

facts: Plum pudding was an old name for dried fruit puddings, where plum meant raisins and prunes.

christmas-pudding.visual: a round dark steamed Christmas pudding, glossy brown and dense, on a plain white plate
christmas-pudding.what: A dark, rich steamed fruit pudding eaten at Christmas.

facts: Chuck comes from the shoulder of the cow, a hard-working muscle with plenty of connective tissue.

chuck-steak.what: A flavourful shoulder cut that suits slow cooking.

facts: Salsa is the Spanish word for sauce, and salsas are central to Mexican cooking.

chunky-salsa.what: A chunky, tangy sauce of chopped tomatoes and chillies.

facts: Ciabatta was developed in northern Italy in the late twentieth century as an alternative to the baguette.

ciabatta.what: A flat Italian loaf with an open crumb and a crisp crust.

facts: Ciabatta is a relatively modern Italian bread, first made in the 1980s.
Its name means slipper in Italian, a reference to its flat shape.

facts: Cider is made by fermenting the juice of apples, and it has been drunk in England for centuries.

cider-apple.what: A bitter, tannic apple, grown mostly to press into cider.

facts: Cider vinegar is made by fermenting apple juice into alcohol, then into acetic acid.

cider-vinegar.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of pale golden cider vinegar, cloudy and amber-tinted
cider-vinegar.what: A fruity, tangy vinegar made from fermented apple cider.

facts: Honeycomb toffee is made by stirring bicarbonate of soda into hot sugar syrup, which makes it foam.

cinder-toffee.what: Crunchy, airy toffee that shatters when bitten.

facts: Cinnamon hearts are hard, sugar-coated sweets that get their flavour from cinnamon.

cinnamon-hearts.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of small red heart-shaped sweets with a glossy sugar coating
cinnamon-hearts.what: Small heart-shaped sweets with a fiery cinnamon flavour.

facts: The filling is usually butter, sugar and ground cinnamon spread over a rolled sheet of dough.

cinnamon-roll.visual: a single cinnamon roll seen from above, a tight spiral of golden bun with a glossy glaze on a plain white plate
cinnamon-roll.what: A swirled, sticky bun flavoured with cinnamon and sugar.

facts: Cinnamon comes from the inner bark of trees in the genus Cinnamomum, peeled and dried as it curls.

cinnamon-sticks.visual: a small loose bundle of rolled cinnamon bark sticks, cut ends visible, a warm reddish-brown colour
cinnamon-sticks.what: Fragrant bark, dried and rolled into quills for simmering.

facts: Cinnamon rolls are sweet yeasted dough, rolled around a filling of cinnamon and sugar.

Swedish cinnamon buns, known as kanelbullar, are a traditional fika treat.
cinnamon-swirl.visual: a spiral cinnamon roll, golden brown, one cut end showing the spiral, on a plain white plate
cinnamon-swirl.what: Soft sweet dough rolled with cinnamon sugar and sliced.

facts: Cipollini takes its name from the Italian word for onion, cipolla, with a diminutive ending.
Cipollini onions are widely grown in Italy and are often braised whole.
cipollini-onion.visual: one whole raw cipollini onion, flat round shape, papery pale copper-brown skin, lying on its side
cipollini-onion.what: A small, flat Italian onion with a mild, sweet taste.

facts: Citric acid was first isolated from lemon juice by the chemist Carl Wilhelm Scheele in 1784.
It occurs naturally in citrus fruits, and today it is mostly made by fermenting sugar with a mould.
It sharpens flavour in sweets, drinks and jams, and helps to preserve food.
citric-acid.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine white crystalline powder
citric-acid.what: A sharp, sour white powder used for preserving and sweets.

facts: Citron is one of the ancestral citrus fruits, and lemons are thought to have developed from it.
Candied citron peel is a traditional ingredient in Italian panettone and in British fruitcake.
Citron has been grown in the Mediterranean since ancient times.
citron.visual: one whole citron with a bumpy, yellow-green skin and an oblong shape
citron.what: A large, bumpy citrus with thick pith and fragrant peel.

facts: Citron is one of the original citrus species from which many modern citrus fruits descend.
Candied citron peel is a traditional ingredient in Italian panettone and British fruitcake.
citron-peel.visual: a small heap of translucent candied citron peel strips, pale green-yellow and lightly sugared
citron-peel.what: Candied rind of the citron, a large, knobbly citrus.

facts: Clams are bivalve molluscs, meaning each shell has two halves joined by a hinge.
Clams are a feature of many coastal cuisines, including the Italian pasta dish spaghetti vongole.
In New England, clam chowder is a famous soup made with clams, potatoes and cream.
clams.visual: one whole raw clam in its grey-brown hinged shell, closed, lying directly on the background
clams.what: A shellfish with a hinged shell and sweet meat.

facts: Clarified butter is made by gently heating butter and skimming off the milk solids and water.
Indian cooking uses a closely related product called ghee, which is cooked for longer and has a nuttier flavour.
clarified-butter.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of pale golden clarified butter, smooth and glossy
clarified-butter.what: Butter with the milk solids removed, so it fries hot.

facts: A clementine is a cross between a mandarin and a sweet orange, and it peels easily by hand.
Clementines are mostly sold in the winter months, especially around Christmas.
Many varieties are seedless or nearly seedless, which makes them popular for lunchboxes.
clementine.visual: one whole bright orange clementine, its skin lightly dimpled and glossy, lying on its side
clementine.what: A small, easy-peel citrus with sweet, seedless flesh.

facts: Clotted cream is made by heating full-fat milk slowly so the cream thickens and forms a crust.
It is closely associated with Devon and Cornwall, in south-west England.
A cream tea is a scone served with clotted cream and jam, a tradition of the West Country.
clotted-cream.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick ivory-yellow clotted cream, topped by a slightly golden crust
clotted-cream.what: Thick, spreadable Cornish cream, often eaten with scones.

facts: Cloudberries grow on cold northern bogs and tundra in Scandinavia, Finland and Canada.
In Scandinavia, cloudberries are often served with cream, or made into jam.
In Swedish they are called hjortron, and in Finnish they are called lakka.
cloudberry.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of ripe amber-orange cloudberries
cloudberry.what: A tart amber-gold Nordic berry that grows in cold bogs.

facts: Cloudberries grow in Arctic and sub-Arctic bogs across Scandinavia and northern Russia.
In Finland and Sweden, cloudberries are a prized seasonal fruit.
The berries turn a golden-orange colour when ripe and are often made into jam.
cloudberry-jam.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with amber-orange cloudberry jam, on a plain background
cloudberry-jam.what: A tangy, honeyed jam made from Arctic cloudberries.

facts: Polenta is made from ground maize, a crop brought to Europe from the Americas.
Polenta is a traditional dish in northern Italy, often served soft or cooled and sliced.
Italian polenta can be grilled or fried once it has set.
coarse-polenta.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of dry, coarse yellow cornmeal
coarse-polenta.what: Golden, coarse cornmeal that cooks into a creamy porridge.

facts: In much of England, a cob is a round bread roll or small loaf.
Kneading develops gluten in bread dough, which gives a cob its stretch and chewy structure.
Cobs are usually shaped by rolling the dough into a smooth ball before proving and baking.
cob-loaf.visual: one whole round cob loaf with a golden crust, lying on a plain background
cob-loaf.what: A round, crusty loaf with a chewy crust and soft crumb.

facts: Cobia is found in warm waters around the world and is also called ling or black kingfish.
Cobia is farmed in several countries in Asia, and it is also caught wild in tropical seas.
Its firm flesh suits grilling and searing, and it holds together well when cooked.
cobia.visual: a skinless fillet of firm, pale pinkish-white raw fish lying flat
cobia.what: A large sea fish with firm, buttery, pale flesh.

facts: Cockles live buried in sand and mud on tidal shores and are dug up at low tide.
In Britain they are traditionally boiled and sold at the seaside, often served with vinegar.
Cockles are bivalves, so they are related to mussels, clams and scallops.
cockles.visual: a small heap of raw cockles in their ridged, creamy-grey shells
cockles.what: Small shellfish with a ridged shell and sweet flesh.

facts: Prawn cocktail, a retro starter, was widely served in Britain in the mid-twentieth century.
Marie Rose is another name for the sauce, especially in Britain.
Mayonnaise is an emulsion of oil, egg yolk and vinegar or lemon juice.
cocktail-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, thick pale pink sauce
cocktail-sauce.what: A pink, tangy dip made from ketchup and mayonnaise.

facts: Cocoa nibs are the inside of the cocoa bean, separated from the shell after roasting.
Nibs can be stirred into cakes, sprinkled on porridge or added to granola for crunch.
cocoa-nibs.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of dark brown cocoa nibs, crunchy and irregular in shape
cocoa-nibs.what: Crunchy bits of roasted cocoa bean, bitter and intense.

facts: Cocoa beans grow in pods on Theobroma cacao trees, which are native to the Americas.
Cocoa powder is made by pressing out most of the cocoa butter, then grinding the solids.
Dutch processing treats the powder with an alkali, which makes it darker and milder.
cocoa-powder.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine, dark reddish-brown cocoa powder with a smooth surface
cocoa-powder.what: A dry, bitter powder made from roasted, pressed cocoa beans.

facts: Coconut aminos are made from coconut palm sap mixed with sea salt.
Coconut palms are grown across tropical regions of Asia, Africa and the Pacific.
It is often used as a soy sauce alternative in cooking.
coconut-aminos.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle filled with dark amber liquid
coconut-aminos.what: A sweet, mild liquid seasoning made from coconut sap.

facts: It is a traditional partner for dosa, a fermented rice and lentil pancake from South India.
Coconut is central to cooking along the southern coasts of India and in Sri Lanka.
coconut-chutney.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of pale off-white coconut chutney, smooth and creamy
coconut-chutney.what: A cool, fresh South Indian chutney, served with dosa.

facts: Coconut cream is the thickest part of coconut milk, which rises to the top when it is left to stand.
Coconut is widely used in South and Southeast Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, in curries and desserts.
coconut-cream.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, creamy white coconut cream
coconut-cream.what: Thick, rich cream made from the top of coconut milk.

facts: Coconut extract is a concentrated flavouring, used in small amounts because its taste is strong.
Coconuts are the fruit of the coconut palm, which grows in tropical coastal areas.
Coconut flavours are common in desserts from the Caribbean, the Philippines and South-East Asia.
coconut-extract.visual: a small plain unlabelled glass bottle of pale golden liquid
coconut-extract.what: A concentrated coconut flavouring for baking and desserts.

facts: Coconut is the fruit of the coconut palm, a tree that grows along tropical coasts around the world.
Flakes are made by drying and shredding the white flesh of the mature nut.
Shredded coconut is common in baking, cakes, biscuits and sweets in many countries.
coconut-flakes.visual: a small heap of dry, pale ivory coconut flakes, thin and curled, loose on the background
coconut-flakes.what: Dried coconut shreds, sweet and crisp when toasted.

facts: Coconut palms grow along tropical coasts, and coconut features in many tropical cuisines.
Coconut flour is very absorbent, so recipes often need more liquid than wheat flour.
coconut-flour.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine, soft, pale cream coconut flour
coconut-flour.what: A fine, soft flour made from dried, ground coconut flesh.

facts: Coconut milk is made by soaking grated coconut flesh in warm water and squeezing out the liquid.
It is a staple in curries across Southeast Asia, South Asia and parts of the Pacific.
coconut-milk.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, creamy white coconut milk
coconut-milk.what: A rich, creamy liquid pressed from grated coconut flesh.

facts: Coconut blossom sap is collected by cutting the flower stalk of the coconut palm, mainly in Southeast Asia.
The sap is gently heated to evaporate its water, which thickens it into a syrup.
Palm sugar is made in a similar way across much of South and Southeast Asia.
coconut-nectar.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle filled with pale amber syrup
coconut-nectar.what: A thin, caramel-like syrup made from coconut blossom sap.

facts: Coconut oil is extracted from coconut flesh, either from dried copra or from fresh coconut.
It stays solid at cool room temperature and melts quickly in a warm pan.
Coconut oil has long been used in cooking across South Asia and the Pacific islands.
coconut-oil.visual: a small plain glass jar without a label, filled with solid white coconut oil, creamy and opaque
