pot-barley.what: Barley with only its husk removed, so it stays chewy.

facts: Dal is a staple across South Asia, usually made from split pulses such as lentils.
The name comes from a word meaning split, referring to the split pulses it is made from.
pot-ready-dal.visual: a small plain white bowl of thick, golden-yellow spiced dal, smooth and glossy
pot-ready-dal.what: Spiced lentils simmered into a thick, comforting stew.

facts: Potato bread uses cooked potato in the dough, which helps it stay soft for longer.
Potato rolls are common in the United States, where they are often used for burgers.
Potatoes were first domesticated in the Andes of South America thousands of years ago.
potato-bun.visual: one whole round potato bun with a soft pale golden top, lying on its base
potato-bun.what: A soft, slightly sweet bread roll made with potato.

facts: Croquette comes from the French word croquer, meaning to crunch, and describes a crisp-coated fried food.
Shaped croquettes are often coated in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs before frying.
potato-croquettes.visual: a few golden-brown oval potato croquettes, crisp and evenly coated, served on a plain white plate
potato-croquettes.what: Mashed potato, shaped, breadcrumbed and fried until crisp.

facts: Potato farls are a staple of Northern Irish breakfasts, often fried alongside bacon and eggs.
Potatoes are mashed with flour and butter, then rolled into a round and cooked on a griddle.
potato-farl.visual: one flat round potato farl with golden-brown griddle marks, served plainly on a plain white plate
potato-farl.what: A thin, griddled potato cake, cut into quarters and fried.

facts: Potato gems are small cylinders made from grated potato, shaped into neat, uniform pieces.
Frying grated potato gives a crisp outside, because the thin shreds have a large surface area.
Grated potato is also the base of Swiss rösti and Jewish latkes, both pan-fried until crisp.
potato-gems.visual: a few golden, crisp cylindrical potato gems arranged on a small plain white plate
potato-gems.what: Small crispy tubes of grated potato, fried until golden.

facts: Shaped potato products like these are usually sold frozen and cooked in the oven or fryer.
Potatoes were first grown in the Andes of South America and reached Europe in the 16th century.
The word potato comes from the Spanish patata, which came from the Taino word batata.
potato-smiles.visual: a small heap of pale golden potato smile shapes, crimped edges, lying loose on the background
potato-smiles.what: Shaped potato bites with smiley faces, a fun side dish.

facts: It is made by washing grated potatoes so the starch settles out and the pulp is removed.
Potato starch is often used to give fried and baked coatings a light, crisp texture.
potato-starch.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine, bright white potato starch powder
potato-starch.what: A fine white starch from potatoes, used to thicken sauces.

facts: Potato waffles are sold frozen and are usually baked, grilled or fried until crisp.
Mashed potato has been pressed into shaped cakes and patties in many cuisines around the world.
potato-waffles.visual: one golden-brown potato waffle, ridged grid surface, lying flat on a plain white plate
potato-waffles.what: Mashed potato pressed into a grid shape and crisped.

facts: Poultry seasoning is an American-style herb blend, and sage is usually its leading herb.
Blends typically also include thyme, marjoram and black pepper, though recipes vary.
It is traditionally used to flavour bread stuffing for roast chicken and turkey.
poultry-seasoning.visual: a plain glass jar without a label holding a coarse, grey-green dried herb mix
poultry-seasoning.what: A dried herb mix, led by sage, used for stuffing.

facts: A poussin is a young chicken, slaughtered when it is very small.
The word poussin is French and means a young chick or chicken.
Splitting and flattening the bird, a method called spatchcocking, is a common way to grill poussin.
poussin.visual: one whole raw poussin, a small plump young chicken with pale skin, lying on its side
poussin.what: A young chicken, often one per person, with tender meat.

facts: Pouting is a small member of the cod family, found in the north-east Atlantic and nearby seas.
Pouting is a common catch for anglers along British coasts.
pouting.visual: one whole raw pouting fish, slim and silvery, lying on its side
pouting.what: A small, sweet white fish from the cod family.

facts: Gelatine is made by slowly simmering animal skin and bones, which releases their natural collagen.
It melts in warm liquid and sets as it cools, which is why it suits jellies and mousses.
Panna cotta, a cooked Italian cream dessert, is one of its best-known uses in European kitchens.
powdered-gelatine.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine, pale golden gelatine powder
powdered-gelatine.what: A powder that sets liquids into a wobbly, firm jelly.

facts: Milk powder is made by evaporating water from fresh milk, then drying it to a fine powder.
Powdered milk was used on long sea voyages and in military campaigns because it kept well.
Bakers add it to bread and dough to give a softer crumb and richer flavour.
powdered-milk.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine off-white milk powder
powdered-milk.what: Dried milk ground to powder that stores for a long time.

facts: In France, praline is a sweet of nuts cooked in caramel, while in Belgium the word usually means filled chocolates.
Crushed praline is often used to flavour ice creams, cakes and pastries.
praline.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of crushed praline, glossy brown caramel-coated nut pieces
praline.what: A crunchy sweet made from caramelised nuts.

facts: In France, praline means nuts cooked in caramelised sugar, and in Belgium it often means filled chocolates.
Hazelnut praline is a traditional filling for chocolates and pastries.
praline-paste.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with smooth golden-brown hazelnut paste
praline-paste.what: A smooth paste of caramelised hazelnuts and sugar.

facts: Pralines are a sweet made from sugar and nuts, and are popular in New Orleans.
In France, praline refers to a sugar-coated nut mixture used to flavour cakes and chocolates.
pralines.visual: a small heap of golden-brown caramelised nut pieces, glossy and brittle, lying loose
pralines.what: Brittle caramelised nut pieces, crushed for topping.

facts: The flavour copies the classic British prawn cocktail, a starter of prawns in a pink, tangy sauce.
The pink colour comes from the seasoning, which is dusted onto the crisps as they are made.
Flavoured crisps are a long-standing part of British snacking, with many styles based on savoury dishes.
prawn-cocktail-crisps.visual: a small plain white bowl of pink-dusted potato crisps, loosely piled
prawn-cocktail-crisps.what: Thin crisps with a pink, tangy flavour of seafood sauce.

facts: Prawn crackers are made from a paste of prawns or fish and starch, shaped, dried, then fried.
They puff up in hot oil because moisture in the dried disc turns to steam.
prawn-crackers.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl heaped with dried prawn crackers, pale pinkish discs, crisp and slightly translucent
prawn-crackers.what: Puffy, shrimp-flavoured crackers that swell in hot oil.

facts: In Britain, the word prawn is used for a range of shrimp-like crustaceans, and the names overlap.
Prawns are found in seas worldwide and are farmed in many countries.
Prawns are often grilled, fried or added to curries and noodle dishes.
prawns.visual: a small heap of raw, shell-on prawns, grey-pink and glossy
prawns.what: Small, sweet shellfish that cook in minutes.

facts: Horseradish is a plant of the cabbage family, grown for its pungent root.
Its heat comes from compounds that are released when the root is cut or grated.
In Britain, horseradish is traditionally served with roast beef.
prepared-horseradish.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, lid off, holding creamy pale grated paste
prepared-horseradish.what: Grated horseradish root in vinegar, sharp and pungent.

facts: Preserved lemons are a staple of Moroccan cooking, where they flavour tagines.
Lemons originated in Asia and spread westward through the Middle East.
preserved-lemon.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, holding halved yellow lemons packed in salt
preserved-lemon.what: Lemons cured whole in salt until the peel turns soft.

facts: Preserved lemons are a staple of Moroccan cooking, salted and left to soften in their own juice.
The rind is usually used, since it is where the fragrant oils of the lemon are concentrated.
preserved-lemon-paste.visual: a small plain glass jar without a label holding a smooth pale yellow paste
preserved-lemon-paste.what: A smooth, salty paste of puréed salt-cured lemon rind.

facts: Salting and drying the turnip draws out water and firms its flesh, so it keeps for long periods.
It is used in small amounts because its salty, savoury flavour is strong.
preserved-turnip.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of dark brown, dried preserved turnip pieces, wrinkled and firm
preserved-turnip.what: Salty, crunchy Chinese pickle of dried, salted turnip.

facts: Its large crystals dissolve slowly, and it is widely used for making jam and marmalade.
Sugar was once a costly luxury in Britain, long before it became cheap and widely available.
preserving-sugar.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of coarse white sugar crystals, large and glistening
preserving-sugar.what: Coarse sugar crystals that dissolve slowly, used for jam.

facts: Pretzels have been baked in Europe since at least the Middle Ages.
Pretzel dough is dipped in an alkaline solution before baking, which gives the crust its deep brown colour.
Soft pretzel rolls are popular in Germany and the United States.
pretzel-roll.visual: one whole round pretzel-style bread roll, glossy deep brown crust with coarse salt flakes on top
pretzel-roll.what: A soft, chewy bread roll with the crust of a pretzel.

facts: Pretzels are baked dough shaped into a knot or twist, and coarse salt is a classic topping.
pretzels.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of salted, twisted, golden-brown pretzels
pretzels.what: Crisp, salted baked snacks shaped into twists.

facts: Prickly pear is the fruit of several Opuntia cacti, native to the Americas.
It is now grown widely around the Mediterranean, including Sicily, where it is called fichi d'India.
Its tiny, hair-like spines can lodge in the skin, so the fruit is usually peeled with gloves or tongs.
prickly-pear.visual: one whole deep magenta prickly pear fruit, its skin dotted with small brown tufts
prickly-pear.what: A spiny cactus fruit with sweet, seedy flesh.

facts: Prosciutto di Parma is made in the Parma area of Italy under a protected designation of origin.
The ham is salted and air-dried for months, a slow process that gives it a sweet, delicate flavour.
prosciutto-di-parma.visual: a neat pile of thin pink-red air-dried ham slices with white fat edges, lying flat
prosciutto-di-parma.what: Sweet, air-dried Italian ham, sliced very thin.

facts: San Daniele ham is made in the small town of San Daniele del Friuli, in north-eastern Italy.
Only hams made in the protected area under the Italian and EU designation can carry the name.
The hams are salted and then air-dried over a long period, with the cool local climate helping the process.
prosciutto-di-san-daniele.visual: a plain white ceramic plate holding a neat fanned stack of thin pink slices of air-dried ham, edged with white fat
prosciutto-di-san-daniele.what: A delicately sweet, air-dried ham from Friuli in Italy.

facts: Prosecco is named after a village near Trieste, in north-eastern Italy.
It is mostly made from the glera grape, grown in the Veneto and Friuli regions.
Its fizz is usually made in large steel tanks, a method called the Charmat process.
prosecco.visual: a clear drinking glass of pale golden sparkling wine, small bubbles rising through it
prosecco.what: A light, dry Italian sparkling wine from the Veneto.

facts: Provolone is a stretched-curd cheese first made in southern Italy.
Its name is linked to provola, an old Italian word for a cheese.
provolone.visual: a block of pale golden provolone cheese with one cut face showing a smooth, closed texture, lying flat on a plain background
provolone.what: A firm, smooth Italian cheese, mild or piquant.

facts: Prunes are dried plums, and many are made from the Agen variety grown in south-west France.
The name prune comes from the Latin word prunum, meaning plum.
They are often stewed with Armagnac, or baked into cakes and tarts.
prune.visual: a small heap of dark, wrinkled, glossy dried prunes
prune.what: A dried plum with a dark, soft, sticky flesh.

facts: Freestone plums have flesh that separates easily from the stone.
Prune plums dry well, and the dried fruit is sold as prunes.
Plums of this type have been grown in Europe for centuries and used in baking.
prune-plum.visual: three whole ripe purple-blue plums with a dusty bloom on their skins
prune-plum.what: A sweet, juicy plum whose stone lifts out cleanly.

facts: Psyllium comes from the seeds of Plantago plants, and India is the main producer.
Psyllium husks absorb water and form a gel, which is why they help structure gluten-free dough.
psyllium-husk.visual: a small heap of pale tan psyllium husks in a small plain white ceramic bowl
psyllium-husk.what: Crushed seed husks that bind dough in gluten-free baking.

facts: Pudding rice is a short-grain variety, widely used in British nursery puddings.
Its grains take up milk slowly and release starch that gives the pudding its creamy texture.
Rice pudding is a baked dish of rice, milk and sugar, often flavoured with nutmeg.
pudding-rice.visual: a small heap of raw white pudding rice, short plump grains spilling slightly
pudding-rice.what: A plump short-grain rice that goes soft and creamy.

facts: Puff pastry is made by folding butter into dough again and again to build many thin layers.
When it bakes, the water in the butter turns to steam and lifts the layers apart.
It is widely used in French and British baking, for things like sausage rolls and tarts.
puff-pastry.visual: one rectangular block of chilled pale cream puff pastry, edges showing thin layers, lying flat on the background
puff-pastry.what: Buttery layered dough that bakes into light, flaky sheets.

facts: Puffed rice is made by heating rice grains under pressure until they burst.
Bhel puri, a snack from Mumbai, is built around puffed rice.
puffed-rice.visual: a small heap of crisp, pale puffed rice grains
puffed-rice.what: Light, crisp grains of rice that have been puffed by heat.

facts: Puffed rice is made by heating rice grains under pressure until they burst into crisp puffs.
It is used in breakfast cereals, sweet bars and crisp toppings.
Rice crispy cakes bind puffed rice with melted marshmallow or syrup.
puffed-rice-cereal.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl heaped with crisp, pale puffed rice cereal
puffed-rice-cereal.what: Light, crisp rice puffs, eaten dry or with milk.

facts: Pumpernickel is a traditional rye bread from Westphalia in north-west Germany.
It is made mostly from coarsely ground rye, which gives it a dense, dark crumb.
Traditionally it was baked slowly in a low oven for many hours.
pumpernickel.visual: one slice of dense, dark pumpernickel bread with a close, moist crumb, lying flat on the background
pumpernickel.what: A dense, dark rye bread from Germany, slow-baked for hours.

facts: Pumpkins are a kind of squash, grown in the Americas for a very long time.
In Britain, pumpkins are often carved into lanterns at Halloween.
Pumpkin pie is a traditional dessert in the United States, especially at Thanksgiving.
pumpkin.visual: one whole round orange pumpkin with a short green stem, lying on its side
pumpkin.what: A large orange-skinned squash with sweet, dense flesh.

facts: Gnocchi are small dumplings, most often made from potato, flour and egg.
Pumpkin gnocchi are found in parts of northern Italy, where pumpkin has long been used in pasta.
Sage and brown butter are a traditional pairing for pumpkin dishes in northern Italy.
pumpkin-gnocchi.visual: several pale golden pumpkin gnocchi, soft and plump, on a plain white plate
pumpkin-gnocchi.what: Soft dumplings made from pumpkin and flour.

facts: Ugu, or fluted pumpkin, is a West African vine grown for its leaves and edible seeds.
Ugu leaves are a common ingredient in Nigerian soups and stews.
The leaves are also eaten in other parts of West and Central Africa.
pumpkin-leaves.visual: a small bunch of tender dark green pumpkin leaves with their stems tied together
pumpkin-leaves.what: Tender leaves from pumpkin vines, cooked like spinach.

facts: Pumpkin pie spice is an American blend, used mainly in autumn pumpkin pies and bakes.
Pre-mixed spices save bakers from measuring each spice separately.
Cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg and clove were once traded over long distances along the spice routes.
pumpkin-pie-spice.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine orange-brown spice powder, slightly mounded
pumpkin-pie-spice.what: A warm mix of cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg and clove.

facts: Pumpkin seed oil is a speciality of Styria in south-east Austria, where it is pressed from toasted seeds.
It is usually drizzled over finished dishes such as salads or soups rather than used for high-heat frying.
pumpkin-seed-oil.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle filled with deep dark green oil
pumpkin-seed-oil.what: A dark green oil pressed from toasted pumpkin seeds.

facts: Pumpkin seeds are known as pepitas in Mexico, where they have been eaten for centuries.
Many pumpkin seeds are sold hulled, so the pale green kernel inside can be eaten whole.
pumpkin-seeds.visual: a small heap of raw pale green pumpkin seeds, flat and oval, loose on the background
pumpkin-seeds.what: Flat green seeds from the inside of a pumpkin or squash.

facts: Puntarelle is a variety of chicory grown in and around Rome.
Its shoots are shaved into thin strips and soaked in cold water so they curl.
In Roman cooking, the strips are traditionally dressed with anchovy, garlic and vinegar.
puntarelle.visual: a loose bunch of long, pale green chicory shoots, thin and curled
puntarelle.what: A crisp, bitter Roman chicory with long curled shoots.

facts: Puri is a small, unleavened Indian bread made from wheat flour and deep-fried until it puffs.
It is commonly served with spiced potatoes, especially at festivals and family meals.
Puri is eaten across South Asia, and similar fried breads appear in many regions.
puri.visual: one whole puffed golden puri bread, round and hollow-looking, on a plain white plate
puri.what: A small, puffed, deep-fried Indian bread.

facts: Purple asparagus gets its colour from anthocyanin pigments, the same family that colours red cabbage.
Its violet colour usually fades to green when the spears are cooked.
Purple varieties are grown in parts of Italy and France, where they are a regional speciality.
purple-asparagus.visual: a small bunch of slender spears with deep violet skin, cut ends neatly trimmed
purple-asparagus.what: Slender violet spears that turn green when cooked.

facts: Purple basil is a cultivar of sweet basil, grown for its dark leaves and decorative colour.
purple-basil.visual: a small bunch of purple basil, deep violet-purple leaves on thin green-purple stems
purple-basil.what: A deep-purple herb with a spicy, sweet flavour.

facts: Purple carrots were grown in Afghanistan and the Middle East long before orange carrots became common.
The purple colour comes from natural pigments called anthocyanins, which are also found in red cabbage.
Purple carrots are now grown in many countries and are often used in salads for their bright colour.
purple-carrot.visual: a bunch of purple carrots, their skin deep violet and their green tops still attached
purple-carrot.what: A carrot with purple skin and a sweet, peppery taste.

facts: Purple cauliflower is a variety of the same plant as white cauliflower, bred for its colour.
Its violet colour comes from natural pigments also found in red cabbage.
It is crisp and mild, so it is often roasted or eaten raw in salads.
purple-cauliflower.visual: a whole violet cauliflower head with tightly packed florets
purple-cauliflower.what: A cauliflower with violet florets and a mild, sweet taste.

facts: Purple potatoes get their colour from anthocyanins, pigments also found in red cabbage.
Potatoes were first domesticated in the Andes of South America, thousands of years ago.
purple-majesty-potato.visual: a whole raw potato, oval and smooth, its deep purple skin dusted with a little earth
purple-majesty-potato.what: A purple-skinned potato with deep violet flesh.

facts: Purple sprouting broccoli is a type of Brassica that is harvested in late winter and early spring.
Unlike the common green broccoli head, it produces many small shoots rather than one large head.
Its purple colour comes from anthocyanin pigments, which are also found in red cabbage.
purple-sprouting-broccoli.visual: a loose bunch of purple sprouting broccoli, thin stems and small purple-green florets, on a plain background
purple-sprouting-broccoli.what: A purple-tinged broccoli with thin, tender, sweet spears.

facts: Purple sweet potatoes are often called Okinawan sweet potatoes after the Japanese islands where they are widely grown.
Their violet colour comes from natural pigments called anthocyanins, which also colour red cabbage.
purple-sweet-potato.visual: a whole purple sweet potato with smooth dark violet-purple skin, lying on its side
purple-sweet-potato.what: A sweet, dense tuber with vivid violet flesh.

facts: Purslane grows wild across much of the world and is often regarded as a weed.
It is eaten in Mediterranean, Middle Eastern and Mexican cooking, often in salads.
purslane.visual: a small bunch of purslane, with thick, fleshy, reddish-green leaves and stems
purslane.what: A low-growing succulent weed with thick, lemony leaves.

facts: The name puttanesca is of uncertain origin, and several stories are told about it.
Its strong, salty flavour comes from olives, capers and anchovies cooked into the tomatoes.
puttanesca-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, chunky dark red tomato sauce
puttanesca-sauce.what: A bold Italian tomato sauce with salty olives and capers.

facts: Puy lentils are grown in the Le Puy area of south-central France under a protected designation of origin.
Lentils were domesticated in the Near East thousands of years ago, alongside early wheat and barley.
Unlike many dried pulses, Puy lentils keep their shape and do not turn mushy when cooked.
puy-lentils.visual: a small loose heap of tiny dark slate-green lentils, lying on the background
puy-lentils.what: Small slate-green lentils with a peppery, firm bite.

facts: The name quahog comes from a Native American word for the clam, used in New England.
Quahog shells were used to make wampum beads in New England.
Chowder is a traditional New England dish made with quahogs.
quahog.visual: one whole raw quahog clam, thick grey-brown hard shell, lying on its side on a plain background
quahog.what: A large, hard-shelled clam from the Atlantic coast.

facts: The common quail is a migratory bird, and European populations travel south to Africa in winter.
quail-breast.visual: a single raw quail breast, small and pale pink with the skin on, lying directly on the background
quail-breast.what: The small, lean breast meat of a tiny game bird.

facts: Quail eggs are much smaller than hen's eggs and have a speckled shell.
Quail have been kept for their eggs and meat in many countries for centuries.
They are a popular topping in Japanese cooking and are sometimes pickled.
quail-egg.visual: a small heap of tiny speckled brown and cream quail eggs
quail-egg.what: A tiny speckled egg, often boiled and served whole.

facts: Quark is made from soured milk that is gently heated and drained to form a soft curd.
It is a staple of German and Central European cooking, used in cheesecakes, dips and spreads.
The name is thought to come from a Slavic word for curd.
quark.visual: a smooth soft white mound of quark in a small plain white ceramic bowl
quark.what: A soft, fresh curd cheese with a tangy, creamy taste.

facts: Queen scallops are smaller than king scallops, and are common around the coasts of Britain and Ireland.
Scallops are bivalve molluscs that swim by clapping their shells together.
queen-scallops.visual: A small plain white ceramic bowl of raw queen scallops, pale cream and pinkish, with a moist sheen.
queen-scallops.what: Small, sweet scallops that cook in minutes.

facts: It is made from the milk of sheep grazing in the Serra da Estrela mountains of central Portugal.
Traditional cheesemakers curdle the milk with cardoon thistle flowers instead of animal rennet.
The cheese is often served by cutting off the top and spooning out the soft, runny centre.
queijo-da-serra.visual: a small round wheel of pale yellow sheep's cheese with a natural rind, one wedge cut away
queijo-da-serra.what: A soft Portuguese sheep's cheese, scooped with a spoon.

facts: Queijo fresco means fresh cheese in Portuguese, and it is not aged.
Fresh cheeses like this are made by curdling milk and draining the curds without ageing them.
queijo-fresco.visual: a block of soft white fresh cheese, one wedge cut away and lying flat beside it
queijo-fresco.what: A soft, mild Portuguese fresh cheese made from cow's milk.

facts: Queso is Spanish for cheese, and queso dip is especially popular in Mexico and the American Southwest.
Many versions use melting cheeses such as Monterey Jack, which blend smoothly when warm.
Queso is a staple of Tex-Mex cooking, a cuisine that blends Texan and Mexican traditions.
queso-dip.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, golden-orange melted cheese, glossy and warm
queso-dip.what: Warm, melted cheese dip with a gentle chilli kick.

facts: Queso fresco means fresh cheese in Spanish, and it is often made from cow's milk.
It is made by curdling warm milk, then draining and pressing the curds.
queso-fresco.visual: a block of soft white crumbly cheese, one thick wedge cut away and lying beside it
queso-fresco.what: A mild, crumbly white cheese from Latin America.

facts: The word quiche is thought to come from the German word Kuchen, meaning cake.
Traditional quiche Lorraine has no cheese, only eggs, cream and smoked bacon.
In the 1970s, quiche became a fashionable dish in Britain and America.
quiche-lorraine.visual: one slice of quiche showing pale golden egg custard and bacon pieces inside, served on a small plain white plate
quiche-lorraine.what: A savoury egg custard tart with bacon, cheese and pastry.

facts: Quince is native to the Caucasus and south-west Asia, and has been grown for thousands of years.
Its flesh is too hard and tart to eat raw, so it is usually poached, baked or made into jelly.
Membrillo, a thick quince paste, is a traditional sweet served with cheese in Spain.
quince.visual: one whole yellow fruit, pear-shaped, soft pale fuzz on the golden skin, lying on its side
quince.what: A fragrant yellow fruit that is too hard to eat raw.

facts: Quince is a hard, fragrant fruit related to apples and pears, and it is cooked before eating.
Spain's membrillo is a thick quince paste, often served with cheese.
The word marmalade comes from the Portuguese word marmelo, meaning quince.
quince-jelly.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, holding clear rosy-pink quince jelly
quince-jelly.what: A rosy, tart, clear jelly made from quince fruit.

facts: Quince paste is made by cooking quinces with sugar for a long time until the mixture sets firm.
In Spain it is called membrillo and is traditionally served with Manchego cheese.
Quinces are hard, fragrant autumn fruits that grow on a tree related to apples and pears.
quince-paste.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of firm ruby-orange quince paste, smooth-surfaced
quince-paste.what: A firm, sliceable paste of sweet, cooked quince.

facts: Quinoa was first grown in the Andes, where it has been eaten for thousands of years.
Its name comes from kinwa, the Quechua word for the plant.
quinoa.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of uncooked white quinoa seeds, loose and dry
quinoa.what: Tiny, fast-cooking seeds that behave like a grain.

facts: Rabbits were domesticated in medieval Europe, initially for meat and fur.
Mustard and cider are classic partners for braising rabbit in French and English cooking.
rabbit.visual: a raw rabbit cut into joints, pale pink meat lying flat on the background
rabbit.what: A lean, delicate meat from a small farmed or wild mammal.

facts: Rabbit has been eaten in Europe for centuries, and it is a traditional dish in France and Italy.
Rabbit legs suit slow cooking, since the meat becomes tender when braised in liquid.
Domestic rabbits descend from the European wild rabbit, which was kept in enclosures for centuries.
rabbit-legs.visual: two raw rabbit hind legs, pale pink meat on the bone, lying side by side
rabbit-legs.what: Delicate, sweet meat from the back legs of a rabbit.

facts: The European rabbit is native to south-west Europe and north-west Africa, and has been farmed for food since medieval times.
rabbit-saddle.visual: one whole raw rabbit saddle, pink meat, two long fillets joined along the spine, lying flat
rabbit-saddle.what: The tender back cut of a rabbit, running along the spine.

facts: In French cooking a rack of lamb is called a carre d'agneau.
Lamb has been raised for meat across Britain and the Mediterranean for many centuries.
Racks are often roasted whole and then cut between the bones into cutlets.
rack-of-lamb.visual: a raw rack of lamb, a neat row of rib bones with bright pink meat and a thin fat cap
rack-of-lamb.what: A row of lamb ribs, cut from the best end of the loin.

facts: A rack is cut from the rib section of the pig, with the bones left in.
Crackling is the crisp, puffed skin that forms when the rind is scored and roasted at high heat.
rack-of-pork.visual: one raw bone-in rack of pork with the rind scored, ribs curved, lying flat
rack-of-pork.what: A bone-in joint of pork, often roasted for its crackling.

facts: Raclette is both a Swiss cheese and the dish of melting it at the table, a tradition from the Alps.
The name comes from the French verb racler, to scrape, which describes serving the melted cheese.
raclette.visual: a block of pale yellow raclette cheese, one thin wedge cut from its edge
raclette.what: A Swiss cheese melted and scraped over hot potatoes.

facts: Raclette is both the name of a Swiss cheese and the dish of melting it over potatoes.
Traditionally the cheese is melted beside a fire and scraped onto the plate.
Pickled onions and gherkins are the classic accompaniments to melted raclette.
raclette-suisse.visual: a whole block of pale yellow raclette cheese with one wedge cut away, showing a creamy face
raclette-suisse.what: A Swiss melting cheese, scraped hot over potatoes.

facts: Radiatori means radiators in Italian, a name given to the pasta's ridged shape.
Pasta has been made in Italy for centuries, with hundreds of named shapes.
Ridged shapes like this are often matched with thick, chunky sauces, such as meat ragu.
radiatori.visual: a loose heap of dried, ridged, frilled pale yellow pasta shapes
radiatori.what: Frilled pasta shapes that cling to thick sauces.

facts: Radicchio is a variety of chicory, grown for a long time in the Veneto region of Italy.
Its bitterness softens when it is grilled or roasted, bringing out a sweeter flavour.
Treviso radicchio is named after the Italian city where it is traditionally grown.
radicchio.visual: one whole round head of radicchio, tightly packed ruby-red and white leaves
radicchio.what: A bitter, ruby-red leaf from the chicory family.

facts: The name comes from the Latin radix, meaning root.
Radishes are often sliced into salads or eaten with butter and bread.
radish.visual: a small bunch of red radishes with green leaves attached, bright round roots
radish.what: A small, crisp root vegetable with a peppery bite.

facts: Kkakdugi is a Korean dish of cubed radish seasoned with chilli, garlic and salted seafood.
Kimchi is a traditional Korean side dish made by fermenting vegetables in salt and seasonings.
Radish kimchi is traditionally made in autumn, when Korean radishes are harvested.
radish-kimchi.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of bright red cubes of fermented radish, moist and glossy
radish-kimchi.what: Crunchy, spicy Korean kimchi made from cubed radish.

facts: Radish sprouts are grown indoors from seed in a few days, usually without soil.
They are often used in salads and sandwiches, adding a peppery bite.
radish-sprouts.visual: a small loose heap of fresh radish sprouts, thin white stems and pale green seed leaves
radish-sprouts.what: Tiny young radish shoots with a peppery, crisp bite.

facts: Nonpareils are tiny sugar balls, and their name comes from a French phrase meaning without equal.
They are built up in layers of sugar around a tiny core.
They have long been used on cakes, biscuits and confectionery.
rainbow-nonpareils.visual: a small heap of tiny round sugar balls in pink, yellow, green and blue
rainbow-nonpareils.what: Tiny sugar balls in bright colours, for decorating cakes.

facts: In parts of the United States, including New England, sprinkles are called jimmies.
They are a common decoration on iced cakes, cupcakes and doughnuts.
rainbow-sprinkles.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl heaped with short rainbow-coloured sugar rods in pink, yellow, blue, green and orange
rainbow-sprinkles.what: Tiny coloured sugar rods used to decorate baking.

facts: Rainbow trout are native to western North America and have since been introduced around the world.
The fish is widely farmed in Britain and across Europe for the table.
rainbow-trout.visual: a whole raw rainbow trout with silvery skin and dark spots, lying flat with its head to one side
rainbow-trout.what: A freshwater fish with pink-tinted, mild, delicate flesh.

facts: The Rainier cherry was bred at Washington State University and named after Mount Rainier.
Rainier cherries are usually eaten fresh, prized for their delicate, sweet flavour.
rainier-cherry.visual: a small heap of bright yellow cherries with pink-red blushed cheeks, stems attached, fresh and glossy
rainier-cherry.what: A yellow cherry with a red blush and a honeyed sweetness.

facts: Raisins are dried grapes, traditionally dried in the sun or in warm, controlled air.
Turkey and California are both major producers, and raisins have been made since ancient times.
raisin.visual: a small heap of dark brown raisins, wrinkled and glossy
raisin.what: A dried grape, dark and sweet, for baking and puddings.

facts: Raita is a yoghurt-based side dish from India and neighbouring countries, eaten alongside spiced rice and curries.
Variations use grated cucumber, onion, tomato, or fruit such as banana, depending on the region.
raita.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl filled with smooth, pale, thick yoghurt, its surface lightly textured
raita.what: A cool yoghurt dip with cucumber, served alongside curry.

facts: Rambutan comes from South-East Asia, and its name is from the Malay word for hair.
It is related to the lychee and longan, and is eaten by peeling the skin and taking out the flesh.
The fruit grows on an evergreen tree that is widely cultivated across South-East Asia.
rambutan.visual: a whole fresh rambutan, bright red fruit with soft hairy spines, lying on the background
rambutan.what: A red, hairy tropical fruit with sweet, translucent flesh.

facts: Ramen is a noodle dish that developed in Japan from Chinese-style noodle soups.
The noodles are often made with kansui, an alkaline mineral water that gives them a springy bite.
Ramen shops in different regions of Japan use their own broths, noodle thicknesses and toppings.
ramen-noodles.visual: a loose nest of pale yellow fresh noodles, kinked and wavy, lying on the background
ramen-noodles.what: Chewy, wheat noodles made to hold up in a rich, hot broth.

facts: Ramps are native to eastern North America, where they grow in shaded, moist woodland.
In the Appalachian mountains, spring festivals are held to celebrate the ramp harvest.
ramps.visual: a loose bunch of wild ramps with slim white bulbs, purple-tinged stems and broad green leaves
ramps.what: A wild leek with a garlicky bulb and broad leaves.

facts: Ranch dressing was developed in California in the 1950s, and it became popular across the United States.
It is usually based on buttermilk and mayonnaise, with garlic, onion and herbs such as dill and parsley.
ranch-dressing.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, pale, creamy dressing with tiny flecks of green herbs
ranch-dressing.what: A creamy buttermilk and herb dressing, popular for wings.

facts: Ranch dressing was developed in the United States, and its seasoning is now sold in many countries.
Dried dill, parsley, chives and garlic are typical flavours in ranch-style mixes.
The mix is usually stirred into mayonnaise, sour cream or buttermilk to make a dip or dressing.
ranch-seasoning.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with a pale speckled dried herb and spice powder
ranch-seasoning.what: A dried mix of herbs, garlic and onion for dressings.

facts: Rangpur limes are named after the Rangpur district in what is now Bangladesh.
Rangpur limes are often used as rootstock for citrus trees because they are hardy.
rangpur-lime.visual: a whole rangpur lime with thin bright orange-yellow skin and a small stalk end
rangpur-lime.what: A sour citrus hybrid, a cross between a lemon and mandarin.

facts: Rapadura is made by boiling cane juice until thick, then pouring it into moulds to set into blocks.
It is a traditional sweetener in Brazil, and in parts of Latin America it is also known as panela.
Unlike refined white sugar, rapadura keeps some of the molasses flavour from the cane juice.
rapadura.visual: a whole rough dark golden-brown block of pressed cane sugar with a grainy surface, lying on the background
rapadura.what: Pressed whole cane juice, earthy and caramel-like.

facts: Rapeseed is a member of the cabbage family, and its oil is pressed from the seeds.
In Canada, low-erucic rapeseed oil is sold as canola, a name combining Canada and oil.
rapeseed-oil.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle filled with golden-yellow oil
rapeseed-oil.what: A mild, golden cooking oil pressed from rapeseed plants.

facts: Ras el hanout is Arabic for head of the shop, meaning the best a spice seller has to offer.
Recipes vary widely between cooks and markets, and blends often include cumin, coriander and ginger.
It is used in tagines and as a rub for lamb, chicken and couscous across Morocco and North Africa.
ras-el-hanout.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of coarse, reddish-brown ground spice blend
ras-el-hanout.what: A warm, fragrant Moroccan spice blend of many ingredients.

facts: Rasam is a thin, tangy soup from South Indian cooking, flavoured with tamarind and black pepper.
Tamarind, which gives rasam its sourness, is the pulp of a pod from a tree native to tropical Africa.
Rasam is often served with rice as part of a South Indian meal.
rasam-paste.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of a dark, glossy brown paste, smooth and thick
rasam-paste.what: A tamarind and pepper paste for making rasam soup.

facts: Rasam is a thin, tangy soup common in South Indian homes, often served with rice.
The blend typically includes black pepper, cumin and coriander, and sometimes dried red chillies.
Tamarind or tomato is usually used to give rasam its sour tang.
rasam-powder.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine, reddish-brown spice powder
rasam-powder.what: A peppery spice blend for a tangy South Indian soup.

facts: Wild raspberries grow across Europe, Asia and North America.
They are often made into jam, sauces and coulis to balance rich desserts.
raspberry.visual: a small heap of fresh red raspberries, plump and slightly glossy
raspberry.what: A soft red berry with a tart-sweet taste.

facts: Coulis is a French term for a strained purée, so the sauce is passed through a sieve.
Raspberries are native to Europe and Asia, and grow on prickly canes.
Raspberry coulis is often spooned onto plates beside cakes and sponge desserts.
raspberry-coulis.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth bright pink-red raspberry sauce
raspberry-coulis.what: A smooth, sieved sauce made from fresh raspberries.

facts: Jam is made by cooking fruit with sugar until it thickens into a spreadable preserve.
raspberry-jam.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with deep red, glossy raspberry jam
raspberry-jam.what: A tart, seedy red spread of cooked raspberries and sugar.

facts: Raspberry liqueur is made by steeping raspberries in spirit, then sweetening the result.
Framboise, the French word for raspberry, names a well-known raspberry spirit from Alsace.
Raspberry liqueur is often used in desserts, sauces and cocktails.
raspberry-liqueur.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of deep red raspberry liqueur
raspberry-liqueur.what: A sweet, rich spirit flavoured with ripe raspberries.

facts: The vanilla bean is the seed pod of a climbing orchid native to Mexico.
Ripple ice cream gets its streaks from fruit sauce swirled through the base before freezing.
raspberry-ripple-ice-cream.visual: a rounded scoop of pale cream ice cream, streaked through in bright pink, in a small plain white ceramic bowl
raspberry-ripple-ice-cream.what: Vanilla ice cream rippled with tart raspberry sauce.

facts: Fruit vinegars are a long-standing part of French cooking, and raspberry is a traditional flavour.
It is often used in salad dressings and to add sharpness to game sauces.
raspberry-vinegar.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle filled with ruby-red raspberry vinegar
raspberry-vinegar.what: A fruity, ruby-coloured vinegar made with raspberries.

facts: The ratte is a small French fingerling potato with a long, slender shape.
It is grown mainly in France and is prized for its buttery, nutty taste.
Ratte potatoes are often boiled or roasted whole with their skins on.
ratte-potato.visual: a small heap of slender, pale golden ratte potatoes with thin skins, dry and unwashed
ratte-potato.what: A small, buttery fingerling with a chestnut-like taste.

facts: Ravioli are a popular dish across Italy, with regional fillings from meat to ricotta and spinach.
Sweet versions, filled with fruit or ricotta and sugar, appear in some regional Italian cooking.
ravioli.visual: a small plain white plate with four cooked ravioli parcels, pale pasta with pinched edges, lying side by side
ravioli.what: Small filled pasta parcels, savoury or sweet inside.

facts: Peanuts are native to South America, where they were domesticated long before reaching Europe.
Peanuts are not true nuts; they are legumes, which develop in pods that grow underground.
In parts of the southern United States, raw peanuts are boiled in their shells as a snack.
raw-peanuts.visual: a small heap of raw, unroasted, pale beige peanuts with their skins still on
raw-peanuts.what: Unroasted peanuts, pale and mild, for cooking at home.

facts: Prawns live in seas and rivers around the world and are both fished and farmed.
In Britain, cold prawns are often served with brown bread and a pink sauce.
Raw prawns turn from grey to pink as they cook, which shows they are done.
raw-peeled-prawns.visual: a small heap of raw peeled prawns, pale grey-pink and translucent
raw-peeled-prawns.what: Shelled raw prawns, ready to add to curries and stir-fries.

facts: Sauerkraut is a German name meaning sour cabbage, and it has been eaten in Europe for centuries.
Fermentation is driven by naturally present lactic acid bacteria, which turn sugars into acid.
Raw sauerkraut is not heated, which keeps its crisp texture and sharp, fresh flavour.
raw-sauerkraut.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, pale shredded cabbage visible through the glass
raw-sauerkraut.what: Shredded cabbage fermented in salt, not heat-treated.

facts: Razor clams are named after their long shells, which look like old-fashioned cut-throat razors.
They burrow quickly into sandy beaches and can dig rapidly when disturbed.
They are popular in Spain and Portugal, often grilled or added to rice dishes.
razor-clams.visual: several whole razor clams in long pale-brown shells lying side by side
razor-clams.what: A long, thin shellfish with sweet, firm meat.

facts: Bangers is British slang for sausages, and the dish pairs them with mashed potato.
Potatoes reached Britain and Ireland from the Americas in the 16th century.
Onion gravy is a common accompaniment, especially in British pubs.
ready-made-bangers-and-mash.visual: a plain white plate holding two cooked pork sausages beside a smooth mound of mashed potato
ready-made-bangers-and-mash.what: Sausages and mashed potato, a British comfort meal.

facts: Chicken curry is eaten throughout South Asia, and versions have been adapted for British kitchens.
Ready meals are cooked, sealed, then chilled or frozen so they can be reheated quickly at home.
ready-made-chicken-curry.visual: a small plain white bowl of chicken curry, pieces of chicken in a thick orange-brown sauce
ready-made-chicken-curry.what: Chicken in a spiced sauce, sold ready to heat.

facts: Chilli con carne is associated with Tex-Mex cooking, combining chilli, cumin and minced beef.
The name is Spanish, meaning chilli with meat.
ready-made-chilli-con-carne.visual: a small plain white bowl of rich dark-red spiced minced beef stew, served plainly
ready-made-chilli-con-carne.what: A spiced minced beef and bean stew, ready to heat.

facts: Coleslaw takes its name from the Dutch word koolsla, meaning cabbage salad.
ready-made-coleslaw.visual: a small plain white bowl of pale creamy shredded slaw, fine strands visible through the dressing
ready-made-coleslaw.what: Shredded cabbage and carrot, bought ready to eat.

facts: Cottage pie is a traditional British dish of minced meat and gravy under a layer of mashed potato.
Shepherd's pie is a close relative, usually made with minced lamb rather than beef.
ready-made-cottage-pie.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of savoury mince in brown gravy, under golden mashed potato
ready-made-cottage-pie.what: A savoury mince and gravy dish topped with mashed potato.

facts: Custard is a sweet sauce or set pudding made by thickening milk or cream with egg yolks.
Custard powder, an egg-free version of custard, was first made in England in 1837.
ready-made-custard.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl holding smooth pale yellow vanilla custard, softly set and glossy
ready-made-custard.what: A ready-to-eat sweet custard, sold chilled.

facts: Fish pie is a British dish of fish in white sauce, usually topped with mashed potato and baked until golden.
Ready-made versions are chilled or frozen so they can be heated and served without preparing the pie from scratch.
ready-made-fish-pie.visual: one plain serving of baked fish pie with a golden mashed potato topping, on a small plain white plate
ready-made-fish-pie.what: Fish in a creamy sauce, topped with mashed potato.

facts: Gravy is a sauce made from meat juices, thickened with flour or starch.
In Britain, gravy is traditionally served with roast meat, Yorkshire puddings and vegetables.
Chilled ready-made gravy is sold in tubs and pots that can be heated on the hob.
ready-made-gravy-pot.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, glossy brown gravy
ready-made-gravy-pot.what: A chilled gravy sold in a pot, ready to warm through.

facts: Lasagne is a dish of wide flat pasta sheets layered with sauce, originating in Italy.
ready-made-lasagne.visual: a square portion of golden baked lasagne with clear layers, served on a plain white plate
ready-made-lasagne.what: Layered pasta baked with meat sauce and white sauce.

facts: It is traditionally baked until the top turns golden and crisp.
ready-made-macaroni-cheese.visual: a portion of baked macaroni cheese with a golden top, served plainly in a small plain white bowl
ready-made-macaroni-cheese.what: Pasta in a cheese sauce, ready to heat and eat.

facts: Pizza dough is traditionally made from flour, water, salt and yeast, which rises as it ferments.
Modern pizza is closely associated with the city of Naples in southern Italy.
ready-made-pizza-base.visual: a round, flat, pale pizza base with a light dusting of flour, lying flat on a plain surface
ready-made-pizza-base.what: A ready-made dough base for sauce and toppings.

facts: Potatoes were domesticated in the Andes of South America thousands of years ago.
Potato salad is eaten cold across many countries, with mayonnaise the usual dressing in Britain.
ready-made-potato-salad.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl filled with pale new potato chunks coated in creamy white mayonnaise
ready-made-potato-salad.what: Cooked potatoes in creamy mayonnaise, ready to eat.

facts: The British Sunday roast is a traditional meal of roast meat, potatoes and vegetables, often served with gravy.
Roast potatoes are usually parboiled first, then roasted in hot fat until crisp at the edges.
Ready-made roast dinners are sold chilled or frozen and heated at home in the oven or microwave.
ready-made-roast-dinner.visual: A plain white plate of sliced roast meat, golden roast potatoes and cooked vegetables, served plainly and fully cooked
ready-made-roast-dinner.what: Roast meat, potatoes and vegetables, sold ready to heat.

facts: The Scotch pie is a traditional Scottish meat pie, usually filled with minced mutton or pork.
Its pastry is a hot-water crust, made by melting fat in hot water and mixing it into the flour.
ready-made-scotch-pie.visual: a whole round Scotch pie with golden-brown hot-water pastry, on a plain white plate
ready-made-scotch-pie.what: A small round pie of minced meat in a sturdy pastry case.

facts: Shepherd's pie is traditionally made with lamb, while cottage pie uses beef.
Mashed potato is the traditional topping, often browned in the oven or under a grill.
ready-made-shepherd-s-pie.visual: a serving of shepherd's pie in a small plain white bowl, golden-brown ridged top over a dark meat filling
ready-made-shepherd-s-pie.what: Minced lamb baked under a crown of mashed potato.

facts: Curry is a broad term in English, used for many spiced dishes from South Asia.
Vegetable curries are common across India, and there are many regional styles.
ready-made-vegetable-curry.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of chunky mixed vegetables in a thick golden-brown spiced sauce
ready-made-vegetable-curry.what: A chunky, spiced vegetable curry sold ready to heat.

facts: Puff pastry is made by folding layers of butter into dough, which then puff up in the oven.
Puff pastry is used across French and British baking, in dishes such as sausage rolls and vol-au-vents.
Making puff pastry from scratch takes time, because the dough must be chilled between each folding.
ready-rolled-puff-pastry.visual: one flat, rectangular sheet of pale, ready-rolled puff pastry, lying open with layered edges visible
ready-rolled-puff-pastry.what: A thin sheet of layered pastry, ready to cut and bake.

facts: Shortcrust pastry is made by rubbing fat into flour, then binding it with a little cold water.
Shortcrust gets its name from the short, crumbly texture given by the fat.
ready-rolled-shortcrust-pastry.visual: one flat rectangular sheet of pale shortcrust pastry, unrolled and lying directly on a plain background
ready-rolled-shortcrust-pastry.what: A ready-made sheet of shortcrust pastry for pies and tarts.

facts: In Britain, the word crisps means what Americans call potato chips.
Ready salted is the classic plain flavour, with salt as the only seasoning added.
ready-salted-crisps.visual: a small heap of thin golden potato crisps with a light dusting of salt, lying loosely
ready-salted-crisps.what: Thin, crunchy fried potato slices with just a pinch of salt.

facts: Potato crisps are thin slices of potato fried until crisp, and they are a popular snack in Britain.
In Britain, ready salted means crisps with only salt added and no other flavouring.
ready-salted-ridged-crisps.visual: a small loose heap of golden ridged potato crisps lying directly on the background
ready-salted-ridged-crisps.what: Thick, ridged potato crisps, lightly salted for dipping.

facts: Sugar paste is made from icing sugar, glucose and water, kneaded until pliable.
It is rolled out thinly and draped over cakes to give a smooth finish.
Modelling sugar paste is also shaped into flowers and figures for celebration cakes.
ready-to-roll-icing.visual: a smooth round block of white sugar paste, matte and soft-looking, sitting on its base
ready-to-roll-icing.what: A smooth, pliable sugar paste for covering cakes.

facts: Real ale is beer that undergoes a second fermentation in the cask it is served from.
The Campaign for Real Ale, founded in 1971, promotes cask beers across Britain.
Bitter is a classic English draught style, typically pale amber and served from a cask.
real-ale.visual: a clear drinking glass filled with amber real ale, a thin cream head on top
real-ale.what: A traditional British beer, drawn straight from the cask.

facts: Reblochon is a soft cheese from the Savoie region of the French Alps, made from cows' milk.
reblochon.visual: one whole small round wheel of reblochon cheese, pale orange-beige washed rind, lying flat
reblochon.what: A nutty Alpine cheese, the heart of tartiflette.

facts: Red bananas are a dessert variety that originated in Southeast Asia.
Their flesh has a slightly raspberry-like tinge, and they are usually eaten fresh.
Their red-purple skin makes them easy to spot among yellow bananas in shops.
red-banana.visual: a single whole red banana with reddish-purple skin, slightly curved
red-banana.what: A sweet banana with reddish skin and a creamy taste.

facts: Anko is the Japanese name for sweetened red bean paste, and it fills many wagashi sweets.
Adzuki beans have been grown in East Asia for centuries and have long been used in Japanese confectionery.
Smooth bean paste is used in dorayaki pancakes and in daifuku mochi.
red-bean-paste.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, dark reddish-brown bean paste
red-bean-paste.what: Sweetened adzuki bean paste, used in Japanese sweets.

facts: Red cabbage gets its colour from anthocyanin pigments, which shift towards red with acid and towards blue with alkali.
In German and Central European cooking it is often braised with apple, vinegar and sugar, as Rotkohl.
red-cabbage.visual: one whole red cabbage, dense and round, deep purple-red leaves, outer leaf intact
red-cabbage.what: A deep purple cabbage that braises well with apple.

facts: It is grown in the Camargue, the marshy delta of the Rhône in southern France.
The red colour comes from a bran layer that stays on the grain after it is hulled.
red-camargue-rice.visual: a small heap of uncooked red-brown rice grains, long and slender, lying loose on a plain background
red-camargue-rice.what: A chewy, nutty red-brown rice grown in southern France.

facts: Chillies are native to the Americas and spread worldwide after European contact.
Chilli heat is measured on the Scoville scale, named after the American pharmacist Wilbur Scoville.
Long red chillies are used fresh in curries, stir-fries and salsas across Asia and Latin America.
red-chilli.visual: a small bunch of long, glossy red chillies, stalks still attached
red-chilli.what: A medium-hot fresh chilli, long and bright red.

facts: Red deer are native to Britain and are found in woodland and upland areas.
In medieval Europe, deer hunting was restricted, and venison was a prized meat.
Venison is dark-fleshed and is often served rare or slow-cooked.
red-deer-haunch.visual: one whole raw venison haunch, dark red meat, a thin layer of fat along one edge, lying flat
red-deer-haunch.what: Lean, rich venison from the back leg of a wild red deer.

facts: The Red Delicious apple was first found as a chance seedling in Iowa in the nineteenth century.
Apple trees are usually propagated by grafting, because seeds grow into fruit that differs from the parent.
It was widely grown across the United States for much of the twentieth century.
red-delicious-apple.visual: a whole glossy deep red apple with a short brown stalk, lying on its side
red-delicious-apple.what: A sweet, mild, crisp apple mostly eaten raw.

facts: Red Duke of York is a heritage potato variety with red skin, grown in Britain.
Red-skinned potatoes tend to hold their shape well when boiled.
Potatoes were first brought to Europe from the Andes of South America in the 1500s.
red-duke-of-york-potato.visual: a small heap of three clean, oval, raw red-skinned potatoes
red-duke-of-york-potato.what: A red-skinned heritage potato, good boiled or baked.

facts: Endive is a type of chicory, a member of the daisy family.
Its crisp leaves are often used raw in salads, with a slight bitterness.
Chicory roots have long been dried and roasted to make a coffee substitute.
red-endive.visual: one whole head of crisp red endive, pale leaves with deep magenta tips, shown upright
red-endive.what: A crisp, red-tinged chicory with a slightly bitter bite.

facts: Red kuri is a Japanese winter squash variety, also sold under the name Uchiki kuri.
Its skin is thin and edible, so the squash can be roasted whole without peeling.
red-kuri-squash.visual: one whole small deep red-orange squash with smooth, glossy skin and a short stem
red-kuri-squash.what: A small squash with a sweet, chestnut-like flavour.

facts: Red Leicester is an English cheese from Leicestershire, coloured with annatto.
red-leicester.visual: a block of orange cheese, one wedge cut away, pale interior showing
red-leicester.what: A mellow, nutty English cheese with a bright orange colour.

facts: It is made by grinding dried red lentils into flour and shaping the dough.
Red lentils are split and hulled, which lets them cook quickly and soften.
Lentils have been grown in the Middle East for thousands of years.
red-lentil-pasta.visual: a small heap of short, twisted pasta shapes in pale orange-pink, dried and matte
red-lentil-pasta.what: Pasta made from ground red lentils, with a nutty taste.

facts: Lentils are one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown in the Middle East for thousands of years.
Red lentils are split and have their dark outer skins removed, so they turn pale and soft.
Dal, a staple of Indian cooking, is often made from red lentils cooked slowly with spices.
red-lentils.visual: a small heap of dried red lentils, split and orange-pink, scattered loosely
red-lentils.what: Small split pulses that cook quickly and soften into soups.

facts: Miso is a Japanese seasoning made by fermenting soya beans with salt and koji mould.
Red miso is aged for longer than white miso, giving it a stronger, deeper flavour.
Its paste is stirred into soups, dressings and glazes across Japan.
red-miso.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, deep reddish-brown paste
red-miso.what: A deep, salty Japanese paste made from fermented soya.

facts: Its small size makes it well suited to being cooked whole, usually by pan-frying or grilling.
Red mullet has been known and eaten since classical times, and appears in Roman writings.
red-mullet.visual: a whole raw red mullet with rosy-red scales, lying on its side
red-mullet.what: A small, rose-coloured sea fish with sweet, firm flesh.

facts: Red onions have a purple-red skin, and their flesh is often tinted pink or violet.
They are commonly eaten raw in salads or pickled in vinegar.
Onions originated in central Asia and have been cultivated for thousands of years.
red-onion.visual: a whole raw red onion with dark purple-red skin, lying on the background
red-onion.what: A purple-skinned onion with a milder, sweeter bite.

facts: Onion marmalade is cooked low and slow until the onions turn sweet and jammy.
red-onion-marmalade.visual: a glossy purple-red onion marmalade filling a plain glass jar without a label
red-onion-marmalade.what: A thick, sweet relish of slow-cooked red onions and vinegar.

facts: Red palm oil is pressed from the flesh of the oil palm fruit rather than from its kernel.
It is a traditional ingredient in West African stews, especially in Nigeria and Ghana.
The oil palm is native to West Africa and is now grown across tropical regions.
red-palm-oil.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, bright orange oil
red-palm-oil.what: Bright orange oil pressed from the fruit of an oil palm.

facts: Bell peppers turn red as they ripen, and become sweeter as the green fruit matures.
Peppers are native to the Americas and reached Europe after the voyages of Columbus.
Sweet peppers are roasted, stuffed or eaten raw in salads in cuisines around the world.
red-pepper.visual: one whole glossy red bell pepper with its green stalk cap, lying on its side
red-pepper.what: A sweet, ripe bell pepper, red all the way through.

facts: These berries are not true peppercorns, which come from a climbing vine in the pepper family.
Schinus berries, sold as red or pink peppercorns, come from a tree in the cashew family.
They are often used whole or crushed over fish, salads and sauces.
red-peppercorns.visual: a small heap of dried red peppercorns, whole berries, bright red and slightly wrinkled
red-peppercorns.what: Ripe red berries, dried, with a sweet and fruity flavour.

facts: Pesto comes from the Italian word pestare, meaning to pound or crush.
Sun-dried tomatoes are preserved by drying in the sun, a method long used across the Mediterranean.
Genoa in north-west Italy is traditionally associated with the basil pesto style.
red-pesto.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with thick deep red-orange paste, flecked dark
red-pesto.what: A thick, tangy sauce made from sun-dried tomatoes and oil.

facts: Beni shoga gets its colour from red shiso leaves in many traditional recipes.
It is served with yakisoba and okonomiyaki in Japan.
The word beni means red in Japanese, and shoga means ginger.
red-pickled-ginger.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thin shreds of bright red pickled ginger
red-pickled-ginger.what: Thin pink-red strips of ginger pickled in sweet vinegar.

facts: Plums are stone fruits, closely related to cherries, apricots and peaches.
Plums were cultivated in China for a very long time before spreading across the world.
Their tart skin and juicy flesh suit crumbles, chutneys and jams, as cooking softens the fruit.
red-plum.visual: a whole red plum with a glossy deep red skin and a faint dusty bloom
red-plum.what: A juicy stone fruit with a tart red skin.

facts: Quinoa was grown in the Andes of South America for thousands of years, and the Inca valued it highly.
Most quinoa is now grown in Bolivia and Peru, and it is farmed in other countries too.
red-quinoa.visual: a small heap of uncooked red quinoa seeds, dark reddish-brown, tiny and round
red-quinoa.what: A small, grain-like seed that holds its shape when cooked.

facts: Red Russian kale is a non-curly kale whose leaves are flatter and more tender than curly types.
Kale is a member of the cabbage family, grown in Europe for many centuries.
Its young leaves can be eaten raw when finely shredded, or cooked lightly.
red-russian-kale.visual: a small bunch of red Russian kale, flat purple-green leaves with pale purple stems
red-russian-kale.what: Hardy kale with flat, tender leaves and purple stems.

facts: Sauerkraut is a German word meaning sour cabbage.
Red cabbage keeps its colour through fermentation, though the shade can shift with acidity.
Fermented cabbage was valued on long sea voyages because it kept for months.
red-sauerkraut.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of shredded red-purple fermented cabbage, moist and glossy
red-sauerkraut.what: Fermented red cabbage, salted and sweetened with apple.

facts: Red shiso is a member of the mint family and is grown widely across East Asia.
In Japan it is used to colour umeboshi, salted pickled plums, giving them their pink-red shade.
Its Japanese name, aka-jiso, means red perilla, and it belongs to the same species as green shiso.
red-shiso.visual: a small bunch of fresh red shiso leaves, deep purple-red with serrated edges and short stems, on a plain white background
red-shiso.what: A purple-red East Asian herb with a minty, citrusy taste.

facts: Snappers are a large family of fish found in warm seas around the world.
In Mexico, whole red snapper is often grilled or cooked with lime and chilli.
Red snapper is valued for its firm, mild flesh and is often sold whole.
red-snapper.visual: a whole raw red snapper, bright pinkish-red scales, lying on its side with the eyes intact
red-snapper.what: A bright red-pink sea fish with sweet, firm, white flesh.

facts: Red wine gets its colour from the skins of dark grapes, which stay in the juice during fermentation.
Some of the earliest evidence of winemaking comes from the Caucasus region, including Georgia.
red-wine.visual: a clear drinking glass filled with deep ruby red wine, plain pale background
red-wine.what: Fermented grape drink, deep in colour, that flavours stews.

facts: Wine-based sauces like this have long been used in French cooking to finish roasted meats.
Cooks often add a knob of butter at the end to give the sauce a glossy finish.
red-wine-gravy.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of glossy dark red-brown gravy, smooth surface with a slight sheen
red-wine-gravy.what: A glossy sauce of reduced red wine and meat stock.

facts: Jus is the French word for juice, and in cooking it means the natural juices of meat.
Red wine jus is often served with roast beef and steak in French-style restaurant cooking.
red-wine-jus.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of glossy, dark red-brown sauce with a smooth, shiny surface
red-wine-jus.what: A glossy, dark sauce made by reducing red wine with stock.

facts: Red wine vinegar is made when bacteria turn red wine into acetic acid.
Its colour and flavour come from the grape variety and the wine it is made from.
red-wine-vinegar.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of deep ruby-red vinegar
red-wine-vinegar.what: Sharp vinegar made from fermented red wine.

facts: Redcurrants are a type of currant, related to blackcurrants and gooseberries.
In Britain they are often cooked into a jelly served with roast lamb or venison.
Their tart juice is used in sauces and desserts as well as in jellies.
redcurrant.visual: a small bunch of glossy bright red redcurrants on their pale green stalks, plain background
redcurrant.what: A small, tart red berry that grows in bunches on bushes.

facts: Redcurrant jelly is a classic accompaniment to roast lamb, venison and other game.
Redcurrants contain natural pectin, which helps the juice set into a firm jelly.
redcurrant-jelly.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with glossy, deep ruby-red jelly that wobbles softly
redcurrant-jelly.what: A glossy, tart red jelly made from redcurrants and sugar.

facts: Soy sauce has a history stretching back many centuries in East Asia, starting in China.
Japanese soy sauce, known as shoyu, is often brewed with roughly equal amounts of wheat and soybeans.
reduced-salt-soy-sauce.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle filled with dark reddish-brown soy sauce, its cap off
reduced-salt-soy-sauce.what: A soy sauce with less salt, for gentler seasoning.

facts: Haricot beans are native to the Americas and were introduced to Europe in the 16th century.
Baked beans are usually made by simmering pre-cooked beans in a tomato sauce.
reduced-sugar-baked-beans.visual: a small plain white bowl of soft haricot beans in a glossy orange tomato sauce
reduced-sugar-baked-beans.what: Haricot beans in tomato sauce, made with less sugar.

facts: Refining removes the coconut smell and flavour, so the oil suits frying and baking.
Copra, the dried flesh of the coconut, is the usual raw material for refined coconut oil.
refined-coconut-oil.visual: a plain glass jar of pale, clear coconut oil without a label
refined-coconut-oil.what: A pale, neutral oil made from dried coconut flesh.

facts: The name comes from the Spanish word refrito, meaning well-fried, and the beans are cooked, mashed and fried.
Pinto beans, commonly used, get their name from the Spanish word for painted, referring to their speckled skins.
Beans were cultivated in the Americas long before European contact and remain a staple across Latin America.
refried-beans.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, mashed pinto beans, pale brown and glossy
refried-beans.what: Mashed, fried pinto beans, a staple of Mexican cooking.

facts: French remoulade is usually made by adding capers, gherkins and herbs to mayonnaise.
Louisiana remoulade is a different sauce, often reddish and spicy, served with seafood.
remoulade.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, pale creamy sauce flecked with green herbs
remoulade.what: A tangy French sauce, a mayonnaise with capers and herbs.

facts: Rendang is a slow-cooked dish from the Minangkabau people of West Sumatra in Indonesia.
It is popular in Indonesia and Malaysia, especially at celebrations and feasts.
rendang-paste.visual: a plain glass jar without a label holding a thick, dark reddish-brown spice paste
rendang-paste.what: A dark, aromatic spice paste used to cook beef slowly.

facts: Rhubarb is a vegetable, though it is used like a fruit in desserts such as crumbles and pies.
Forced rhubarb, grown in dark sheds in Yorkshire in winter, has a particularly delicate pink colour.
Rhubarb stalks are traditionally sweetened with sugar, and ginger is a common partner in British puddings.
rhubarb.visual: a small bunch of long pink rhubarb stalks, trimmed, with pale green ends
rhubarb.what: Tart pink stalks that are usually cooked with sugar.

facts: Rhubarb was long grown in Britain, and forced rhubarb from Yorkshire is a famous speciality.
Rhubarb jam is often flavoured with ginger or vanilla to balance its sharpness.
rhubarb-jam.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with glossy bright pink rhubarb jam
rhubarb-jam.what: A tart, sweet spread made by cooking rhubarb with sugar.

facts: Rice bran oil is widely used in parts of Asia for high-heat frying.
Its smoke point is high, so it is suited to deep-frying and stir-frying.
The oil is made from the bran that is removed when rice is milled to white.
rice-bran-oil.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of pale golden oil
rice-bran-oil.what: A mild oil extracted from the bran layer of rice grains.

facts: Puffed rice cakes are made by heating rice grains under pressure in a mould, which makes them expand.
rice-cakes.visual: a small heap of round, pale golden puffed rice cakes, lying loosely
rice-cakes.what: These light, crisp discs are made from puffed rice grains.

facts: Rice flour is used in many batters, including some Japanese tempura, for a crisp coating.
In Asia, rice flour is a traditional base for noodles, cakes and dumplings.
Rice flour is often used in shortbread and biscuits to give a crumbly, sandy texture.
rice-flour.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine, bright white rice flour
rice-flour.what: A fine, starchy flour milled from white or brown rice.

facts: Rice milk is made by blending cooked or soaked rice with water and then straining the liquid.
It is sold as a dairy-free alternative to cow's milk in many shops.
Rice-based drinks are common across Asia, where rice is a staple grain.
rice-milk.visual: a clear drinking glass of thin, pale white rice milk
rice-milk.what: A thin, lightly sweet milk-style drink made from rice.

facts: It is widely used in Vietnamese cooking, where it wraps fresh spring rolls.
Despite its name, rice paper contains no wood pulp and is not paper in the usual sense.
rice-paper.visual: a neat stack of dry, round, pale translucent rice paper sheets, lying flat
rice-paper.what: Thin, edible sheets made from rice flour and water.

facts: Rice vermicelli is widely eaten across Vietnam, China, Thailand and the Philippines.
Vermicelli means little worms in Italian, a name given to many thin pasta shapes.
rice-vermicelli.visual: a small heap of dry, translucent white rice noodles, fine thin strands
rice-vermicelli.what: Fine, thread-like noodles made from rice flour and water.

facts: Rice vinegar is central to Japanese sushi rice, where it seasons the cooked grains.
Chinese black rice vinegar is a different product, darker and richer.
Like other vinegars, it is made when bacteria turn alcohol into acetic acid.
rice-vinegar.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle, pale straw-coloured liquid inside
rice-vinegar.what: A mild, slightly sweet vinegar made from fermented rice.

facts: Rich tea biscuits are a traditional British biscuit, usually eaten dunked in a cup of tea.
Their sturdy, plain texture makes them hold up well to dunking in hot drinks.
rich-tea-biscuits.visual: a few round, pale golden rich tea biscuits, lightly pricked, on a small plain white plate
rich-tea-biscuits.what: Plain, lightly sweet British biscuits, made for dunking.

facts: Ricotta means re-cooked in Italian, because it is made by heating the whey left from other cheeses.
It is a classic filling for ravioli, cannoli and lasagne in Italian cooking.
ricotta.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of soft, white, moist ricotta with a fine grainy texture
ricotta.what: A soft, mild curd cheese made from whey.

facts: Gnudi means 'naked' in Italian, because they are like ravioli filling without the pasta wrapper.
Ricotta means 'recooked' in Italian, from the way the cheese is made by heating whey again.
ricotta-gnocchi.visual: a small plain white plate holding pale, soft ricotta gnocchi, barely shaped
ricotta-gnocchi.what: Soft, pillowy dumplings made from ricotta cheese and flour.

facts: Ricotta salata is ricotta that has been salted, pressed and dried until firm.
It comes from Sicily and Sardinia, where it has long been made from sheep's milk.
ricotta-salata.visual: a firm white block of ricotta salata with one thick wedge cut away, showing a close crumbly texture
ricotta-salata.what: Firm, salted ricotta that crumbles over pasta and salads.

facts: The wine ranges from bone-dry to very sweet, depending on how the grapes are picked and fermented.
Its acidity lets some rieslings age for decades.
riesling.visual: a clear drinking glass filled with pale golden-straw white wine, a little below the rim
riesling.what: A white wine grape known for fresh acidity and fruit.

facts: The name comes from rigato, the Italian word for ridged or lined.
Its wide ridged shape holds thick meat sauces, and it is often baked with cheese.
It is a common shape across Italy and in many Italian-American kitchens.
rigatoni.visual: a small heap of dried rigatoni tubes, pale cream with ridged outer surfaces
rigatoni.what: Large ridged Italian pasta tubes that suit thick sauces.

facts: Rillettes is a French preparation, traditionally made from pork cooked slowly in its own fat.
It is especially associated with the city of Tours in the Loire valley.
rillettes.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of pinkish-brown shredded meat, topped with a smooth layer of pale fat
rillettes.what: Slow-cooked shredded pork, set in fat for spreading.

facts: The Rioja region is in northern Spain, along the Ebro River.
Rioja is a protected name, so the wine must come from the official region to use it.
rioja.visual: a clear drinking glass holding deep ruby red wine, filled about halfway
rioja.what: A dry red wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

facts: Roasting a whole bird was a traditional way to cook chicken in Britain and Europe.
Chickens were domesticated thousands of years ago in Southeast Asia, from the red junglefowl.
roast-chicken.visual: a portion of cooked roast chicken, golden skin and pale white meat, lying on a plain white plate
roast-chicken.what: Cooked chicken from a roast, good in sandwiches and salads.

facts: Flavoured crisps are made by tumbling plain fried or baked crisps with seasoning.
Crisps like these are a popular snack in Britain.
roast-chicken-crisps.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thin golden crisps, lightly dusted
roast-chicken-crisps.what: Thin, crunchy savoury crisps with a roast chicken flavour.

facts: Sweet chestnuts are native to southern Europe and western Asia.
They are often roasted over an open fire and sold from street stalls in winter.
Chestnuts are used in soups, stuffings and in marrons glacés, sugar-preserved French sweets.
roasted-chestnuts.visual: a small heap of roasted chestnuts in dark brown shells, a few split open to show golden flesh
roasted-chestnuts.what: Sweet nuts roasted in their shells until soft and smoky.

facts: Roasting dries the chickpea and makes it crisp, a method used across the Middle East and South Asia.
Chickpeas are known as garbanzo beans in parts of the Americas and as chana in India.
roasted-chickpeas.visual: a small heap of roasted chickpeas, golden brown and crunchy, loose on the background
roasted-chickpeas.what: Crisp toasted chickpeas, often spiced for snacking.

facts: Peanuts are not true nuts but legumes that grow underground, and they are related to peas and beans.
The peanut is thought to have been domesticated in South America, and it spread around the world through trade.
In South-East Asia, roasted peanuts are often ground into sauces and sprinkled over noodles.
roasted-peanuts.visual: a small heap of roasted shelled peanuts, golden brown and slightly glossy
roasted-peanuts.what: Crunchy, salted nuts, roasted until golden and toasty.

facts: In Mexico, toasted pumpkin seeds are known as pepitas.
Many pumpkin seeds are sold hulled, with the outer shell removed.
Pumpkins and squashes were domesticated in the Americas long before European contact.
roasted-pumpkin-seeds.visual: a small heap of toasted pale green pumpkin seeds, roasted and lightly salted
roasted-pumpkin-seeds.what: Crunchy, salted seeds scooped from pumpkins and roasted.

facts: Sweet peppers are native to the Americas and reached Europe in the 1500s.
Ajvar is a famous red pepper relish in Balkan cooking, often made in large batches each autumn.
roasted-red-pepper-spread.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, glossy orange-red roasted pepper spread
roasted-red-pepper-spread.what: A smooth, smoky, sweet spread made from roasted red peppers.

facts: Red peppers are roasted over a flame or under a grill until the skins blister and peel away.
Roasted peppers are popular in Spanish, Italian and Middle Eastern cooking.
Peppers, native to the Americas, reached Europe in the 1500s after Columbus.
roasted-red-peppers.visual: two roasted red pepper halves, soft and glossy with charred edges, lying flat
roasted-red-peppers.what: Sweet red peppers, roasted until soft and smoky.

facts: Sunflower seeds come from the large flower head of the sunflower plant.
Toasting seeds in a dry pan brings out a nutty flavour and makes them crisp.
Pumpkin seeds, known as pepitas in Mexico, are widely used in Mexican cooking.
roasted-seed-mix.visual: a small heap of toasted sunflower, pumpkin and sesame seeds, golden and mixed together
roasted-seed-mix.what: Toasted sunflower, pumpkin and sesame seeds for crunch.

facts: Many robiola cheeses are made from a mixture of cow, sheep and goat milk.
robiola.visual: a small round of soft white cheese with one wedge cut away, creamy ivory interior, lying on a plain background
robiola.what: A soft, creamy Italian cheese with a mild tang.
