surstromming.what: A Swedish fermented herring with a famously strong smell.

facts: Sushi rice is a Japanese short-grain rice, and its sticky texture helps it hold its shape.
The vinegar mixture is called sushi-zu, and it is folded into the rice while the rice is still warm.
The name sushi refers to the vinegar-seasoned rice rather than the fish.
sushi-rice.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of glossy, cooked short-grain rice, slightly sticky
sushi-rice.what: Short, sticky white rice seasoned with vinegar and salt.

facts: Seasoned sushi vinegar is mixed into warm cooked rice, which is then fanned to cool it.
Rice vinegar is made from fermented rice and is milder than many Western vinegars.
sushi-vinegar.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of pale golden liquid
sushi-vinegar.what: Rice vinegar seasoned with sugar and salt for sushi rice.

facts: Yaji is the name of the spice mix, built around ground roasted peanuts and dried chilli.
The spice is rubbed onto the meat before grilling and often sprinkled over it again afterwards.
suya-spice.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of coarse reddish-brown spice powder, gritty and dark, mixed evenly
suya-spice.what: A hot, nutty Nigerian spice for grilled meat skewers.

facts: In Britain it is also called swede, short for Swedish turnip.
In Scotland it is served as neeps, often mashed with butter and pepper alongside haggis.
swede.visual: a whole raw swede, round and bulbous, with a purple-tinged top and a pale yellow base
swede.what: A sweet root vegetable with dense golden flesh.

facts: Sweet and sour flavours are a feature of Cantonese cooking, balancing sugar and vinegar.
It is usually made from sugar, vinegar and a thickener such as cornflour.
sweet-and-sour-dipping-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl filled with glossy orange-red sweet and sour sauce
sweet-and-sour-dipping-sauce.what: A sweet, tangy dip, often served with takeaway food.

facts: Sweet and sour flavouring is a long-standing feature of Chinese cooking.
Versions of sweet and sour sauce are found across many cuisines, often made with pineapple and vinegar.
The sauce is often thickened with cornflour, which gives it a glossy, clinging texture.
sweet-and-sour-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of glossy, bright orange sauce, smooth and evenly coloured
sweet-and-sour-sauce.what: A glossy, tangy sauce made from sugar and vinegar.

facts: Its name, tian mian jiang, means sweet flour sauce in Mandarin Chinese.
It is traditionally served with Peking duck, spooned onto thin pancakes with spring onion.
It is made by fermenting wheat flour, which gives it a dark colour and a deep, savoury sweetness.
sweet-bean-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, glossy dark brown paste
sweet-bean-sauce.what: A dark, sweet paste made from fermented wheat flour.

facts: Sweet chestnuts have been an important food in parts of southern Europe for centuries.
Chestnut flour once served as a staple in mountain villages of Italy and France.
Mont Blanc is a French dessert of chestnut purée piped over cream and meringue.
sweet-chestnut-puree.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth pale-brown chestnut purée
sweet-chestnut-puree.what: A smooth, sweet paste made from cooked chestnuts.

facts: Crisps are usually made by slicing potatoes thinly, frying or baking them, then seasoning.
Sweet chilli sauce is a Thai-style condiment made from chillies, sugar, garlic and vinegar.
sweet-chilli-crisps.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of glossy orange-red potato crisps
sweet-chilli-crisps.what: Crisps coated in a sticky, gently spicy sweet chilli.

facts: Sweet chilli sauce is a Thai-style condiment that balances chilli heat with sugar, garlic and vinegar.
It is often served with spring rolls, fried chicken and fish cakes.
sweet-chilli-dipping-sauce.visual: a small plain clear glass bowl of glossy red sweet chilli dipping sauce
sweet-chilli-dipping-sauce.what: Sticky, mildly hot sauce with a sweet, tangy flavour.

facts: Many versions use red chillies, garlic, sugar and vinegar, with the sweetness balancing the heat.
sweet-chilli-sauce.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of glossy red sweet chilli sauce
sweet-chilli-sauce.what: Syrupy, mildly spicy sauce with a sweet, tangy flavour.

facts: Sweet cicely is a hardy plant native to mountain areas of Europe, and it has long grown in herb gardens.
Its leaves and seeds carry the anise-like flavour, and the roots can also be eaten.
sweet-cicely.visual: a small bunch of fresh sweet cicely, feathery pale green fern-like leaves on thin stems
sweet-cicely.what: A herb with aniseed flavour that sweetens tart fruit.

facts: Cider is made by pressing apples and fermenting the juice, and has been made in Europe for centuries.
In England, cider apples are grown in orchards in counties such as Herefordshire and Somerset.
sweet-cider.visual: a clear drinking glass of pale golden sweet cider
sweet-cider.what: A sweet, mild apple drink made from pressed apples.

facts: Sweet marjoram is native to the Mediterranean region and western Asia.
Marjoram has been grown as a culinary herb since ancient times.
sweet-marjoram.visual: a small bunch of fresh sweet marjoram, soft oval grey-green leaves on thin pale stems
sweet-marjoram.what: A mild, sweet herb in the oregano family.

facts: Paprika is made from dried peppers and is central to Hungarian cooking, especially goulash.
Pimentón, the smoked paprika of Spain, is dried over oak fires, which gives it a smoky flavour.
sweet-paprika.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine, bright red paprika powder, level on top
sweet-paprika.what: A mild, sweet red powder made from ground dried peppers.

facts: Relish is a condiment of chopped vegetables preserved in vinegar and sugar.
Commercial versions are often made from chopped cucumbers, cooked with sugar and spices.
sweet-pickle-relish.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of finely chopped green sweet pickle relish
sweet-pickle-relish.what: Chopped sweet pickles, a tangy topping for hot dogs.

facts: Peppers originated in the Americas and reached Europe after 1492.
Sweet pointed peppers are often roasted or grilled until the skin blisters.
They are popular in Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cooking.
sweet-pointed-pepper.visual: one whole sweet pointed pepper, glossy red, long and tapering at the tip
sweet-pointed-pepper.what: A thin-walled, sweet pepper that tapers to a point.

facts: Popcorn is made by heating corn kernels until the moisture inside turns to steam and bursts them open.
Popped corn has been eaten in the Americas for thousands of years.
Sweet popcorn is often coated in caramel or sugar syrup, which hardens as it cools.
sweet-popcorn.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl heaped with glossy, sugar-coated popcorn
sweet-popcorn.what: Popped corn kernels coated in a crisp sugar glaze.

facts: Sweet potatoes are not related to the common potato; they belong to the morning glory family.
They were domesticated in the Americas thousands of years ago and are now grown across the tropics and subtropics.
In the United States, sweet potatoes are a traditional part of autumn and winter holiday meals.
sweet-potato.visual: a whole sweet potato with smooth reddish-brown skin and tapered ends, lying on a plain background
sweet-potato.what: An orange-fleshed root that turns sweet when roasted.

facts: Gnocchi are small dumplings made with potato or flour, and are especially associated with Italian cooking.
Sweet potatoes originated in Central and South America and are not closely related to the common potato.
Gnocchi are often shaped by rolling the dough over the tines of a fork, which leaves ridges.
sweet-potato-gnocchi.visual: a small heap of raw orange sweet potato gnocchi with ridged, pillowy shapes on a plain background
sweet-potato-gnocchi.what: Soft, pillowy dumplings made with orange sweet potato.

facts: Sweet potato leaves are eaten as a leafy vegetable in parts of Africa, Asia and the Pacific.
The plant belongs to the bindweed family, Convolvulaceae, and is grown for its roots.
sweet-potato-leaves.visual: a small bunch of fresh tender sweet potato leaves, bright green, stems attached
sweet-potato-leaves.what: Tender green leaves of the sweet potato, cooked as greens.

facts: In Japan the paste is called anko, and it is a core filling for traditional sweets.
In Japanese dorayaki, two small pancakes sandwich a layer of this paste.
sweet-red-bean-paste.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of dark reddish-brown sweet bean paste, smooth and glossy
sweet-red-bean-paste.what: A sweet, smooth paste made from cooked adzuki beans.

facts: Jiuniang is made by fermenting glutinous rice with a starter of yeast and mould.
It is often served as a dessert, or stirred into a warm soup with beaten egg.
Its sweetness comes from starches in the rice being broken down into sugars during fermentation.
sweet-rice-wine-paste.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with soft pale cream rice paste showing visible grains
sweet-rice-wine-paste.what: A sweet, soft paste of fermented glutinous rice.

facts: Pâte sucrée is a French name meaning sweet dough, and it is the usual pastry for French fruit tarts.
Unlike flaky pastry, it is rich and short, so it crumbles softly rather than layering.
It is often baked blind first, with weights in the case, before the filling goes in.
sweet-shortcrust-pastry.visual: one rolled ball of pale yellow sweet pastry dough, smooth and slightly crumbly at the edge, on its own
sweet-shortcrust-pastry.what: Sweet, crisp pastry made with butter, sugar and egg yolk.

facts: Amaebi is the Japanese name, from 'ama' meaning sweet and 'ebi' meaning shrimp.
It is usually served raw as sushi, and the heads are often fried separately.
sweet-shrimp.visual: a whole raw sweet shrimp, translucent pinkish-white body and curled tail, lying on its side
sweet-shrimp.what: A small, sweet shrimp often eaten raw in sushi.

facts: Kecap manis means sweet soy sauce in Indonesian, and it is used in cooking and at the table.
It is made by simmering soy with palm sugar, sometimes with spices such as star anise.
It is a key flavour in satay, where it is brushed over grilled meat skewers.
sweet-soy-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, dark, glossy sweet soy sauce
sweet-soy-sauce.what: A thick, syrupy Indonesian soy sauce with palm sugar.

facts: Vermouth is a wine flavoured with botanicals, traditionally including wormwood.
The name vermouth comes from the German word Wermut, meaning wormwood.
sweet-vermouth.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle filled with deep amber-red vermouth liquid
sweet-vermouth.what: A sweet, herbal fortified wine used in cocktails.

facts: Sweet woodruff is a small plant native to the woodlands of much of Europe.
Its leaves develop a sweet, hay-like scent once cut and dried.
In Germany it is traditionally steeped in white wine to make Maibowle, a May punch.
sweet-woodruff.visual: a small bunch of fresh sweet woodruff sprigs, whorls of narrow bright green leaves on thin stems, on a plain background
sweet-woodruff.what: A woodland herb with a hay and vanilla scent.

facts: Maize was first domesticated in southern Mexico from a wild grass called teosinte.
Sweetcorn's sugar turns to starch soon after picking, so it is best eaten fresh.
After European contact with the Americas, maize spread to farms across Asia, Africa and Europe.
sweetcorn.visual: a whole fresh sweetcorn cob, yellow kernels visible, green husk partly peeled back, lying on its side
sweetcorn.what: A sweet variety of maize, eaten fresh from the cob.

facts: A Swiss roll is a sponge baked thin, spread with jam and rolled while still warm.
Sponge cakes rely on whisked eggs for their lightness, and this method underlies many rolled cakes.
swiss-roll.visual: one whole Swiss roll lying on its side, golden sponge rolled into a neat log with a red jam spiral visible at one end
swiss-roll.what: A light sponge cake rolled round a layer of jam.

facts: Swordfish get their name from their long, flat upper bill, which they use to slash at prey.
Swordfish live in warm and temperate oceans around the world and are often grilled or seared.
Swordfish is a popular fish in Italy and Sicily, where it is cooked in many traditional ways.
swordfish-steak.visual: one raw swordfish steak, cut crosswise, dense pale pink-red flesh, lying flat
swordfish-steak.what: A firm, meaty steak from a large sword-billed ocean fish.

facts: Szechuan pepper is the dried husk of a prickly ash tree, not a true peppercorn.
It gives a tingling, numbing sensation and is central to Sichuan cooking in south-west China.
szechuan-pepper-salt.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of coarse grey-brown salt speckled with dark specks
szechuan-pepper-salt.what: Toasted salt blended with numbing Szechuan peppercorns.

facts: Szechuan peppercorns are not related to black pepper; they are the dried husks of a prickly ash tree.
They are a key flavour in Sichuan cooking from south-western China, used in dishes such as mapo tofu.
US authorities banned Szechuan peppercorn imports from 1968 over fears of citrus disease.
szechuan-peppercorns.visual: a small heap of dried reddish-brown peppercorn husks, some split open to show small dark seeds
szechuan-peppercorns.what: Dried husks with a citrusy, tingling, numbing bite.

facts: Sichuan cooking is known for chilli heat and the tingling numbness of Sichuan pepper.
Sichuan pepper comes from the husks of a plant related to the prickly ash tree.
Sichuan is a province in south-west China, and its cuisine is among the best known in the country.
szechuan-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of dark reddish-brown sauce, thick and glossy
szechuan-sauce.what: A hot, savoury sauce from the Sichuan region of China.

facts: The T-bone takes its name from the T-shaped bone that runs through the middle of the steak.
The sirloin side is firmer, while the fillet side is more tender.
t-bone-steak.visual: one raw T-bone steak, dark red beef with a T-shaped bone through the middle, lying flat on the background
t-bone-steak.what: A beef steak cut with a T-shaped bone and two muscles.

facts: Tabil is a seasoning used in Tunisian cooking, often on couscous, meat and bread.
Its caraway seeds come from a plant in the parsley family, Apiaceae.
tabil.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine reddish-brown spice powder
tabil.what: A Tunisian spice blend of coriander, caraway and chilli.

facts: Salt is mined from underground deposits or made by evaporating seawater.
Table salt is usually refined, which gives it a fine, uniform grain.
In Britain, salt was once a valuable commodity, and Droitwich in Worcestershire was a centre of production.
table-salt.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine white salt crystals
table-salt.what: Fine white salt, ground small for quick, even seasoning.

facts: Cumin has been used as a spice for thousands of years and is a common ingredient in many Mexican blends.
Paprika is made from dried, ground peppers, and its flavour ranges from sweet to hot.
taco-seasoning.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl heaped with reddish-brown ground spice blend, fine and powdery
taco-seasoning.what: A spice mix of chilli, cumin and paprika for tacos.

facts: A hard taco shell is a corn tortilla that has been folded and fried.
Corn tortillas have been made in Mexico for centuries, from nixtamalised maize.
Hard shells became popular in the United States, where ready-made versions are widely sold.
taco-shell.visual: three crisp golden corn taco shells, U-shaped, standing upright on a plain white plate
taco-shell.what: A crunchy, U-shaped corn shell that holds spiced mince.

facts: Tagliatelle is traditionally served with a slow-cooked meat ragu, a tradition from Bologna.
Dried tagliatelle keeps for a long time in a cupboard, unlike fresh pasta.
Its wide, flat shape holds rich sauces well.
tagliatelle.visual: a loose heap of dried golden tagliatelle ribbons, flat and slightly curled
tagliatelle.what: Flat, ribbon-shaped egg pasta, classic with meat ragu.

facts: Tagliolini is a type of tagliatelle, cut very narrow, from the Emilia-Romagna region of Italy.
The name comes from the Italian word taglio, meaning a cut.
Fresh egg pasta like this is traditionally rolled by hand and cut into thin strips.
tagliolini.visual: a small loose heap of uncooked pale yellow tagliolini pasta ribbons, slightly curled
tagliolini.what: Thin ribbons of egg pasta, finer than tagliatelle.

facts: Tahini is a staple across the eastern Mediterranean and the Middle East, used in hummus and baba ghanoush.
The word tahini comes from Arabic, where it refers to ground or crushed seeds.
Sesame has been grown for thousands of years in Africa and Asia, and its seeds are pressed for oil.
tahini.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, pale beige tahini paste with a slightly glossy surface
tahini.what: A smooth paste made from ground sesame seeds.

facts: Tahini is a paste made by grinding toasted or raw hulled sesame seeds.
Sesame has been grown for thousands of years, and tahini has long been used across the eastern Mediterranean.
tahini-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl holding a smooth, thick, pale beige sauce with a glossy top
tahini-sauce.what: A creamy dressing of sesame paste, lemon and garlic.

facts: Takuan is made from daikon, a long white radish, often sun-dried before pickling.
Traditional takuan is pickled in rice bran, salt and sometimes sugar over several weeks.
Takuan is a common side dish in Japan, often served alongside rice and miso soup.
takuan.visual: one whole long bright yellow pickled daikon radish, smooth and firm, lying on its side
takuan.what: Bright yellow Japanese pickled radish, crunchy and tangy.

facts: Taleggio takes its name from Val Taleggio, a valley in the Bergamo area of Lombardy.
It is a washed-rind cheese, rinsed during ripening, which gives it a strong aroma and fruity flavour.
taleggio.visual: A small square block of soft pale cheese with a pinkish-orange washed rind, one wedge cut away to show the creamy interior.
taleggio.what: A soft, fruity Italian cheese that melts smoothly.

facts: Tallow is made by slowly heating raw beef fat so that it separates from the tissue and sets solid.
Before vegetable oils were widely available, tallow was used for frying and for making candles.
Beef dripping, the fat left from roasting meat, is a close relative used in British kitchens.
tallow.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of creamy white, solid rendered beef fat
tallow.what: Rendered beef fat, used for frying and savoury cooking.

facts: Tamagoyaki is a Japanese omelette cooked in a rectangular pan and rolled as it sets.
Tamago is also the Japanese word for egg.
It is often served as a sushi topping and in bento boxes.
tamago.visual: a block of golden layered rolled omelette, one end cut to show its layers, on a plain white plate
tamago.what: A sweet, layered Japanese omelette, rolled and sliced.

facts: Tamari began in Japan as the liquid that pooled on top of miso as it fermented.
Traditional tamari is brewed mainly from soybeans, with little or no wheat.
Tamari is widely used in Japanese cooking as a dipping sauce and seasoning.
tamari.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle filled with dark brown liquid, glossy and rich
tamari.what: A rich, dark soy sauce, often made without wheat.

facts: Tamarillo is a small tree native to the Andes of South America, and it is also called tree tomato.
It is widely grown in New Zealand, where it is sold as a fruit crop.
The skin is bitter, so the flesh is usually scooped out or peeled away before eating.
tamarillo.visual: a whole, egg-shaped tamarillo with smooth, glossy deep red skin
tamarillo.what: An egg-shaped fruit with tangy, sweet flesh.

facts: The name tamarind comes from the Arabic for Indian date.
The tree is native to tropical Africa and is now grown across South Asia, Mexico and beyond.
Its pulp is soaked in water to make a sour paste used in curries, chutneys and drinks.
tamarind.visual: a whole brown tamarind pod, its brittle shell cracked open to show the sticky pulp inside
tamarind.what: A brown, sticky pod with a sweet-sour pulp.

facts: Tamarind is the pulp of a pod from a tree that is native to tropical Africa.
It is served with chaat and samosas across India and in British Indian restaurants.
tamarind-chutney.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, glossy dark brown tamarind chutney
tamarind-chutney.what: A sweet-sour brown sauce of tamarind pulp and spices.

facts: Tamarind is a tropical tree whose pods hold a sticky, sour brown pulp around large seeds.
It is widely used in Thai, Indian and Mexican cooking to add a sharp, fruity sourness.
tamarind-concentrate.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with dark brown, glossy tamarind concentrate
tamarind-concentrate.what: A dark, sour paste made from the pulp of tamarind pods.

facts: The tamarind tree is native to Africa, and its sour pulp is now used across Asia and Latin America.
The word tamarind comes from an Arabic phrase meaning Indian date, reflecting early trade routes.
Tamarind paste is made by soaking the pulp in water, then straining out the seeds and fibres.
tamarind-paste.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, dark brown tamarind paste, smooth and slightly glossy
tamarind-paste.what: A sour, dark paste made from tamarind fruit pulp.

facts: Tamarind is a tree native to tropical Africa, now grown across South Asia and Latin America.
The name tamarind comes from an Arabic phrase meaning date of India.
Tamarind pulp is widely used in Indian chutneys and Thai sauces.
tamarind-pods.visual: a small heap of brown tamarind pods, papery and slightly cracked, lying on the background
tamarind-pods.what: Long brown pods holding a sticky, sweet-sour fruit pulp.

facts: Tamarind is the pulp from the pods of a tropical tree, used across Asia, Africa and Latin America.
Its name comes from the Arabic tamr hindi, meaning Indian date.
Tamarind gives a sour note to Indian and Thai cooking, and it is an ingredient of Worcestershire sauce.
tamarind-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, dark brown tamarind sauce, glossy and smooth
tamarind-sauce.what: A sweet-sour brown sauce made from tamarind pulp.

facts: Tandoori cooking takes its name from the tandoor, a clay oven used across South Asia.
Blends often include paprika, cumin, coriander and garlic for colour and warmth.
The red colour often comes from paprika or Kashmiri chilli.
tandoori-masala.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl filled with fine, brick-red spice powder
tandoori-masala.what: A red spice blend for yoghurt marinades and grilled meat.

facts: The tandoor is a clay oven used across South Asia to cook marinated meats and breads.
Tandoori marinades are traditionally made with yoghurt and spices such as cumin and chilli.
tandoori-paste.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, brick-red spiced paste
tandoori-paste.what: A red, spiced paste for marinating meat and vegetables.

facts: Tangelos were developed by crossbreeding in the United States.
The Minneola is a well-known tangelo variety with a distinctive bulb-shaped tip.
Tangelos are grown in warm, citrus-growing regions such as Florida and California.
tangelo.visual: a whole tangelo with glossy deep orange skin and a small nub at the top
tangelo.what: A juicy hybrid of mandarin and pomelo, sweet with a tang.

facts: The name tapenade comes from tapeno, the Provençal word for capers.
Tapenade is a traditional dish from Provence in south-eastern France.
Black olives are the traditional base, though green olives are sometimes used.
tapenade.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of dark olive tapenade, thick, glossy and finely chopped
tapenade.what: A thick, savoury paste of olives, capers and anchovies.

facts: Tapioca comes from cassava, a root vegetable native to South America.
The root is crushed and washed, then the starch is separated and dried to a powder.
Tapioca pearls, made from the same starch, are used in Taiwanese bubble tea and in old-fashioned British milk puddings.
tapioca-starch.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine white tapioca starch
tapioca-starch.what: A fine white starch made from cassava root.

facts: Taramasalata is a Greek meze dip made by blending fish roe with bread or potato and olive oil.
The name comes from tarama, the Greek word for fish roe.
Carp roe was the traditional base, and cod roe is now widely used.
taramasalata.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth pale pink taramasalata, lightly textured surface
taramasalata.what: A pale pink Greek dip made from salted fish roe.

facts: Taro is one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown in Asia, Africa and the Pacific for thousands of years.
In Hawaii, taro is traditionally pounded into poi, a smooth, slightly sour paste.
Raw taro contains calcium oxalate crystals that irritate the mouth, so it must always be cooked thoroughly.
taro.visual: one whole raw taro corm with rough brown skin and small root hairs, lying on its side
taro.what: A starchy root vegetable that tastes nutty when cooked.

facts: Taro is one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown in Asia and the Pacific for thousands of years.
In Trinidad and other Caribbean islands, taro leaves are a key ingredient in callaloo, a thick green stew.
The leaves are cooked down until soft, as they are not eaten raw.
taro-leaves.visual: a loose bunch of large fresh green taro leaves with pale stems, lying flat
taro-leaves.what: Heart-shaped leaves of the taro plant, cooked until silky.

facts: Dijon is a city in France's Burgundy region, and mustard has been made there for centuries.
Tarragon is a herb with a faint aniseed flavour, native to Eurasia.
French tarragon is grown for its leaves, while Russian tarragon has a much weaker taste.
tarragon-mustard.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with smooth pale-yellow mustard, slightly grainy
tarragon-mustard.what: Dijon-style mustard flavoured with fresh tarragon leaves.

facts: Tarragon vinegar is a traditional ingredient in French cooking, used in sauces such as bearnaise.
French tarragon has an aniseed-like flavour, which passes into the vinegar when the herb is steeped in it.
tarragon-vinegar.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle holding pale green-gold tarragon vinegar, filled to the shoulder
tarragon-vinegar.what: A sharp white wine vinegar infused with tarragon.

facts: Tartare sauce is a classic French cold sauce, and is now a staple with fish and chips in Britain.
Its name is often linked to the Tatars, though the exact origin of the name is not certain.
Fried fish dishes in Britain are often served with tartare sauce, a mayonnaise-based sauce.
tartare-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, pale cream sauce flecked with chopped capers and gherkins
tartare-sauce.what: A creamy mayonnaise sauce with capers, gherkins and herbs.

facts: Tartaric acid occurs naturally in grapes and forms as a by-product of winemaking.
Cream of tartar, a salt of tartaric acid, is used to stabilise whipped egg whites in baking.
It gives a sharp, fizzy bite to sweets and some sherbet powders.
tartaric-acid.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine white crystalline powder
tartaric-acid.what: A sharp, white acid powder used in sweets and baking.

facts: Tatsoi is a leafy green from the mustard family, cultivated in East Asia for many centuries.
It is grown as a baby leaf, or left to mature into a dense, dark green rosette.
In Japan and China it is cooked lightly in stir-fries and soups, or eaten raw in salads.
tatsoi.visual: a whole tatsoi head, a flat dark green rosette of rounded glossy leaves and a pale white stem base
tatsoi.what: A small Asian salad green with a mild mustard flavour.

facts: Tawny port is aged in wooden casks, which gives it a brown-amber colour and a nutty taste.
Port is made in the Douro Valley of northern Portugal and is fortified with grape spirit.
Tawny ports are commonly served slightly chilled with cheese or desserts.
tawny-port.visual: a clear drinking glass of deep amber tawny port, filled to just below the rim
tawny-port.what: A sweet, nutty Portuguese wine, aged to a golden amber.

facts: It takes its name from the River Tay in Scotland, where it was bred.
It is a cross of raspberry and blackberry, and the berries are usually sold in summer.
tayberry.visual: a small loose heap of large, dark crimson tayberries, glossy and slightly rounded
tayberry.what: A large, sweet-sharp raspberry and blackberry hybrid.

facts: Tea eggs are a common street food in China, sold in the shell from carts and stalls.
Cracking the shell lets the tea and soy colour the egg in a marbled pattern.
They are often flavoured with spices such as star anise and cinnamon.
tea-egg.visual: one whole peeled hard-boiled egg with a brown marbled pattern on its surface
tea-egg.what: A boiled egg, cracked and simmered in tea and soy sauce.

facts: Teacakes are a British bun, traditionally eaten with a cup of tea.
They are often spread with butter and sometimes toasted.
teacake.visual: a whole round soft golden bun, speckled with dried fruit, lying on its side
teacake.what: A soft fruited bun, eaten split and buttered.

facts: The Eurasian teal is a small dabbling duck that breeds across Europe and Asia.
Teal are roasted quickly and served pink, because the breast dries out if overcooked.
Wild ducks like the teal have been hunted for food in Britain for many centuries.
teal.visual: one whole small plucked raw teal, pale skin and a plump body, lying on its breast
teal.what: A small wild duck with dark, richly flavoured meat.

facts: Teff is a very small grain, and its seeds are only a fraction of the size of wheat grains.
It is the main grain used for injera, the soft, spongy flatbread of Ethiopia and Eritrea.
Teff is grown in Ethiopia, where it has been cultivated for thousands of years.
teff.visual: a small heap of tiny, rounded, reddish-brown teff grains with a fine, granular texture
teff.what: A tiny grain from Ethiopia with a malty flavour.

facts: Tellicherry pepper takes its name from Tellicherry, the British name for Thalassery on the Malabar coast.
Pepper from the Malabar coast was traded across the Indian Ocean for centuries.
Black peppercorns are dried until the outer skin turns dark and wrinkled.
tellicherry-peppercorns.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl heaped with large dark black peppercorns, slightly glossy and wrinkled
tellicherry-peppercorns.what: Large, bold black peppercorns from India's Malabar coast.

facts: Tempeh is a traditional food from Java in Indonesia, made by fermenting cooked soybeans.
A mould called Rhizopus binds the soybeans into a firm cake that holds its shape when cooked.
Tempeh is now eaten across Southeast Asia and is popular in vegetarian kitchens around the world.
tempeh.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl heaped with cubes of pale beige tempeh, the grainy soybean texture visible
tempeh.what: A firm, nutty cake made from fermented soybeans.

facts: Tench is a carp-family fish found across Europe and western Asia, in still or slow-moving water.
Tench spawn in summer among weeds, and anglers have long valued it as a sporting fish.
tench.visual: a whole raw tench with olive-green skin, a golden sheen and small rounded red fins
tench.what: A mild, sweet-fleshed freshwater fish from slow rivers.

facts: Its stems are eaten along with the florets, and they cook in only a few minutes.
Broccoli is a cultivated form of wild cabbage, grown for its flower buds.
The English name broccoli comes from the Italian broccolo, meaning the flowering top of a cabbage.
tenderstem-broccoli.visual: a small bunch of raw tenderstem broccoli, slender green stems with small florets, lying flat
tenderstem-broccoli.what: Slender broccoli with long, thin, tender stems.

facts: Tequila can only be made in designated regions of Mexico, most famously around the town of Tequila in Jalisco.
It is made from the cooked and fermented juice of the blue agave, a spiky succulent plant.
Tequila is made mainly from blue agave, while mezcal can use many agave species.
tequila.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle filled with clear pale liquid
tequila.what: A clear spirit distilled from blue agave in Mexico.

facts: The word teriyaki combines teri, meaning lustre, and yaki, meaning grilled or broiled.
Teriyaki-style dishes became popular in Hawaii and the United States after Japanese migration.
teriyaki-beef-slices.visual: thin slices of glossy, brown-glazed cooked beef, overlapping and lying flat
teriyaki-beef-slices.what: Thin slices of beef glazed in a sweet soy and mirin sauce.

facts: The name combines 'teri', meaning shine, and 'yaki', meaning grilled.
It is traditionally made from soy sauce, mirin and sugar, simmered until it thickens.
Teriyaki-style cooking spread widely outside Japan during the twentieth century.
teriyaki-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of dark, glossy brown teriyaki sauce
teriyaki-sauce.what: A sweet, glossy soy glaze from Japanese cooking.

facts: Terrine takes its name from the earthenware dish in which it is traditionally baked.
Pâté de campagne, or country pâté, is coarsely minced and usually contains pork.
It is a classic part of French charcuterie, the craft of preparing cooked and cured meats.
terrine-de-campagne.visual: a thick cut slice of coarse, pale brown country terrine, flat-cut face showing its speckled texture, lying on a plain background
terrine-de-campagne.what: A coarse, rustic French meat pâté, sliced cold.

facts: Its name means monk's head, and it comes from the Bernese Jura in Switzerland.
Traditionally it is shaved into rosettes with a girolle, a small hand-cranked tool.
Its texture is firm and it is often served with bread, fruit or cured meats.
tete-de-moine.visual: a small wheel of pale cream-coloured cheese with a dark rind, one wedge cut away and lying on the background
tete-de-moine.what: A hard Swiss cheese, shaved into delicate rosettes.

facts: Its name, tetilla, is a word for a small breast, referring to its shape.
It has a soft, creamy texture and a mild, buttery taste when young.
tetilla.visual: a whole smooth, domed cheese with a pale yellow rind, lying on a plain background
tetilla.what: A mild, creamy cheese from Galicia in north-west Spain.

facts: Texas barbecue is known for slow-smoked beef brisket, and sauce styles vary widely across the state.
In traditional Texan barbecue, sauce is often served on the side rather than brushed on the meat.
texas-bbq-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thin, dark reddish-brown barbecue sauce
texas-bbq-sauce.what: A thin, peppery tomato sauce for slow-cooked brisket.

facts: Thai aubergines are small, round and grown widely across South-East Asia.
They keep a slightly bitter taste and a firm texture when cooked, which suits green curries.
In Thailand they are also eaten raw in some dishes, served as a crunchy addition to a meal.
thai-aubergine.visual: a small heap of tiny round green aubergines, pale green with dark green stalks, lying loose on the background
thai-aubergine.what: Tiny round green aubergines, used whole in Thai curries.

facts: Thai basil is a different variety from Italian sweet basil, with a stronger aniseed taste.
It grows widely across South-East Asia, and is a key herb in Thai curries and stir-fries.
thai-basil.visual: a small bunch of Thai basil, dark green pointed leaves with purple-tinged stems
thai-basil.what: A basil with an aniseed flavour, used in Thai cooking.

facts: Bird's eye chillies are a Southeast Asian variety, widely used in Thai cooking.
Dried chillies keep for a long time and are often ground or toasted before use.
Their heat is measured on the Scoville scale, where they rank among the hotter common chillies.
thai-bird-s-eye-chilli-dried.visual: a small heap of dried red bird's eye chillies, wrinkled and tiny, with dark red and brown tones
thai-bird-s-eye-chilli-dried.what: Tiny dried red chillies with a sharp, fierce heat.

facts: Traditionally the paste is pounded by hand in a stone mortar with a pestle.
Kaffir lime leaves and lemongrass are common ingredients in Thai green curry pastes.
thai-green-curry-paste.visual: a small plain glass jar without a label, filled with bright green curry paste
thai-green-curry-paste.what: A fiery green paste of chilli and herbs for Thai curries.

facts: Thai cooks traditionally pound the paste in a mortar before adding coconut milk.
Coconut milk gives the sauce its richness and softens the heat of the chillies.
thai-green-curry-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth pale green curry sauce with a glossy sheen
thai-green-curry-sauce.what: A creamy Thai sauce of coconut milk and green chillies.

facts: Thai red curry paste is pounded or blended from dried and fresh chillies with aromatic herbs and spices.
Garlic, shallots and lemongrass are common ingredients, along with galangal, a relative of ginger.
Cooks often fry the paste in coconut cream before adding meat, vegetables or fish to make a red curry.
thai-red-curry-paste.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, deep red curry paste
thai-red-curry-paste.what: A hot paste of chilli, lemongrass and a ginger-like root.

facts: Yellow curry is one of the milder Thai curries, and its colour comes from turmeric.
Thai curry pastes have traditionally been pounded by hand in a stone mortar.
Yellow curry reflects the influence of Indian cooking on Thai food, through centuries of trade.
thai-yellow-curry-paste.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth golden-yellow curry paste, slightly glossy
thai-yellow-curry-paste.what: A mild, golden Thai paste of spices, herbs and turmeric.

facts: Bacon is cured pork, often salted and sometimes smoked, and it has been eaten for centuries.
Rashers are slices cut from the back or the belly of the pig.
thick-cut-bacon.visual: a few thick, raw pork bacon rashers, lean and pink with white fat, lying flat in a neat row
thick-cut-bacon.what: Chunky pork rashers that stay meaty when crisped.

facts: Sliced white bread became widely sold once bread-slicing machines came into commercial use.
Toasting stale bread dries it out and gives it a crisp, golden surface.
thick-cut-white-toast.visual: a thick slice of golden toasted white bread on a plain white plate
thick-cut-white-toast.what: Golden toasted white bread, cut in thick, chunky slices.

facts: Pre-sliced bread was first sold in the United States after a bread-slicing machine was invented there.
British thick-cut white bread is usually a soft loaf sliced thicker than standard sandwich bread.
White bread is made from flour with the bran and germ removed, which gives it a pale, soft crumb.
thick-cut-white-toast-bread.visual: two thick-cut slices of plain white bread lying flat, soft pale crumb and square edges visible
thick-cut-white-toast-bread.what: Thick slices of soft white bread that toast golden.

facts: Pizza as a flatbread with toppings has roots in Naples in southern Italy.
Basic pizza dough is made from flour, water, yeast and salt.
A thinner base bakes quickly, so it crisps more evenly than a deep one.
thin-and-crispy-pizza-base.visual: one round thin pizza base, pale and flat with slightly raised edges, lying on a plain white plate
thin-and-crispy-pizza-base.what: A thin round pizza base that bakes up crisp at the edges.

facts: Shisanxiang is the Chinese name for the blend, meaning 'thirteen fragrances'.
Blends vary by cook, but often include star anise, cinnamon, clove, fennel and Sichuan pepper.
It is used in slow-braised Chinese dishes, such as red-cooked pork.
thirteen-spice.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of fine reddish-brown ground spice blend, smooth and level
thirteen-spice.what: A warm, fragrant Chinese blend of many ground spices.

facts: Thousand Island is a mayonnaise-based dressing, often pink from tomato.
Homemade versions often mix mayonnaise with tomato ketchup and finely chopped gherkins.
thousand-island-dressing.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, thick pale pink dressing
thousand-island-dressing.what: A creamy pink dressing with a sweet pickle flavour.

facts: Egg noodles are made from wheat flour and eggs, which give them their yellow colour.
In Chinese cooking, fine noodles are often stir-fried or added to clear broths.
Dried noodles keep for a long time, which made them a useful store-cupboard food.
thread-egg-noodles.visual: a small loose heap of dried, fine, pale yellow egg noodles
thread-egg-noodles.what: Fine, pale strands of noodle made with egg, quick to cook.

facts: It comes from the port city of Tianjin in northern China, where it has long been made.
Dong cai is another name for it, and a small amount adds a strong, salty depth to a dish.
tianjin-preserved-vegetable.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of finely chopped, dark greenish-brown pickled leaves, moist and textured
tianjin-preserved-vegetable.what: Finely chopped salty pickle, used to season Chinese soups.

facts: Ticklemore is a goat's cheese made in Devon, in south-west England.
ticklemore.visual: a block of firm, crumbly white goat's cheese, one wedge cut away, lying directly on the background
ticklemore.what: A firm, crumbly goat's cheese with a clean, fresh taste.

facts: In Spain, tiger nuts are soaked, ground and sweetened to make horchata de chufa.
In Spain the tubers are known by the name chufa.
tiger-nuts.visual: a small heap of dried, wrinkled, dark brown tubers, each small and oval
tiger-nuts.what: Small, chewy tubers with a sweet, nutty taste.

facts: Tiger prawns are farmed and wild-caught across the Indo-Pacific region.
They are named for the dark bands across their shells, which look like tiger stripes.
Prawns are often grilled, stir-fried or added to curries and paella.
tiger-prawns.visual: a whole raw tiger prawn with banded grey and black shell, lying in a gentle curve on the background
tiger-prawns.what: Large, striped prawns with a firm, sweet bite.

facts: Tikka refers to small pieces of meat marinated in spices and cooked in a tandoor oven.
Masala is a word for a mixture of spices used across South Asian cooking.
Pastes like this are sold ready-made so cooks can build a curry quickly at home.
tikka-masala-paste.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick orange-red paste, smooth and glossy on top
tikka-masala-paste.what: A creamy tomato-spice paste for flavouring grilled chicken.

facts: Tikka masala is strongly associated with British Indian restaurants, where it became very popular.
Sauces of this kind are typically made from tomato, cream and ground spices such as garam masala.
tikka-masala-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, orange-red, creamy sauce
tikka-masala-sauce.what: A creamy, mildly spiced tomato sauce for chicken or paneer.

facts: Tikka is a term from Hindi and Urdu for a bite-sized piece of meat.
Chicken tikka is strongly associated with the British curry house.
The paste is usually built from spices such as cumin, coriander, paprika and chilli.
tikka-paste.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with a thick, smooth red-orange paste
tikka-paste.what: A thick, smoky red paste for marinating meat.

facts: Tilapia are native to Africa and the Middle East and are now farmed in many warm countries.
The fish is farmed widely in ponds and tanks, and it is sold fresh, frozen or as fillets.
tilapia.visual: a single raw white tilapia fillet, skin side down, moist and flaky
tilapia.what: A mild, white-fleshed fish farmed in warm waters.

facts: The berries come from a prickly ash tree, Zanthoxylum armatum, that grows in the Himalayan foothills.
Like sansho and Sichuan pepper, it belongs to a group of spices that give a tingling sensation.
Nepali cooks use it in pickles and chutneys, and it is a common seasoning in the region.
timut-pepper.visual: a small heap of dried timut pepper husks, pale brown-green and slightly ridged, some tiny dark seeds among them
timut-pepper.what: A citrusy, tingly Himalayan pepper used in Nepali cooking.

facts: The loaf takes its shape from the tin it is baked in, which keeps its sides straight.
Square-shaped loaves are popular for sandwiches and toast across Britain.
tin-loaf.visual: one whole square-topped white tin loaf, pale golden crust, straight sides, on a plain background
tin-loaf.what: A soft white loaf baked in a tin, with a flat top.

facts: Apricots are thought to have originated in China and spread westward along ancient trade routes.
Canning apricots in syrup lets cooks use the fruit long after the short growing season has ended.
Apricots feature in tagines across North Africa and in sweet pastries across Europe.
tinned-apricots.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of soft apricot halves in pale golden syrup
tinned-apricots.what: Halved apricots preserved in syrup, soft and ready to use.

facts: Baby squid are a popular seafood in Mediterranean cooking, where they are often fried or stuffed.
Squid ink is used in Italian dishes such as black pasta and black risotto.
Preserving seafood in oil has long been a way to keep it for later use in southern Europe.
tinned-baby-squid.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of small pale squid pieces in dark oil
tinned-baby-squid.what: Small squid, preserved in oil or ink for a quick meal.

facts: Beans cooked in tomato sauce are a long-standing British breakfast and lunch food.
Haricot beans are small, dried white beans that are widely grown in Europe and the Americas.
tinned-baked-beans.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of haricot beans in thick orange-brown tomato sauce, glossy and warm
tinned-baked-beans.what: Haricot beans cooked in a sweet, thick tomato sauce.

facts: Black beans are a staple of Latin American cooking, especially in Cuba and Brazil.
Black beans are native to the Americas, where they were grown long before European contact.
tinned-black-beans.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of cooked black beans in their dark glossy liquid
tinned-black-beans.what: Soft, dark beans, cooked and ready to heat for burritos.

facts: Borlotti beans are a variety of common bean, originally from the Americas, now popular in Italy.
The beans turn plain brown when cooked, losing their colourful markings.
tinned-borlotti-beans.visual: a small plain white bowl of cooked speckled borlotti beans, plump and cream-coloured with red-brown streaks, in their liquid
tinned-borlotti-beans.what: Plump, speckled beans, ready-cooked and sold in tins.

facts: Broad beans, also called fava beans, have been eaten around the Mediterranean since ancient times.
Ful medames, a stew of cooked fava beans, is a traditional dish in Egypt.
tinned-broad-beans.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of cooked green broad beans, drained and glossy
tinned-broad-beans.what: Ready-cooked broad beans that come in a can.

facts: Butter beans are the large variety of lima bean, grown in many warm parts of the world.
Butter beans are a common ingredient in the Greek dish gigantes, baked with tomato and herbs.
tinned-butter-beans.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of cooked butter beans in a little liquid
tinned-butter-beans.what: Large, creamy white beans, ready cooked and soft.

facts: Cannellini beans are a large white variety of kidney bean, widely used in Italian cooking.
Common beans were first grown in the Americas and reached Europe in the 1500s.
Tinned beans are already cooked, so they need no long soaking like dried beans.
tinned-cannellini-beans.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of soft, cooked white beans in a little liquid
tinned-cannellini-beans.what: Soft, creamy white beans, ready-cooked for stews.

facts: Carrots are a root vegetable that has been cultivated for many centuries.
Tinned vegetables are cooked inside sealed tins, so they can be stored for long periods.
tinned-carrots.visual: a small plain white bowl of soft orange carrot pieces, glossy and tender, in a little liquid
tinned-carrots.what: Soft, sweet carrot pieces, cooked and preserved in a tin.

facts: Cherries are stone fruit, related to plums, peaches and apricots, all members of the genus Prunus.
tinned-cherries.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of dark red cherries in glossy syrup
tinned-cherries.what: Sweet dark cherries preserved in syrup, ready to eat.

facts: A white sauce is a basic sauce of flour, butter and milk, known in French as béchamel.
Béchamel is one of the mother sauces of classic French cooking.
tinned-chicken-in-white-sauce.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of pale cooked chicken pieces in creamy white sauce
tinned-chicken-in-white-sauce.what: Pieces of chicken in a creamy white sauce, sold in a tin.

facts: Condensed soup is thickened and can be diluted with water or milk before heating.
tinned-chicken-soup.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, creamy pale chicken soup
tinned-chicken-soup.what: A creamy, ready-to-heat chicken soup sold in cans.

facts: Chickpeas are one of the oldest cultivated pulses, grown in the Middle East for thousands of years.
Hummus, a smooth paste of chickpeas, tahini and lemon, is eaten across the Middle East.
In India, chickpeas are a staple of curries such as chana masala.
tinned-chickpeas.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of cooked chickpeas, plump and pale beige, lightly drained
tinned-chickpeas.what: Pre-cooked chickpeas, sold in cans and ready to use.

facts: Chilli con carne is linked to Texas and the American Southwest, though its origins are debated.
The name is Spanish for chilli with meat, a dish that spread widely across the United States.
Ready-made canned versions became a popular pantry item in the twentieth century.
tinned-chilli-con-carne.visual: a small plain white bowl of chilli con carne, a thick red stew of minced beef and beans

Flat, soft breads like this are made in many countries, from Mexican tortillas to Armenian lavash.
tomato-wrap.visual: one soft round tomato wrap, pale orange-red, flat and lightly folded at one edge, lying on its own
tomato-wrap.what: A soft, flatbread-style wrap tinted red with tomato.

facts: Tomme de Savoie is made in the Savoie region of the French Alps.
tomme-de-savoie.visual: a round wheel of greyish cheese with a rough natural rind, one wedge cut away showing a pale interior
tomme-de-savoie.what: A mild, earthy French mountain cheese with a grey rind.

facts: Tonic water was developed in the nineteenth century and is still sold as a mixer.
Its bitter flavour is a classic partner to gin, most famously in the gin and tonic.
tonic-water.visual: a clear drinking glass of pale, fizzy tonic water with bubbles rising through the liquid
tonic-water.what: A bitter, fizzy soft drink, classic with gin.

facts: Tonka beans come from a large South American tree, Dipteryx odorata, which grows in tropical forests.
They have long been used to scent perfumes and snuff, as well as sweet dishes.
They are grated over desserts in very small amounts, as a little goes a long way.
tonka-beans.visual: a small heap of wrinkled, shiny black tonka beans, each about the size of a thumbnail
tonka-beans.what: Dark, wrinkled seeds that smell of vanilla and almond.

facts: Tonkatsu, the breaded pork cutlet the sauce is named for, was adapted from European cutlet dishes in Japan.
Tonkatsu sauce is a thick, fruity, savoury sauce popular in Japan.
tonkatsu-sauce.visual: A small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, glossy dark brown sauce.
tonkatsu-sauce.what: A thick, sweet and tangy brown sauce for breaded pork.

facts: Toor dal is made from pigeon peas that have been split and usually husked.
It is a staple of everyday cooking in India, where it is often cooked into a thick soup called dal.
Sambar, a tangy South Indian stew, is usually made with toor dal.
toor-dal.visual: a small heap of dry yellow split pulses, pale gold and slightly rough-edged, scattered on a plain surface
toor-dal.what: Split yellow pulses that cook soft and creamy.

facts: Torshi takes its name from the Persian word torsh, meaning sour.
Cauliflower, carrots and turnips are commonly pickled in brine or vinegar for torshi.
Pickling has long been a way to preserve summer vegetables for the cooler months in Iran.
torshi.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with mixed pickled vegetables in bright, cloudy liquid
torshi.what: Tangy mixed pickles, a classic of Middle Eastern tables.

facts: Torta del Casar comes from the village of Casar de Cáceres in Extremadura, western Spain.
It is made from sheep's milk and set with rennet from the cardoon thistle, not animal rennet.
Because the cheese is so soft, it is often served scooped with a spoon, sometimes with bread.
torta-del-casar.visual: a small round cheese with its top cut away, showing soft, creamy pale yellow paste inside
torta-del-casar.what: A soft, spoonable sheep's cheese from western Spain.

facts: Tortellini come from Emilia-Romagna in northern Italy, where they are a traditional dish.
They are often served in a clear broth at celebrations, especially at Christmas.
tortellini.visual: a small heap of uncooked fresh tortellini, pale yellow pasta rings with pinched edges
tortellini.what: Small pasta rings folded around a cheese or meat filling.

facts: Tortelloni is the larger cousin of tortellini, from the Emilia-Romagna region of Italy.
The name is the augmentative form of tortellino, meaning a larger version of the small filled pasta.
Ricotta and spinach is a classic filling, though many versions use meat or other cheeses.
tortelloni.visual: a small heap of fresh uncooked tortelloni, pale yellow pasta with crimped edges, on a plain background
tortelloni.what: Large stuffed pasta, filled with ricotta and spinach.

facts: Tortiglioni is an Italian pasta, one of many short tubular shapes made from durum wheat.
Ridged tube shapes like this are designed to hold sauce in their grooves and inside the tube.
tortiglioni.visual: a small heap of short, dried, ridged tubes of pasta, pale golden-beige
tortiglioni.what: Short, grooved pasta tubes that cling to thick sauces.

facts: Tortillas are flatbreads from Mexico and Central America, traditionally made from corn.
Tortilla chips are made by cutting tortillas into wedges and frying or baking them.
Corn was domesticated in Mexico thousands of years ago and is central to Mesoamerican food.
tortilla-chips.visual: a small heap of golden, triangular fried corn tortilla chips, lightly crisp, lying loose
tortilla-chips.what: Crisp triangles of fried corn tortilla, ideal for dips.

facts: The name tostada means toasted in Spanish, describing its crisp corn tortilla base.
Tostadas are made by frying or baking corn tortillas until they become firm and crisp.
Tostadas are a common everyday food across Mexico, often topped with beans, meat and salsa.
tostada.visual: One plain, crisp golden corn tostada, flat and round, lying on a small plain white plate.
tostada.what: A flat, crisp fried or baked corn tortilla for toppings.

facts: Tostada means toasted in Spanish, and the shells are made from corn tortillas.
Corn tortillas are made from masa, a dough of ground corn treated with lime.
tostada-shells.visual: a neat stack of flat, golden, crisp corn tostada shells on a plain white plate
tostada-shells.what: Flat, crisp corn discs, fried or baked and ready to top.

facts: Toulouse sausage is a fresh pork sausage from the city of Toulouse in south-west France.
It is a traditional ingredient in cassoulet, a slow-cooked bean stew.
toulouse-sausage.visual: one whole raw Toulouse sausage link, pinkish-brown and coarse-looking, lying in a gentle curve
toulouse-sausage.what: A coarse, garlicky pork sausage from south-west France.

facts: Toum is a traditional Lebanese sauce, and its name is the Arabic word for garlic.
It is made by slowly beating peeled garlic with oil until it forms a thick, pale emulsion.
Toum is commonly served with grilled chicken and flatbreads across the Levant.
toum.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, creamy white garlic sauce, smooth and glossy on top
toum.what: A fluffy, pale whipped sauce made from garlic and oil.

facts: Traditional balsamic vinegar is made in Modena and Reggio Emilia in northern Italy.
It is made from cooked grape must, not wine, then aged in a series of wooden barrels of different woods.
The traditional version is protected by a designation of origin, so production rules are strict.
traditional-balsamic-vinegar.visual: a small plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of very dark, thick brown vinegar
traditional-balsamic-vinegar.what: A dark, syrupy vinegar aged slowly in wooden barrels.

facts: Nuts, seeds and dried fruit keep well for a long time, which made them useful for travel.
Mixes of this kind are sold in many countries, often with chocolate pieces added.
trail-mix.visual: a small heap of loose trail mix, mixed nuts, seeds and small pieces of dried fruit
trail-mix.what: Nuts, seeds and dried fruit mixed for snacking on the go.

facts: Its pastry base is usually shortcrust, the same as many British tarts.
treacle-tart.visual: a single slice of golden-brown treacle tart with a glossy amber filling, on a small plain white plate
treacle-tart.what: A sweet tart with a golden syrup filling and breadcrumbs.

facts: Treacle is a thick, dark syrup left over when sugar is refined, and it has a strong, bittersweet taste.
Treacle toffee is a traditional British sweet, often eaten around bonfire night in November.
Toffee is made by boiling sugar and butter to a high temperature, which sets it hard as it cools.
treacle-toffee.visual: a small heap of dark brown treacle toffee pieces, glassy and brittle, one piece broken to show its texture
treacle-toffee.what: Hard, dark, glassy toffee flavoured with black treacle.

facts: Trenette is a traditional pasta of Genoa and the wider Ligurian coast.
It is classically served with pesto, a sauce of basil, pine nuts, garlic and Parmesan.
Trenette is similar to linguine, and in Liguria it is often cooked with potatoes and green beans.
trenette.visual: a small loose heap of uncooked, flat ribbon pasta, pale golden and dry
trenette.what: Flat, narrow pasta ribbons from Liguria, northern Italy.

facts: Tardivo, the late-harvest variety, has long slender leaves and is named for its late season.
The leaves are bitter when raw, and cooking them softens and sweetens the bitterness.
treviso-radicchio.visual: one whole long Treviso radicchio head, deep red-purple leaves with pale white ribs, a firm elongated shape
treviso-radicchio.what: Long, bittersweet red chicory that is good grilled.

facts: Tri-tip is a cut from the bottom sirloin of beef, named for its triangular shape.
It became popular in Santa Maria, California, where it is grilled over red oak.
Cooks usually slice tri-tip thinly across the grain so each piece stays tender.
tri-tip.visual: one whole raw tri-tip beef roast, triangular, deep red meat with a thin fat cap along one edge
tri-tip.what: A triangular beef roast cut from the bottom sirloin.

facts: Sponge is usually soaked in sherry or fruit juice before the custard and cream go on top.
trifle.visual: a trifle in a small plain glass bowl, layers of sponge, pale custard and cream visible
trifle.what: A layered English dessert of sponge, custard and cream.

facts: Sponge cake is made by whisking eggs and sugar to trap air, which makes it light.
In Britain, a trifle is a dessert of layered sponge, custard and fruit, often soaked in sherry.
trifle-sponges.visual: a small plain white plate of pale golden sponge cake, cut into small rectangular pieces
trifle-sponges.what: Light, fluffy sponge cake, often used to make a trifle.

facts: Triple-cream cheeses have extra cream added to the milk, which makes them much richer than most soft cheeses.
Brillat-Savarin, a French triple-cream cheese, is named after a famous food writer.
The bloomy white rind is a mould, usually Penicillium candidum, that forms during ripening.
triple-cream-cheese.visual: one whole round soft white cheese with a fluffy bloomy rind, pale ivory and creamy
triple-cream-cheese.what: A soft, mild, very creamy cheese with a white bloomy rind.

facts: Triple sec is an orange-flavoured liqueur, usually made from the dried peel of oranges.
It is a key ingredient in margaritas and in cocktails such as the Cosmopolitan.
triple-sec.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of colourless orange liqueur on a plain background
triple-sec.what: A clear orange-flavoured liqueur, sweet and citrusy.

facts: Trofie is traditionally hand-rolled from a small piece of dough, twisted into a spiral.
It is traditionally served with pesto, a sauce made from basil, garlic and pine nuts.
trofie.visual: a small loose heap of short, twisted pale cream pasta spirals, dry and uncooked
trofie.what: Short, twisted pasta from Liguria in north-west Italy.

facts: Tromboncino is an Italian squash, named after its shape, which resembles a trombone.
It belongs to Cucurbita moschata, the same species as butternut squash.
Young fruits are tender and are often cooked in the same ways as courgettes.
tromboncino.visual: one whole long, curved, pale green squash with a smooth skin, lying on its side
tromboncino.what: A long, curved summer squash with a greenish skin.

facts: Trout roe is the eggs of trout, which are fish that live in cold rivers and lakes.
Roe is usually cured with salt before eating, which firms the eggs and gives them a clean taste.
Trout eggs are sometimes called trout caviar, though true caviar comes only from sturgeon.
trout-roe.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of glossy orange trout roe, the separate eggs shining in a loose heap
trout-roe.what: Small, glossy orange eggs taken from trout.

facts: Black truffles are wild fungi that grow underground, usually near the roots of oak and hazel trees.
truffle-mayonnaise.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, pale ivory mayonnaise, its top in a soft peak
truffle-mayonnaise.what: Creamy mayonnaise flavoured with earthy black truffle.

facts: Truffles are underground fungi that grow alongside the roots of trees such as oak and hazel.
Many truffle oils are flavoured with synthetic compounds rather than real truffle.
Truffles have been prized in European cooking for centuries, especially in Italy and France.
truffle-oil.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of pale golden oil, light shining through
truffle-oil.what: Oil infused with truffle, giving a strong earthy aroma.

facts: Black truffles are fungi that grow underground around the roots of certain trees, mostly oak and hazel.
Truffle salt is sea salt mixed with ground dried truffle or truffle oil, and is often sprinkled on eggs and chips.
truffle-salt.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, holding fine greyish-beige salt, dark specks scattered through it
truffle-salt.what: Sea salt mixed with dried black truffle.

facts: Truffles are underground fungi that grow in association with the roots of trees such as oak.
Black truffles from the Périgord region of France have long been prized by chefs.
truffle-slices-in-brine.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, holding thin dark truffle slices in clear brine
truffle-slices-in-brine.what: Preserved truffle slices, for adding to sauces and mash.

facts: Tsukemono means pickled things, and the pickling can use salt, rice bran or vinegar.
Nukazuke is a traditional way of pickling vegetables in fermented rice bran.
Tsukemono is traditionally served alongside rice and miso soup in a Japanese meal.
tsukemono.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thinly sliced pickled vegetables, pale and pink, in a loose jumble
tsukemono.what: Japanese pickled vegetables, served as a side dish.

facts: Tteok are made by pounding steamed rice, often glutinous rice, until smooth and elastic.
Rice cake soup, tteokguk, is traditionally eaten on Korean New Year.
Tteok are used in dishes such as tteokbokki, a spicy dish of rice cakes in a red chilli sauce.
tteok.visual: a small heap of plump, glossy white rice cake cylinders, smooth and slightly soft, lying loose
tteok.what: Chewy Korean rice cakes, shaped into cylinders or slices.

facts: Tubetti is Italian for little tubes, and the pasta is cut very short.
Small pasta shapes like tubetti are traditionally added to Italian soups such as minestrone.
tubetti.visual: a small heap of dry, uncooked tiny pasta tubes, pale yellow and smooth, lying loose
tubetti.what: Tiny tubes of pasta, often used in Italian soups.

facts: Toro is the fatty belly cut of tuna, and it is prized in Japanese sushi and sashimi.
Bluefin tuna is the species most prized for its belly meat in Japan.
The marbling of fat through the flesh is what makes it melt on the tongue.
tuna-belly.visual: one fresh raw tuna belly fillet, deep pink and marbled with white fat streaks, lying flat
tuna-belly.what: The fatty, rich underside of a tuna, prized in sushi.

facts: Ventresca is the belly cut of tuna, prized in Italy and Spain for its richness.
Tuna packed in olive oil has a long tradition in Mediterranean countries.
tuna-in-olive-oil-jar.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with pale pink tuna belly pieces in golden olive oil
tuna-in-olive-oil-jar.what: Rich tuna belly packed in olive oil.

facts: Tuna is often eaten raw in sushi and sashimi, as well as seared.
The name tuna comes from the Latin thunnus, a word for this kind of fish.
tuna-steak.visual: one thick, deep-red raw tuna steak with a smooth, glossy surface, lying flat on its side
tuna-steak.what: A thick, meaty fish steak with deep red flesh.

facts: Tunworth is made in Hampshire, in southern England, in the style of camembert.
Camembert-style cheeses have a white, bloomy rind created by a mould that ripens the cheese from the outside in.
Soft cheeses like this ripen over several weeks, becoming softer and creamier as they age.
tunworth.visual: a whole round soft cheese with a fine white bloomy rind, standing upright
tunworth.what: A soft, creamy English cheese in the style of camembert.

facts: Turbinado is partly refined cane sugar, steamed and spun in a centrifuge to remove syrup.
The name is linked to the turbines, or centrifuges, once used to spin off its syrup.
It is often used in coffee, porridge and baking, where its crunch and light caramel notes stand out.
turbinado-sugar.visual: a small heap of pale golden coarse sugar crystals
turbinado-sugar.what: Coarse, pale golden sugar with a light molasses flavour.

facts: Like other flatfish, it has both eyes on one side of its head as an adult.
It is prized in European kitchens and often poached or roasted whole on the bone.
turbot.visual: a whole raw turbot, diamond-shaped flatfish with dark brown skin and small bony bumps, lying flat on a plain background
turbot.what: A large, meaty flatfish with firm white flesh.

facts: Turkey bacon is made from turkey meat that is cured and smoked to resemble pork bacon.
Turkey is a bird native to the Americas, and it has long been a festive meat in Britain.
turkey-bacon.visual: a few thin turkey bacon rashers, pinkish-brown with pale streaks of fat, lying flat
turkey-bacon.what: Thin, smoked strips of cured turkey meat, ready to crisp.

facts: Turkey was first domesticated in Mexico or Central America, and reached Europe in the sixteenth century.
Turkey breast steaks are cut from the breast meat, which is paler and milder than the leg.
turkey-breast-steak.visual: one raw boneless turkey breast steak, pale pink, flat and even in thickness
turkey-breast-steak.what: A lean, thick slice of turkey breast, quick to cook.

facts: Turkeys were domesticated in Mexico and reached Europe through Spanish trade.
The bird became a centrepiece of the American Thanksgiving tradition.
turkey-crown.visual: one raw boneless turkey crown, pale skin on, lying flat on the surface
turkey-crown.what: A boneless joint of turkey breast, sold ready to roast.

facts: Turkeys were first domesticated in Mexico, and reached Europe after the Spanish arrived in the Americas.
turkey-drumstick.visual: one whole raw turkey drumstick with its skin on and the bone exposed at one end, lying on its side
turkey-drumstick.what: A turkey's leg, rich dark meat that roasts well.

facts: Turkey eggs are larger than hen's eggs and have a cream or pale brown shell with darker speckles.
Turkey eggs can be boiled, fried or scrambled in much the same way as hen's eggs.
turkey-egg.visual: one whole turkey egg, large and oval, pale cream shell with dark brown speckles, lying on its side
turkey-egg.what: A large, speckled egg with a mild flavour.

facts: Giblets are the edible organs and neck removed from a bird before it is roasted.
Giblets are traditionally simmered to make the stock for turkey gravy.
A gizzard is a muscular stomach that helps birds grind up their food.
turkey-giblets.visual: a small heap of raw turkey giblets, a pale neck, a dark heart and a gizzard
turkey-giblets.what: The neck, heart and gizzard of a turkey, for stock.

facts: Turkey gravy is a classic part of Christmas dinner in Britain and the United States.
Gravy is also served with roast beef, sausages and mashed potatoes in British cooking.
turkey-gravy.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, glossy brown gravy
turkey-gravy.what: A savoury brown sauce made from roast turkey pan juices.

facts: Turkey was domesticated in Mesoamerica and reached Europe in the 16th century.
turkey-mince.visual: a loose heap of raw minced turkey, pale pink-white and finely textured, on a plain white background
turkey-mince.what: Lean minced meat from turkey, good for burgers and chilli.

facts: Domestic turkeys descend from wild birds native to the Americas, and were first domesticated in Mesoamerica.
The thigh is worked harder than the breast, so its meat is firmer and suits slow braising.
turkey-thigh.visual: one whole raw turkey thigh, skin on, pale pink flesh, bone in, lying on its side
turkey-thigh.what: The dark, rich leg meat of a turkey, good for slow cooking.

facts: A wing has three joints, and the tip is often removed and used for stock.
Turkeys were first brought to Europe from the Americas after European explorers arrived there.
turkey-wings.visual: a single raw turkey wing with pale skin and its three joints visible, lying flat
turkey-wings.what: Wing joints from a turkey, rich in gelatine for gravy.

facts: Turkey is a major producer of dried apricots, and the Malatya region is well known for them.
Apricots are believed to have originated in China and were carried westward along trade routes.
turkish-apricot.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of plump, orange-gold dried apricot halves, slightly glossy
turkish-apricot.what: A plump, sweet dried fruit used in stuffings and cakes.

facts: Lokum has a long history in the Ottoman Empire, where it was often offered as a gift.
It is made by cooking sugar and starch, then setting the mixture before cutting it into cubes.
Cubes are traditionally dusted with icing sugar or cornflour so they do not stick together.
turkish-delight.visual: a small heap of soft pale pink cubes, each dusted in white powdered sugar
turkish-delight.what: Soft, chewy sweet cubes, usually flavoured with rose.

facts: Turnips have been cultivated in Europe and Asia since ancient times.
Turnips became a staple of European farming, especially as winter fodder for livestock.
Roasting turnips softens their sharp taste and brings out a sweet, nutty flavour.
turnip.visual: a whole round white turnip, its top tinged purple, lying on its side
turnip.what: A round white root with a peppery taste when raw.

facts: Cime di rapa is the Italian name, meaning turnip tops, and it is common in southern Italy.
Rapini is an alternative name for the same leafy vegetable, often sold in North America.
It is often served with orecchiette pasta in Puglia, a region of southern Italy.
turnip-tops.visual: a loose bunch of raw turnip tops, slender green stems, leaves and small yellow buds
turnip-tops.what: Bitter leafy shoots of the turnip plant, eaten as greens.

facts: Tuscany is one of Italy's best-known olive oil regions, with groves across its hills.
Olive oil has been pressed in the Mediterranean for thousands of years.
Frantoio and Leccino are two olive varieties commonly grown in Tuscany.
tuscan-olive-oil.visual: a plain unlabelled clear glass bottle of golden-green olive oil
tuscan-olive-oil.what: Peppery olive oil from Tuscany, often drizzled on soup.

facts: Tzatziki is a staple of Greek cooking and is often served with grilled meats and pitta bread.
Similar yoghurt and cucumber dips are found across the Middle East and the Balkans, under different names.
tzatziki.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of thick, creamy, pale green-white dip
tzatziki.what: A thick Greek dip of yoghurt, cucumber and garlic.

facts: Ube is a purple yam from Southeast Asia, and it is widely used in Filipino desserts.
The flesh is naturally violet, which is why ube is often used to colour ice cream and cakes.
In the Philippines, ube jam and ice cream are popular, and ube is the local name for the yam.
ube.visual: one raw ube yam cut in half, rough brown skin and vivid violet flesh showing, lying directly on the background
ube.what: A purple yam with a sweet, vanilla-like flavour.

facts: Ube is a purple yam, and its vivid colour makes it popular in desserts.
It is often used as a filling for pastries and as a topping for shaved ice.
ube-halaya.visual: a plain glass jar without a label, filled with smooth, deep violet ube halaya
ube-halaya.what: A sweet, purple yam paste from the Philippines.

facts: Udon is a traditional Japanese noodle, and its history in Japan goes back many centuries.
Udon are often served in a hot broth made from dashi, soy sauce and mirin.
Udon noodles are made from wheat flour, salt and water, kneaded and rolled into thick strands.
udon-noodles.visual: a small loose heap of thick, pale, dried udon noodles, uncooked
udon-noodles.what: Thick, chewy Japanese noodles made from wheat flour.

facts: Ugli fruit is a cross between a tangerine and a grapefruit, probably with another citrus.
It was first found growing in Jamaica, and it is still grown there today.
The skin is loose and easy to peel, while the segments inside are juicy and sweet-tart.
ugli-fruit.visual: one whole ugli fruit, rough yellow-green loose skin, slightly lopsided
ugli-fruit.what: A loose-skinned citrus fruit with sweet, tart, juicy flesh.

facts: Ulluco is grown high in the Andes, in countries such as Peru and Bolivia.
It is one of several Andean tubers grown for its bright skin and waxy flesh.
ulluco.visual: one whole knobbly ulluco tuber, waxy skin in bright yellow and pink, lying on its side
ulluco.what: A knobbly Andean tuber with a waxy, crisp texture.

facts: Ume trees are native to China and were introduced to Japan many centuries ago.
Umeboshi are ume pickled in salt, a traditional Japanese preserve.
Raw ume are not eaten, as they must be processed before use.
ume-plum.visual: a small heap of firm, round, yellow-green ume fruits with a blush on one side, on a plain background
ume-plum.what: A sour Japanese fruit, pickled or steeped in liqueur.

facts: Umeboshi are Japanese ume plums, a relative of the apricot, pickled in salt.
Red shiso leaves are often added during pickling, which gives the plums their red colour.
Umeboshi are traditionally served with rice, especially in packed lunches called bento.
umeboshi.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of whole, dark red pickled plums
umeboshi.what: Salty, sour pickled plums from Japan, eaten with rice.

facts: They are traditionally salted and dried with red shiso leaves, which colour them.
Umeboshi paste is used in Japanese cooking to season rice, dressings and dips.
umeboshi-paste.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, deep rose-brown umeboshi paste
umeboshi-paste.what: A sharp, salty paste made from pickled Japanese plums.

facts: Unagi is the Japanese name for freshwater eel, usually grilled over charcoal.
It is often served over rice in a dish called unadon.
unagi.visual: a grilled eel fillet with a glossy dark-brown glaze, cut into thick pieces, served plainly on a small plain white plate
unagi.what: Grilled freshwater eel, glazed with a sweet, smoky sauce.

facts: In Britain, butter must contain at least 80 per cent milk fat to be sold under that name.
unsalted-butter.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of smooth, pale yellow butter with a neat surface
unsalted-butter.what: Butter with no added salt, so you control the seasoning.

facts: Green bacon is the British term for bacon that is cured but not smoked.
In Britain, back bacon is cut from the loin, while streaky bacon comes from the belly.
unsmoked-bacon.visual: one raw unsmoked bacon rasher, pale pink meat and white fat, lying flat
unsmoked-bacon.what: Pork cured in brine or salt, not smoked, for a mild taste.

facts: Urfa biber is named after Şanlıurfa, a city in south-eastern Turkey.
The peppers are dried in the sun by day and sweated overnight, which develops their dark, raisiny character.
It is widely used as a table seasoning and in cooking across Turkey and the wider Middle East.
urfa-biber.visual: a small heap of dark, coarse reddish-purple chilli flakes in a small plain white bowl
urfa-biber.what: Dark, raisin-like chilli flakes from Turkey, mild and smoky.

facts: Vacherin Fribourgeois is a cheese made in the canton of Fribourg in western Switzerland.
The cheese has long been made on farms in the hills around Fribourg.
vacherin-fribourgeois.visual: a block of pale ivory cheese with a golden rind, one wedge cut to show a creamy interior, on a plain background
vacherin-fribourgeois.what: A creamy Swiss cheese, good for melting into fondue.

facts: Vacherin Mont d'Or is a soft cheese from the Jura mountains on the French and Swiss border.
It is wrapped in a band of spruce bark, which gives it a woodsy flavour.
Its rind is washed in brine as it ages, giving a strong, savoury character.
vacherin-mont-d-or.visual: a whole round soft cheese in a thin band of spruce bark, pale golden rind, lying on its side
vacherin-mont-d-or.what: A soft Jura cheese, best baked until it is spoonable.

facts: Roasted chestnuts have long been sold from street stalls in winter across Europe.
Sweet chestnut trees were once an important food crop in parts of southern Europe.
Chestnuts are starchy rather than oily, which sets them apart from most other nuts.
vacuum-packed-chestnuts.visual: a small plain white ceramic bowl of peeled cooked chestnuts, pale golden-brown and smooth
vacuum-packed-chestnuts.what: Chestnuts already peeled and cooked, ready to use.

facts: Valençay is a goat's milk cheese from the Berry area of central France.
It takes its name from the town of Valençay in the Indre department.
The ash coating is a traditional feature of the cheese, which is shaped as a truncated pyramid.
valencay.visual: one whole small pyramid-shaped goat's cheese with a thin grey ash coating, lying on its base
valencay.what: A soft, ash-coated goat's cheese shaped like a pyramid.

facts: Valencia oranges are named after the region of Valencia in Spain, where they are widely grown.
They ripen late in the season, and they are used for juice more than for eating fresh.
The variety is widely grown in California, Florida and South Africa as well as in Spain.
valencia-orange.visual: one whole Valencia orange, smooth bright orange peel, lying on its side on the background
valencia-orange.what: A juicy, balanced orange, widely grown for squeezing.

facts: Vanilla comes from the pods of a climbing orchid native to Mexico.
Vanilla pods are hand-pollinated on plantations, which is why the spice is labour-intensive.
